So `event_type` and `subject_kind` are `text` in the store and closed unions in [notification.ts](../../packages/contracts/src/notification.ts) — the only arrangement in which both rules hold — and `subject_id` is **deliberately not a foreign key**, since a per-kind FK column is the same forbidden schema change wearing a different hat. A DB-level test inserts a `lock-flipped` row over an existing subject kind with no DDL, which is the guard passing rather than being asserted.
  🔒 **The row stores no content, and that is §3 rather than economy.** `NotificationSubject.label` is resolved **on every read**, through the same access path as the subject itself; nothing is copied. A stored label would be the subject's content sitting *outside* the subject's access path — still readable after the share that permitted it was revoked — which is precisely the leak §3 exists to prevent, arriving through a field that looks like a display convenience. A test renames a container and reads the notification again to prove the label tracks the subject rather than a copy of it, and the mention case asserts the response never contains the comment's text: §4's rule about what an email may carry is **also** the rule about what the record may hold.
  ⚠ **The count is not `SELECT count(*)`, and getting that wrong would be a leak rather than a cosmetic bug.** Because visibility is re-resolved per row, a badge counting three over a list showing two would itself disclose that a third thing exists. Both therefore come off **one** resolution pass, and a test asserts it against a participant holding two rows they cannot see: zero listed, zero counted, `unreadByProject` empty. Mark-all runs the same pass, so it can never touch a row the requester was not shown.
  **`subject_kind` is a separate column from `event_type` on purpose**, and it is what makes the guard cheap in code as well as in DDL: the visibility resolver keys on the KIND, so `lock-flipped` over an existing `sandbox-document` needs a union member and an emitter and **no new resolver**. Each resolver reuses the access path its own surface already runs — `canSeeContainer` (exported from [cycle.ts](../../apps/api/src/cycle.ts) for it) for the deliverable and its rounds, the sandbox document's organisation for the working area — because a second implementation of a wall rule is a second answer, and a wall with two answers is a wall with one bug.
  **Participant grain, not User**, and it pays for itself twice: it is the grain the access predicate already resolves (ADR-0033), and the interval closing on removal is the same act that darkens the notifications — nothing has to remember to sweep them. The project is **derived** through that column and never stored beside it. §6b's two scopes are two queries over one resolution: `GET /notifications` is the user's own across every project they can reach, `GET /projects/:id/notifications` is one project's, and a test proves a notification on a second project pointing at a first project's subject resolves to nothing — the wall does not open because a notification crossed a project.
  **Three things this ticket did NOT do.** It does not emit — nothing writes a row, which is T-330 and is why the tests insert directly. It does not forbid `DELETE` on the table: whether a notification ever expires is `Q-015`'s retention theme, which ADR-0049's own Open section defers it to, and a trigger would have ruled it on the way past. And it adds **no purge reach** — a notification stores a pointer and never content, so a purged subject leaves a row that is visible to nobody, which is the erasure §3 already guarantees; that asymmetry is recorded in [personal-data.md](../architecture/personal-data.md) rather than fixed silently. The register also gains the row this table needs, and the reason it needs one is the non-obvious half: **`read_at` is a read receipt** — behavioural data about a named person, saying when they looked and by absence when they did not — and the `*_by_*` guard would never have caught it, because the recipient column is not that shape.
- **T-331 — The in-app notification surface: the rail count and the "Needs you" panel.** ✅ **Built 2026-08-28** (no migration). **Two surfaces, ruled 2026-08-01 against drawn mockups (ADR-0049 §6a) — build both; they are each small and neither works alone.** (1) A **`Notifications` rail item** alongside Home and Review carrying an unread count — the only placement that survives wherever the user is, which is the point, because the person a round-issued event most needs to reach has been in the editor all afternoon. (2) A **"Needs you" panel on the project home, directly above the work items**, so a notification sits beside the thing it is about — and **absent at zero rather than showing an empty state**. **The scopes differ deliberately (§6b): the rail count is the user's own across every project they can reach, grouped by project; the panel is scoped to its project.** Get this wrong and a mention on a second project is silently invisible. **A floating panel over the canvas is rejected** (§6c) — it covers the drafting canvas and reads as transient, against the durability the record exists for; that shape is for confirming an action just taken, which is a different mechanism. Deliberately **not** in scope: per-event preferences, digests, batching, or any setting beyond on/off. **If the ticket has to be split, the rail ships first.** | *(Deps: T-329)*
  **As built, and neither half was split** — both landed, as the ticket asks. The rail item sits between Review and Sandbox and reads `GET /notifications`; the panel sits directly above *Your work items* and reads `GET /projects/:id/notifications`. **The two scopes are two queries over one resolution**, not two implementations: [notifications.tsx](../../apps/web/src/screens/notifications.tsx)'s `useNotifications(projectId?)` is the only reader either surface has, so they cannot come to different conclusions about what is visible.
  🔒 **The count survives the collapsed rail, as a dot.** That is not polish: reaching the user *wherever they are* is the entire argument §6a makes for this placement, and the collapsed rail hides `nav a span:not(.glyph)` wholesale — so without an explicit override the one thing the item exists for disappears exactly when the rail is at its most persistent. **Zero renders nothing at all**, which is the panel's absent-at-zero rule applied to the badge: an item that always wears a count stops being read on the day it means something. A count over 99 renders `99+`, because three digits push the label out of a 216px rail.
  **`RailNavItem` gained one optional field** (`count`) rather than a Notifications-specific component — it is a nav item like the others, and a second component would have carried a second copy of the rail's collapse behaviour. **The route target is resolved server-side, in domain terms.** `NotificationSubject.opens` names WHICH object to open — a container or a sandbox document — because most subjects are not openable at their own grain: a round is read on its deliverable's cycle screen and a comment on its document. A client holding only `{kind, id}` would have had to join its way back to something openable, a second traversal outside the access path that had just decided the row was visible. This keeps §3 whole — one pass decides both *whether* you may see it and *what* it points at — and it is still not a URL, so no surface's routing table leaks into the API.
  ⚠ **The surfaces are built and have nothing to show, and that is the sequencing rather than a defect.** Nothing emits a notification until **T-330**, which waits on T-323, so there is **no e2e spec and no walkthrough beat** for either surface: the seed deliberately gains no notification row. Seeding one would put a row in the demonstration dataset that no code path can produce — T-301's rule (*a value the schema carries and no code can set is a claim the schema makes falsely*) applied one level up, and it would leave a reader of the seed concluding the telling already works. The e2e arrives with the emitter.
  **One unrelated break fixed in passing, and it is worth naming because of how it hid.** `packages/ui`'s `RunTrace` keeps a `Record<Step['type'], string>` of step labels; T-263 widened `STEP_TYPES` with the seven worker types (migration 0055) and did not widen the map, so `@infora/ui` had not typechecked since — **invisible because turbo's cache was still serving the pre-T-263 result**, and `pnpm run check` reported green. Touching a `packages/ui` file for the rail count invalidated that cache and the error surfaced immediately. The seven labels are added here; the lesson is that a green `check` over a cached task is not evidence about the current tree.
- **T-332 — Promotion blocks on open threads and open findings.** ✅ **Built 2026-08-28** (migrations 0057 and 0058). Owner-ruled 2026-08-01 (ADR-0049 §7), **against the recommendation to warn** — nothing reaches the controlled library with loose ends, and threads and findings are treated identically so the surface never explains why one list stops you and the other does not. **The override is `Participant.elevated` only, and every use is audited** (§8): a block with no escape is a deadlock, not a stricter gate — a finding against a paragraph a later redraft deleted would otherwise prevent promotion permanently. Reuses the 2026-07-31 tier rather than inventing a bypass; ADR-0016 does not reopen. **The non-obvious dependency: promotion must *count* open threads and open findings**, which is a query obligation on the finding schema, not a display concern. | *(Deps: T-328)*
  **As built, and the findings half counts a store that does not exist.** T-328 built the finding *schema*; the checker (T-310) that produces findings is unbuilt and gated on open questions, so the count is structurally **zero** today. The gate is built over **both** lists anyway, as the Deps say — and as a **named seam** rather than an omission: [open-items.ts](../../apps/api/src/open-items.ts) holds `countOpenFindings` with the parameters the real query needs, so when the checker lands one body changes and no caller does. **The empty case is asserted explicitly** (`expect(pre.openItems.findings).toEqual({ open: 0, bySeverity: { required: 0, advisory: 0 } })`) rather than left incidental, which is what makes the second half of the gate testable at all: a suite exercising only threads would leave it untested *and* nobody would know.
  🔒 **The gate sits inside `resolvePromotion`**, the one decision function T-373 built for exactly this reason, so the promotion window states the block before the click and the click enforces it — a preflight computed separately from the act is a preflight that will eventually lie. **Threads, not comments:** a thread is a root comment still `open`, because counting replies would make a thread with four answers look four times as blocking as one with none. The status vocabulary is the one T-328 deliberately borrowed for `FindingStatus`, so the count really is one shape over both lists.
  ⚠ **Holding the tier is not using it, and that distinction is the ticket's sharpest edge.** `overrideOpenItems` is an explicit flag on the request; inferring the override from `Participant.elevated` would have made §7 read *"blocked unless you happen to be senior"*, which is not what was ruled — an elevated lead author who has not looked at the open items is stopped exactly as an ordinary one is, and then decides. A test pins it: an elevated promote with no flag is still `409 open_items`. Two more pin the record's meaning — an override on a **clean** draft writes no row (a record of forcing a gate that was not closed would dilute every real one), and the table is **append-only**, because the people who hold this tier are exactly the people who would want the trail gone.
  **`promotion_overrides` is a new table, not a reuse of `elevated_refusals`** — that one records an act **refused** for want of the tier and this one an act **performed** with it, and merging them would need a column meaning "did this happen", which is two records wearing one shape. It stores the **counts** rather than recomputing them, for `purge_events`' reason one store along: afterwards there is nothing to count, and a record answering *"somebody pressed the button"* is worth less than one answering *"somebody pressed the button past two open threads"*. **No reason column** — §8 names exactly two things the record must say, and inventing a third obligation on the one path a person reaches under deadline is not this ticket's to impose. It is written **inside the promotion's own transaction**, because an audit that can fail separately from the act it audits is an audit with a gap in it.
  **Two things the ticket did not name and this build did.** `elevated_action` gains `promote_over_open_items` (migration 0058), so an **unelevated** attempt to force is refused *through* `refuseElevated` — the repo's one elevated-gate path, written as a single call precisely so a later caller cannot add the gate and forget the record (T-301). The ticket asked for uses to be audited; recording refusals too is T-301's rule applied rather than extended, and it costs one enum value. Two migration numbers rather than one because drizzle-kit emits an enum widening separately, and hand-merging two generated snapshots to save a number is the edit T-344 spent a ticket recovering from. The window's copy names **what** is open and offers the override **only** to a requester the server says holds it, so nobody is shown a control they will be refused on.


### Waypoint C — the executor rule, the style guide and the document creator

*Built 2026-08-30, the session after [ADR-0053](../architecture/adr/0053-the-checkers-run-and-the-executor-rule.md) was ruled. Execution only: every design question these tickets carry was settled by that ADR or by ADR-0048's two dated addenda, and nothing here re-derives one.*

- **T-396 — The executor rule: a plan step executes the capability it names.** ✅ **Built 2026-08-30.** *(Plainly: make a plan step actually run the tool it names — today the engine ignores the name and runs its own default.)* *(Minted 2026-08-30 → [ADR-0053](../architecture/adr/0053-the-checkers-run-and-the-executor-rule.md) §7.)* `runChain` dispatches on **stage** and never reads a step's `worker` ([chain.ts](../../packages/orchestration/src/chain.ts)), so the drafting stage runs the draft leaf whatever a step names — which is why the checker cannot call the built corpus search and why T-309 stopped mid-build. **Done when:** the step's named capability is what runs; **stage keeps only** its two remaining jobs (deciding what runs a step naming *no* capability, and being the vocabulary the plan and footer are written in); the capability is resolved through the set **assembled** for this requester (T-269), a step naming an unentitled one failing with the entitlement refusal rather than a generic error; a capability declaring `writes` runs **only** inside a workflow that declared `writes` and its label-propagation, which makes validator rule 4 bite for the first time; the definition format gains a **fan-out step** whose width is computed **in code** at plan time and never model-chosen; and **per-step cost attribution starts working**, because a cost is recorded on a Step row and the row is opened by the executor. **This creates no generic worker** — the executor is a dispatcher over a closed registry of built capabilities and non-negotiable 8 is untouched. 🔒 **The interim refusal is deleted by this ticket, and its test inverts.** [validate.ts:303](../../packages/workflows/src/validate.ts#L303) currently refuses a worker on any stage but the retrieve step, because a definition naming an executor the engine does not have must not load; that guard expires the moment the engine has one, and the test must assert the definition now **loads and executes** rather than that it is refused. | *(Deps: T-264, T-265, T-269)*
  **As built. *Plainly: the engine now runs the tool a plan step names — before this it ignored the name and ran its own default, which is why no built tool was reachable.*** All five guards of ADR-0053 §7 landed, each with its own test in [executor.test.ts](../../packages/orchestration/src/executor.test.ts), plus the two consequences the ruling named. **The dispatch sits BEFORE the stage switch** in [chain.ts](../../packages/orchestration/src/chain.ts) — a step naming a capability runs it, and stage never sees the step at all; a step naming none reaches the switch exactly as before, so the coded chain's four leaves are byte-identical. The registry is [capability-registry.ts](../../packages/orchestration/src/capability-registry.ts): a `Map` of name → `{ declaration, run }`, built once at composition, holding `corpus_retrieval`, `document_builder` and `extractor`. It has no entry that takes a name and improvises, which is the structural form of *"this creates no generic worker"*.
  🔒 **All three refusals fire BEFORE ANY SPEND**, in a pre-walk pass over the ordered plan, for the same reason the no-`present`-step refusal already did: an unbuilt capability, an unentitled one and an undeclared write are defects in the **plan**, and paying a retrieval and a model call to discover one would be paying for the discovery. `CapabilityRefused` extends `PlanNotExecutable` and carries a `reason`, so **the entitlement refusal is distinguishable from a generic error** as the ADR requires — and the API maps `not_entitled` to **404**, not 400: telling a requester a capability exists but is not theirs is the *absent, never disabled* rule failing at the last step (principle 4). **An absent assembled set is EMPTY, not permissive** — a caller that ran no entitlement check refuses every capability, which is the fail-safe direction and is asserted.
  ⚠ **The descriptive `worker:` had to go, and its going is the ticket's one behaviour change to a shipped path.** `project-question.yaml` carried `worker: corpus_retrieval` on its retrieve step, placed there at T-265 as a label because the runner read it never. Under the executor rule a label is not available: what a step names is what runs, and running the `corpus_retrieval` **worker** there would be a *different* retrieval from the one Ask does — the leaf does baseline assembly **plus the retrieval sub-agent's child run**, and carries the guiding and informing channels the draft step steers on, none of which a leaf worker returns. So the name came off and the definition is **v2**. Nothing that ran changed, because nothing was reading it. The same correction was needed in `modelChosenStages` (T-266), where the entitlement now decides whether the retrieval **stage exists** rather than putting a name on it.
  🔒 **And that exposed a fiction worth recording: `expect_calls` had been observing a label, not a call.** The eval harness reads the workers a plan recorded, and the only thing any plan recorded was Ask's descriptive name — so `expect_calls: [corpus_retrieval]` passed against a worker that had never executed. `workersCalled` for an Ask run is now `[]`, which is the truthful observation, and the harness test says so. Both directions are still exercised at unit grain in `assertions.test.ts`, where the observation is supplied; the *"never a vacuous pass"* guard is untouched, because an unreadable plan still raises `Unevaluable` rather than passing.
  **The fan-out is a step field, and its width may come from a parameter and NOTHING ELSE.** `fan_out: '{{parameters.NAME}}'` against a declared `id_list`; `{{item}}` inside that step's inputs is the element. **A `fan_out` pointing at `{{steps.x.output}}` is refused at load**, and that single rule is the whole guarantee: a step's output can be model-written, so a width read from one would make the plan's **shape** model-chosen while it still called itself declared — losing the one promise (same inputs, same steps, same order) a declared workflow is sold on. `bindWorkflow` expands in code, keys each expansion `id#0`, `id#1`… so two expansions are two outputs, and **refuses an unbound fan-out** rather than silently producing zero steps and reporting success. A width of **zero is legal and silent about nothing** — it means the code that bound the list found nothing to fan out over.
  **Per-step cost attribution starts working**, exactly as `document-builder.ts`'s own comment predicted: the builder now reports the drafting call's usage and model, the executor's adapter writes them onto the Step row it opened, and the row is of the capability's own kind (`document_builder`, from migration 0055's vocabulary). Absent usage stays **absent, never zero** (T-254).
  **Two deviations, both narrow.** (1) **`{{steps.x.output}}` resolves at run time from an in-memory map keyed on the declaring step's id**, carried on `PlannedStep` as `key` and deliberately **not stored**: a step output is a value in flight, not a record, and a stored copy would be a second name for a plan step. This needed no migration, which matters because T-397 carries this session's only one. (2) **A plan mixing a capability retrieval with the orchestrator's own drafting leaf is refused, loudly** (*"has nothing to draft from"*) — a leaf reads the chain's own state and a capability's output is not that state. Asserted as its own case, because the alternative is drafting from nothing and reporting success.
  **Fixed in passing, unrelated:** `cycle.test.ts`'s review-period assertion required ≥ 13 calendar days for ten working days, which is true from a weekday and false from a **Sunday** — where the count starts on the Monday after and lands on 12. The suite therefore failed every Sunday; found on one. *(Review notes, 2026-08-31: "five guards" is this record's own grouping of ADR-0053 §7's eight bullets — everything is covered, three structurally rather than as named guards. And the yaml relabel was not the only shipped-path behaviour change: an EDITED plan naming a capability now runs that capability rather than the stage's default leaf — three T-267 test fixtures moved with it.)*
- **T-397 — The project style guide, and the rulebook moves to the channel it was always on.** ✅ **Built 2026-08-30** (migration 0060). *(Minted 2026-08-30 → [ADR-0053](../architecture/adr/0053-the-checkers-run-and-the-executor-rule.md) §3 and ADR-0048's dated addendum (1).)* Two halves, one migration. **The correction:** ADR-0048 §4 placed a firm's rulebook on the **guiding** channel while asserting nothing in ADR-0021 was amended, and both cannot hold — ADR-0021 maps org context to **informing** and classifies **by ownership, not purpose**. [guiding.ts](../../packages/knowledge/src/guiding.ts) tags org-keyed rulebook rows `channel: 'guiding'` and the informing pipeline is a stub; the label and its tests move. **Access is unaffected** — the query keys on organisation with no wall predicate — so this is a relabel, not a reach change, and the test that proves it is the one asserting no wall predicate was added or removed. **The new store:** the **project style guide** — project context, owner-curated, binding every organisation on the project, clause-structured like the rulebook so a finding can quote *§4.2* rather than *"page 11"*. It is the guiding channel's definitional occupant ([CONTEXT.md](../../CONTEXT.md): *"the project's templates, style guides and guardrails"*) and **the first material that channel has ever carried.** 🔒 **On conflict, guiding wins and firm know-how fills the gaps** — ADR-0029's precedence, refined 2026-07-06, which the mislabel had made unreachable; a test pins it. ⚠ **Its governance is not settled here** — who may load and amend it, and whether amending it mid-project is an event anyone is told about, is either answered by this ticket or raised as a question by it. | *(Deps: T-308)*
  **As built, and the governance half is answered in part and raised in part. *Plainly: the project gains its own style guide — the client's writing rules, binding every firm — and the firm's own manual moves to the shelf it always belonged on; nobody's access changed.*** **Who may load and amend one: the OWNER organisation's super user** — `membershipRole === 'owner'` **and** `Participant.elevated`. That is not a new judgement; it is the record's existing shape applied. Whole-project configuration — `conflict_attestation_required` (ADR-0046 §8) and `review_period_default_days` (T-371) — is fixed by the owner super user, and a document every consultant on the scheme is checked against is the same kind of act as those rather than a smaller one. **Reading is every participant's**, and the asymmetry is deliberate: a rule that binds you is a rule you may look up, and a guide only the owner can see would produce findings quoting a clause the consultant cannot check. This is not a wall breach — ADR-0053 §9 makes privacy a property of the source's **scope**. The refusals split: **404** for a member organisation (principle 4 — it has no business learning a curation route exists for a project it does not own) and **403 `super_user_required`** for the owner's own non-elevated person, which is something they can act on.
  ⚠ **The other half is `Q-050`, raised rather than resolved**: whether amending a guide mid-project is an event anyone is told about. It is a ruling about the **notification set**, which ADR-0049 fixed and which a build ticket may not add to on its own. The reversible state ships — **nobody is told** — and the question carries the recommendation (tell the lead reviewer of every in-flight deliverable, once, as `record-state-changed-by-another-organisation` is told) with its own stress test against it.
  **The relabel moved the label and provably nothing else.** `guidingRules` → `informingRules`, the file renamed with it, and `channel: 'guiding'` → `'informing'` on every row. **The query is byte-for-byte T-308's**: same table, same `organisation_id` key, **no wall predicate added and none removed**. The test file moved with the code and every reach assertion in it was restated against the new label, plus one that asserts the store now puts **nothing** on the guiding channel — because *"we only changed a label"* is the kind of sentence that needs evidence rather than assurance.
  🔒 **The precedence is reachable for the first time, and is pinned in two places.** ADR-0029's *guiding wins, firm know-how fills the gaps* could not be applied while both style sources sat in one bucket with nothing to rank them by. Now: `mergeChannels` orders guiding first and drops **informing** first when the budget binds (asserted), and the draft prompt states the precedence in a **sentence** — because ordering is not an instruction, and a model reading two conflicting house rules has nothing in the order to tell it which governs. The sentence is emitted **only when both channels are present**, since a precedence announced over one source describes a conflict that cannot arise, and steer describing nothing is steer that gets ignored. Both halves asserted.
  **The store is `rulebooks`' shape and a different key, and the key is the ruling.** Migration 0060 adds `project_style_guides` + `project_style_guide_clauses`, drawn in [data-model.md](data-model.md) before being written, single `CHECK` and `GRANT`s hand-added as always. **There is deliberately no `organisation_id`**: an owning-organisation column would make it a firm's manual wearing a project's name, and the wall would then have two answers to *"who may read this clause"* — which is exactly what makes a quoted style-guide clause **not** org-private where a quoted rulebook clause is. The clause parser is **reused, not copied**: two parsers would be two answers to what a clause is, and the checker reads both style sources through one shape.
  **A named person, registered same-commit.** `project_style_guides.loaded_by_user_id` is in [personal-data.md](../architecture/personal-data.md) on the rulebooks row's worked precedent, with the difference stated: this material binds every organisation on the project, so it is the owner's own document and is **not** org-private. **An amendment is a retire-and-reload, never an edit** — the stored clause text is what past findings quote, so editing one in place would rewrite the evidence behind a review that has already happened.
  **One thing found by building it:** the CSRF guard's multipart allow-list is a list of literal paths, so the new upload route returned *"content-type must be application/json"* until it was added. Worth naming because the failure is a **400 that reads like a client bug** rather than like a missing registration. *(Review correction, 2026-08-31: the AUTHORITY is genuinely the existing whole-project-settings rule, but the refusal shape is new — a member organisation gets 404 while the owner's non-elevated user gets 403 with a named reason, a split neither cited precedent makes. Kept as a defensible refinement of principle 4; recorded because the entry called it "not a new judgement", which was true of who may act and not of how refusal answers.)*
- **T-398 — A finding declares whether its fix is mechanical.** ✅ **Built 2026-08-30.** *(Minted 2026-08-30 → [ADR-0053](../architecture/adr/0053-the-checkers-run-and-the-executor-rule.md) §6.)* T-328 shipped the finding schema before bulk acceptance was permitted, so nothing on a finding says which kind of fix it carries. **Done when:** a proposed revision is typed as **mechanical** — the same substitution applied consistently, expressible as find-and-replace and displayable in one line (*"Scheme → scheme, 55 places"*) — or as a **rewrite**, model-written prose. 🔒 **The model does not self-certify into the bulk lane.** If a fix cannot be expressed as a substitution and rendered as one line, it is not mechanical, and that test is **code** rather than a field the model fills in — which is what stops *"avoid the passive voice"* riding fifty-five rewritten sentences in behind an accept-all. The two-level severity (`required` / `advisory`) is unchanged and orthogonal. | *(Deps: T-328)*
  **As built. *Plainly: a suggested fix now says whether it is a mechanical correction (safe to accept in bulk) or a rewrite (read each one) — and code decides which, never the AI's own claim.*** `Fix = MechanicalFix | RewriteFix` and `classifyFix(original, revised)` live in [finding.ts](../../packages/contracts/src/finding.ts) beside the schema they complete, and the placement is a decision rather than convenience: **`apps/web` depends only on `contracts` and `ui`**, and the findings surface (T-311) has to render an accept-all above a group's mechanical fixes and withhold it from its rewrites — so the test has to be reachable from a surface, or the surface would have to guess. One test, one answer, both sides.
  🔒 **Three structural conditions, and each one rejects a real case.** (1) **The difference is one substitution**, found by a **longest-common-subsequence diff over word tokens**. A prefix/suffix peel was written first and is wrong in the ticket's own example: peeling *"The Scheme was assessed. The Scheme continues."* against its lowercased twin yields the whole middle as one difference, because the first and last changes sit at either end — so the very case the rule exists for classified as prose. (2) **Applying the candidate everywhere reproduces the proposal exactly** — this is *"applied consistently"*, and it is what fails *"avoid the passive voice"*: fifty-five sentences each rewritten differently do not survive one substitution. (3) **The one line fits** (`MECHANICAL_SUMMARY_LIMIT`, 80 characters), which is what keeps a rewritten sentence out — a sentence swapped for another sentence can satisfy (1) and (2) and is plainly not a find-and-replace anybody would accept in bulk.
  **`RewriteFix` carries a `reason`, and the reason is user-facing.** A fix that *looks* mechanical and was not admitted is exactly the case a reviewer will query, and *"it is a rewrite"* with no why reads as an arbitrary system. Four reasons, each naming the condition that failed.
  **`MechanicalFix.summary` is built once, here.** *"Scheme → scheme, 55 places"* is the sentence a reviewer reads before taking fifty-five decisions at once, and the count is the point of it — it states the SIZE of what is being accepted. Two surfaces rendering it two ways is how a bulk action starts meaning two things.
  **One judgement worth recording, because it looks like a gap.** A **single-occurrence** substitution is still `mechanical` — *"SI → metric, 1 place"*. The count exists to tell a reviewer how big the decision is, not to set a threshold, and one occurrence accepted in the bulk lane is one click either way. **A pure insertion is a rewrite**, because there is nothing to *find*, so there is nothing that could be applied anywhere else.
  **`Finding.fix` is optional and present exactly when `proposedRevision` is.** Nothing writes it yet: the checker DAG that produces findings is T-310 and the surface that renders the distinction is T-311, both next session. The schema and its test land ahead of them for T-328's original reason — neither can be specified without it.
- **T-309 — The document-creation DAG.** ✅ **Built 2026-08-30.** Largely composition, and the unblocked half of Waypoint C: `document_builder` (T-280) wrapped in a declared workflow — drafting into a template with an explicit source manifest and the computed label enforced against the destination. No new capability; the value is that a declared workflow is **evaluable end to end** where an improvised one is not. ✅ **Unblocked 2026-08-30 → [ADR-0053](../architecture/adr/0053-the-checkers-run-and-the-executor-rule.md) §7** — the Session C stop is cleared: a plan step now executes **the capability it names**, entitlement-checked, with a writing capability admitted only inside a workflow that declared `writes` and its label-propagation. **T-396 lands that rule; this ticket consumes it** and should not re-derive it. | *(Deps: T-264, T-265, T-280, T-396)*
  **As built. *Plainly: the document creator now runs as a real workflow — the plan and its price are shown before anything runs, and the run states what it covered.*** [document-creation.yaml](../../packages/workflows/definitions/document-creation.yaml), a **one-step** DAG, and the single step is the design rather than a shortcut. `document_builder` **does not retrieve** — its own header has said so since T-280 — and T-335's board entry rules the ordering: *"sources are chosen ahead of drafting, so the run has an explicit source manifest rather than a retrieval guess, which is what makes the output auditable against what the author asked for."* A `corpus_retrieval` step here would be a search whose answer the builder then narrows away: money spent, nothing changed, and a step that spends and changes nothing is worse than no step.
  🔒 **`writes: sandbox_document` + `label_propagation: refuse` are load-bearing rather than descriptive.** Since T-396 a capability that writes runs **only** inside a workflow that declared both, and refuses before any spend otherwise — so this definition is the thing that makes validator rule 4 bite. `refuse` and not `require_override`: the builder already withholds the write and names both labels when the sources are broader than the destination (finding F2), and V1 has nobody asking to override it.
  **The plan prices before the click, and is computed in code** ([tool-plan.ts](../../packages/capabilities/src/tool-plan.ts), ADR-0053 §4 — the run semantics are **not** checker-specific). Fixed per-section and per-source token allowances, capped at the assembly budget so the estimate cannot describe a call that could not happen; the price is `costOf` against the model the drafting call would be routed to. **An unpriced deployment reports `null` and the total refuses to be a number** — T-254 reaching an estimate: a total summed over an unpriced step is a partial figure wearing a total's name. Asserted, along with *"the same inputs produce the same plan"*, which is the sentence a model-chosen planner could not say.
  **Coverage is stated twice, in the same shape** (ADR-0053 §5): *"3 sections · 1 bound source · 1 drafting pass"* before, *"1 of 3 sections written · 1 of 1 bound sources used · 1 drafting pass"* after, with unreachable sources and withheld sentences appended because both are absences the document itself cannot show. The **same shape** matters more than the same words — a reader comparing the two sees the difference at a glance rather than having to go looking for it.
  **`/plan` and `/runs` call ONE planner**, for T-373's rule one surface along: a preflight computed separately from the act it previews is a preflight that will eventually lie. The plan the user saw and the plan the run executed cannot differ, because there is only one. **The plan's refusal is honoured by `/runs`**, not treated as advice.
  **Two things this ticket found, both worth the board knowing.** (1) **`runChain` now returns `outputs`** — what each capability step returned, keyed on the declaring step's id. A tool's caller needs the worker's own typed output (a manifest, a computed label, a list of unreachable sources) and cannot read it off the Run record, which stores an answer and an audit rather than a return value. In memory only; the durable facts are already Step columns. (2) 🔒 **A chat turn is never classified into a workflow that WRITES.** Shipping a second declared workflow made the deterministic classifier stop matching (*"one option is not a judgement"* only holds at one), and the fix is a rule rather than a special case: the document creator is a tool the user launches deliberately, with a destination chosen and a plan seen first, and a question that silently started writing into a sandbox would decide **who can read the result** (T-295) off a classification the user never saw. The candidate set is the read-only workflows; writing ones are reached through their own launcher.
  **`Q-037` is untouched.** Nothing here reads a bound container's plan row, and the unbound path is the only one built — see T-335.
- **T-334 — The Tools section stops being an empty state.** ✅ **Built 2026-08-30.** The rail has carried a **Tools** item since T-109 whose own copy records why it is empty: *"Tool launch beyond the chat/draft path is post-skeleton (ruled 2026-07-06)"* ([main.tsx:45](../../apps/web/src/main.tsx#L45)). That deferral has expired — **V1's tool set is three standalone tools** (re-cut 2026-08-30 → [ADR-0053](../architecture/adr/0053-the-checkers-run-and-the-executor-rule.md)): the **document creator** (T-335), the **QA checker** (T-336) and the **extractor**, whose tool is fog plus `Q-049`. This ticket is the launcher they live in. **Assembled from entitlements, not filtered** — the T-269 rule applies to tools exactly as to workers: an unentitled tool is *absent*, never disabled, so the section never advertises a capability the viewer cannot use. Infora-standard tools only; org-built and user-built tools are the builder, `Q-014`, and stay post-V1. | *(Deps: T-269)*
  **As built. *Plainly: the Tools page now lists real tools — the document creator live, the checker's slot honestly waiting on its build.*** `GET /projects/:id/tools` returns the set **assembled for this requester** — the same T-269 assembly the classifier is handed — and the surface has no `enabled` check to lose it in. The creator is present only where BOTH hold: this deployment carries the declared workflow, and the requester is entitled to `document_builder`. Either missing makes the tool **absent** rather than broken: a tile that launches a run the executor would refuse is a promise the product cannot keep.
  **Three tools, three different states, and that is the design rather than an incomplete build** (ADR-0053 §11). The **creator** is live. The **checker** is a tile in the `unbuilt` state **naming what it waits on** (T-336) — because a Tools section with one tile and no explanation reads as a product with one tool, and the note names the ticket so the copy cannot go stale silently. The **extractor** gets **nothing at all**: its tool is `Q-049` and unspecified, and a tile promising a screen nobody has designed is worse than no tile. All three are asserted, including the absence.
  **`unbuilt` is a different thing from unentitled**, and the type says so: an unentitled tool never reaches the client, an `unbuilt` one carries `waitsOn` and no `href`. Collapsing them would have made *"we have not built it"* and *"it is not yours"* the same sentence on screen, which is the one distinction the assembled-not-filtered rule exists to keep.
  **No recapture.** The rail's Tools item — the only part of this that any photographed screen contains — is unchanged: same label, same glyph, same path (`project.tsx`). No shot in `capture.mjs` navigates to `/tools`, verified by reading every `goto` in the file rather than assumed. *(Review note: this commit also added §8 to component-8-surfaces.md — the Tools surface's component record — unmentioned here.)*
- **T-335 — Document creator: the structure-first authoring surface.** ✅ **Built 2026-08-30.** The owner's V1 tool set, half one: *"rather than drafting a document using the editor/chat interface, you build the structure of a document, define what content you want in it, and the sources it will draw from in the library."* **T-309 builds the DAG; this builds the thing a user actually operates** — compose the outline, state the intent for each section, and **bind library sources per section before anything generates**. The ordering is the design: sources are chosen *ahead* of drafting, so the run has an explicit source manifest rather than a retrieval guess, which is what makes the output auditable against what the author asked for. Reached from Tools (T-334). **Where it meets the deliverable plan is `Q-037`** (raised 2026-08-06, pulled out of this ticket's prose per the Q/T boundary rule): whether a bound container's plan row seeds the structure is unruled — build the unbound path; do not invent the bound one. ⚙ **Unblocked downstream 2026-08-30**: T-309's executor stop is cleared by **T-396**, so this ticket's dependency chain now runs T-396 → T-309 → here rather than terminating in an unruled question. **The launch flow keeps its state** — the pattern T-336 sets (pick, configure, see the plan, step back and change one thing without re-entering the rest) applies here too and should not be re-invented. | *(Deps: T-309, T-334, T-396)*
  **As built.** The unbound path, and only it. Choose the shape, say what the document is for, **bind the library sources before anything generates**, choose where it goes — then see the plan, then run. **Sources first is the ticket**: it is what makes the output auditable against what the author asked for rather than against a retrieval guess.
  **The source list is `grounding-scope`, not the library list**, so a document offered here is one the draft could actually have used — the same pre-filter retrieval runs (T-292). `GroundingSource` gained `versionId` for this: a container is a series, a draft rests on **one revision** of it, and the manifest recording what the document was built from has to name which.
  🔒 **The launch keeps its state** (ADR-0053 §1). Changing any answer **discards the plan and keeps the answers** — a plan is about the inputs it was computed from, so a stale one shown beside changed answers would be a lie the user cannot see. That is the pattern T-336 sets for the checker and it should not be re-invented there.
  **The plan is rendered and not editable**, and the copy says why: *"the steps are not editable, which is what makes the run repeatable"*. Cost is shown before the click and **an unpriced deployment says so in words** rather than showing £0.00. Coverage appears twice, in the same shape, and the refusal — no bound sources — replaces the button rather than sitting under it.
  ⚠ **The bound-container path is refused WITH A POINTER, not built.** Arriving with `?containerId=` renders a refusal naming `Q-037` and sending the user to Tools. Ignoring the binding would have looked like it worked, which is the failure the pointer exists to prevent. Nothing here reads a plan row.
  **The label refusal is rendered in the creator's own words**, naming **both labels** — the T-295 rule reaching a second surface: *"this draft would draw on material X, the working area you chose is Y, writing it there would widen who can read it"*.
  **No recapture** — see T-334's note; the creator's screen is photographed by nothing.
- **T-395 — `apps/web` gets a test runner, and the load-bearing sentences get pinned.** ✅ **Built 2026-08-30.** *(Minted 2026-08-29 in review.)* The definition of done says **unit-tested**, and an entire app cannot be: `apps/web` has no test runner, so T-292's zero-source warning and T-295's both-labels block — the two most load-bearing sentences on their branch — shipped unpinned, and T-338's diff had already routed its tests into `packages/contracts` for the same want of one. **Done when:** `apps/web` runs a vitest suite under `turbo run test` like every other package, and the two sentences above (statement-not-menu; both labels named, blocked by default, reason mandatory) are asserted at render. | *(Deps: none)*
  **As built. *Plainly: the web app can finally run tests, and the two most safety-critical sentences on its screens are now checked by one.*** `apps/web` runs `vitest run` under `turbo run test` like every other package, inheriting `test`'s `dependsOn: ["^typecheck"]` edge. Static markup via `renderToStaticMarkup`, following `packages/ui`'s own suite: what is under test is the **copy** and the **state it renders in**, both decided before any handler runs, so no DOM emulation is needed.
  **The `dedupe` line in the vitest config is not boilerplate and is worth naming.** The kit is consumed as SOURCE across the workspace, so without `resolve.dedupe: ['react', 'react-dom']` a kit component and an app component resolve two different Reacts and every hook in a kit component throws *"Cannot read properties of null (reading 'useState')"* — which reads as a broken component rather than as a resolution problem.
  **Both sentences are pinned.** T-292's zero case is asserted as a **statement**: the warning tone, the words, **and the absence of a dropdown** — the half that actually distinguishes it, since a menu offering an empty list reads as a loading failure. Its two neighbours are pinned with it, because the claim is only meaningful against them: a scope that could not be READ says nothing at all (a claim we could not check must not be made), and a non-empty scope IS a menu. T-295's block asserts **both labels in words**, the destination's name, *"so it is blocked"*, and the override **disabled until a reason is typed**.
  **One production change, and it is the reason the sentence was unpinnable.** `DestinationWarning`'s copy lived behind an effect and a network call, so it could not be rendered in a test at all. The fetch stays where it was and the block is now `DestinationBlock`, a pure component holding the words. Nothing about the behaviour moved — and the split is the honest general lesson: **a sentence that cannot be rendered in a test is a sentence nobody is checking.**

### Waypoint C — the checker

*Built 2026-08-31, the session after [ADR-0053](../architecture/adr/0053-the-checkers-run-and-the-executor-rule.md) was ruled and the one after the executor landed. Execution only: every design fork these tickets carry was settled by that ADR or by ADR-0048 and its two dated addenda, and nothing here re-derives one.*

- **T-310 — The checker DAG: the check families and their grain.** ✅ **Built 2026-08-31** (migration 0061). *(Plainly: build the five checks the QA checker actually performs, and somewhere to keep what they find.)* ✅ **Unblocked 2026-08-01 → ADR-0048; specified 2026-08-30 → [ADR-0053](../architecture/adr/0053-the-checkers-run-and-the-executor-rule.md) §2–§3.** The new capability, and the one a consultancy will judge. **Six families, and two of them cost nothing:** *style* (one section + the style guides, model), *corpus accuracy* (one section + the passages retrieved for it, model), *self-contradiction* (**one call** over the section summaries, which ride free as a by-product of the section calls), *readability* (**code** — scored per section against a project target with outliers flagged, **never pass/fail**, because Flesch-Kincaid scores technical prose badly by construction and a pass/fail would be a verdict), *completeness* (**code** — missing template sections and placeholder text), and the three inputs' three honest treatments unchanged from ADR-0048 §7. **Corpus accuracy carries a depth**: *quick* searches once per section; *full* extracts the section's checkable assertions and searches for each, which is what catches a buried figure rather than only a section's main topic. **Full is the default** — a too-cheap default fails invisibly, a too-expensive one fails visibly. ⚠ **The launcher, the planner and the coverage statement are T-336, not here** — this ticket builds the checks; T-336 decides how many of each run. | *(Deps: T-328, T-396, T-397 — re-cut in review 2026-08-30: T-271/T-274/T-308 are built, and none of the six ruled check families uses the extractor, so T-274 was a stale dependency, not a wait)*
  **As built. *Plainly: the QA checker's five checks now exist and run, and what they find is written down for the first time — so the rule that an unresolved problem stops a draft being promoted has stopped being a rule about an empty list.*** Three things landed together, and they had to: the checks, the store the checks write into, and the promotion gate's seam closing onto that store.
  **FIVE FAMILIES, THREE CAPABILITIES, AND THE GRAIN IS THE CAPABILITY BOUNDARY.** ADR-0053 §2 gives each family its own unit of work, so a single capability could not have held them: `qa_section_check` takes one section and everything it is read against (style, corpus accuracy), `qa_contradiction_check` takes the section summaries and nothing else, and `qa_document_check` takes the whole draft and **calls no model at all** (readability, completeness). ADR-0027 fixes code-or-model **per capability at design time**, so one capability spanning arithmetic and a model call would have had no honest declaration to make — the split is that rule, not tidiness. Three `step_type` values, drawn before written. `createQaDocumentCheck` is handed **no `Router` and has none to be handed**, so its CODE declaration is structural rather than a promise in a comment.
  ⚠ **ADR-0053 §2 says "six families" and its own table lists five.** Built as the table specifies, which is also what T-310's board entry enumerates and what §3 forces: *"on conflict the project style guide wins and firm know-how fills in where the project is silent"* is a precedence **one reader has to apply**, so splitting the two style sources into two families would leave nothing able to resolve the conflict. Recorded in [checker.ts](../../packages/contracts/src/checker.ts) rather than silently reconciled.
  🔒 **THE ADMISSION RULES ARE THE TICKET.** ADR-0048 promises a surface three things — the finding points at real text (§2), a quoted rule is the rule verbatim (§5), each input gets its own treatment (§7) — and none survives a model trusted to fill the fields in. So the model supplies a **quote** and a **marker**, never an offset and never a rule's words. A quote not present in the section resolves to no anchor and the finding is **discarded and counted**; a style finding naming a rule this run did not load is discarded; a corpus finding citing a passage this run did not see is discarded — `extractor`'s own rule, one capability along. **The quoted clause text is read out of our copy of the clause**, so a model-authored "quote" of a rule cannot reach a screen where it would be unfalsifiable. The discards are counted rather than swallowed, because *"no findings"* and *"the model answered and none of it was usable"* are opposite facts.
  **The store is `findings`, drawer 4, migration 0061** — drawn in [data-model.md](data-model.md) before it was written. Drawer 4 and not drawer 2 is the near-miss worth naming: a finding resolves like a sandbox comment and is counted beside one, but it is **produced by a run**, may carry a **Suggestion** as its fix, and clearing it is a human resolution of an agent's output, which is drawer 4's whole subject. Mutable, for the sandbox comment's reason. Three `CHECK`s, each closing a way the row could lie: the `input` column must match its evidence payload, the fix classification is present **exactly when** the proposed revision is, and a closed finding **names who closed it and when**.
  🔒 **`classifyFix` runs at the write, and nothing else may set `fix`.** T-398 built the structural test; this is where it bites. The model proposes a replacement, the test decides whether it may ever appear under T-311's accept-all, and the Suggestion it becomes enters the accept/edit/reject path that is already audited, already reversible and already produces Signals — so the checker acquires **no write path the drafting side lacks** (ADR-0048 §3).
  **T-332's seam is closed, and closing it changed one function body and no caller.** That is worth recording because it is the whole argument for building a seam rather than an omission: the signature T-332 wrote was already the one the real query needed, `promotion-gate.test.ts`'s empty case still asserts zero on a document with no findings and still passes, and nothing else in the promotion path learned that a finding exists. The real query lives in [findings.ts](../../apps/api/src/findings.ts) beside the writes and is re-exported through `open-items.ts`'s own name.
  🔒 **THE WALL IS ENFORCED IN THE READ, NOT IN THE RENDER** (ADR-0048 §6, ADR-0053 §9), and the two style sources come out on opposite sides of it. A finding quoting a **firm's** rulebook is **absent** from another organisation's read — absent and not redacted, because a blanked finding still tells the other firm that a rule of ours has something to say about this paragraph. A finding quoting the **project's** style guide reaches everyone on the project, because it binds everyone and quoting it across the wall is the point of it. The owning organisation is resolved through `rulebooks` at read time rather than copied onto the finding, so the wall has **one answer** to *"whose is this"*; a reference that no longer resolves **fails closed**, since an unresolvable pointer is not evidence that a clause was shareable.
  ⚠ **TWO ADDITIONS TO A TYPE ADR-0048 FIXED, BOTH FLAGGED RATHER THAN SMUGGLED.** (1) **`RulebookEvidence.scope`** — `organisation` or `project`. ADR-0053 §9 rules that privacy belongs to the source's **scope** rather than to the word "rulebook", and the existing shape could not express which of the two style sources a quote came from, so the wall predicate had nothing to read. (2) **`FindingInput` gains `draft`.** ADR-0048 §7 named the three inputs the checker checks *against*, written when the checker was conceived as reading a draft against external material; ADR-0053 §2 then ruled five families of which **three check the draft against nothing external at all** — self-contradiction compares its own sections, readability is arithmetic over its sentences, completeness compares it with its template. None has a passage, an excerpt or a clause to point at, and forcing one into `corpus` with an empty citation list would have stored exactly the dishonest object the union exists to make untypeable. The treatment is the honest one and reopens nothing — **nothing external, so nothing cited** — and `DraftEvidence` carries no Citation and no clause, only what the finding was measured against, in words. **Recorded as a deviation for the owner to rule on**: it reads to this session as an implementation consequence of ADR-0053 §2 rather than a design fork, since no reading of it changes what a user sees, but it is an extension to a type another ADR fixed and should not pass unremarked.
  **A named person, registered same-commit.** `findings.closed_by_participant_id` and `closed_at` are in [personal-data.md](../architecture/personal-data.md), `CHECK`-enforced as a pair on the `users.removed_by_user_id` precedent. **A dismissal records no reason**, deliberately (ADR-0053 §6): declining forty advisory findings from one rule is one professional judgement, not forty skipped.
  🔒 **PER RUN OF ONE DOCUMENT, AND NOTHING ACROSS RUNS.** There is no column, index, key or query relating one run's findings to the previous run's, and a test asserts that a second run's identical finding lands as a **second row**. **Whether findings persist across runs of the same document** — so a dismissal is remembered and a re-raised finding recognised — is ADR-0048's own open lifecycle question, given a driver by ADR-0053 §13 and deliberately left unruled by the checker session. A carry-over built here would have been answering it in schema.
  **What this ticket deliberately does NOT build, per its own boundary.** No launcher, no planner, no route, no coverage statement — *"this ticket builds the checks; T-336 decides how many of each run"*. The pieces the planner will drive are present and typed: `clauseSlice` **takes** a style-clause pass (ADR-0053 §5's split-rather-than-drop) where T-336 **computes** how many passes there are; `splitIntoSections` is the deterministic width the plan will be computed from; and the attached-document excerpts (ADR-0022 — never grounds, never cited) are an **input** the capability handles correctly and that T-336's *"attach a document"* affordance supplies.
  **The section splitter is deterministic and that is load-bearing rather than tidy.** The planner's width is the section count, so a splitter consulting a model would have moved the non-determinism one file below where anybody would look for it and lost the declared-workflow promise there instead. Pinned by its own test, ahead of T-336's planner-determinism test which runs through it.
  ⚠ **The `step_type` widening needed a label the compiler only asks for on a cold cache.** `RunTrace`'s `LABEL` is a `Record` over the step union, so three new values made it a compile error — and its own header records T-331 finding exactly this before: it *"typechecks only while a stale turbo cache hides it"*. `pnpm run check` went green on a warm cache and the failure surfaced on the next ticket's forced run. Labelled here; worth naming because the guard exists and still let a widening past.
  **Two small judgements worth naming.** The checker's model calls route on the existing **`verify`** task class — claim verification, frontier tier — rather than widening the Wave 5 task vocabulary for a new caller; that is the routing class and **not** the `verifier` worker, which stays beyond V1. And the three capabilities are registered **unconditionally** where `document_builder` and `extractor` are conditional: those need domain content a deployment may not carry, while a project with no style guide and no rulebook still gets a corpus check, a contradiction check and the two arithmetic families — making the whole capability absent for want of a style guide would turn a stated coverage gap into a missing tool. *(Review note, 2026-08-31: the flagged type extension is three additions, not two — `checkFamily` extends the same fixed type and was caught in review; all three are now recorded as a dated note on ADR-0048 itself.)*

- **T-311 — The marked-up edit: the checker's output surface.** ✅ **Built 2026-08-31.** *(Plainly: the reviewer's screen — the checker's findings as marks in the draft and as a list, taken or set aside one at a time.)* ✅ **Unblocked 2026-08-01 → ADR-0048**, which decided the surface rather than following it; **re-scoped the same day** to a marked-up edit the reviewer accepts or rejects change by change, as the Word add-in already behaves. **Re-cut 2026-08-30 → [ADR-0053](../architecture/adr/0053-the-checkers-run-and-the-executor-rule.md) §6, and `Q-031`'s caveat is now a ruling this ticket carries rather than a question it waits on.** **Two views of one set:** the document with marks anchored into the text, *and* a **grouped-by-check** panel that unrolls to its findings. **Bulk acceptance is permitted for *mechanical* fixes only** — a consistent substitution, expressible as find-and-replace and displayable in one line — and **never for rewrites**, which stay per-mark always; a group therefore shows its mechanical fixes with an accept-all *above* its rewrites without one, so the distinction is on the screen rather than only in the ADR. **Bulk dismissal** by rule, severity or check is permitted and **records no reason** (it resolves findings; it does not override ADR-0049 §7's gate). Which kind a fix is comes from **T-398**, not from a judgement made here. **Two obligations remain load-bearing:** a **quoted rule must render differently from a grounded citation**, and a quoted *firm-rulebook* clause is **org-private** — but a quoted **project style guide** clause is not, because it binds every organisation on the project (ADR-0053 §9). **Anchoring is the whole point.** | *(Deps: T-328, T-310, T-398)*
  **As built. *Plainly: the reviewer's screen. What the checker found is shown twice — as marks in the draft itself and as a list grouped by the check that raised each one — and the reviewer takes each suggested wording change or sets it aside. Corrections that are the same small change made over and over can be taken in one click; new sentences the AI wrote cannot, and the screen says why.*** Two views of **one** set, from **one** read: a second read for the panel would be a second answer to *"what did the checker find"*, and the two would eventually disagree about which marks exist.
  **The marks ride the mirror the comment anchors already use, and they anchor better than comments do.** A comment's anchor is an advisory quote *searched for* in the text; a finding carries real offsets (ADR-0048 §2), so its span is used directly and then **verified against the words under it**. A draft edited since the check ran simply does not paint that mark — the same degrade rule, one grain more precisely. Findings are toned by severity and are visibly not comment anchors: a comment is a colleague asking a question, a finding is a check reporting a defect, and the advisory tone is deliberately quiet because neither severity is a verdict on the document.
  🔒 **THE ACCEPT-ALL SITS ABOVE A GROUP'S MECHANICAL FIXES AND NO REWRITE EVER GETS ONE**, which is ADR-0053 §6's ruling made into a layout. A mixed group renders the accept-all scoped to its mechanical half, then the sentence *"The rest are rewritten wording, so they are read one at a time"*, then the rewrites with no bulk control anywhere near them. The button states the **size** of the decision (*"Scheme → scheme, 55 places"*), which is the whole difference between bulk acceptance and bulk inattention. Which kind a fix is comes from `Finding.fix` — `classifyFix`'s structural verdict (T-398) — never from a judgement made on the surface and never from the model.
  🔒 **And the split is enforced in the SERVER, not on the screen.** The layout is the honest fact being *shown*; a client that put a rewrite in a bulk batch anyway would be sending exactly the request ADR-0048 §3 exists to refuse. So the route checks every id **before applying any of them** and refuses the batch **whole** — a half-applied batch is a decision the reviewer never took, landing on the half nobody read. Asserted with the document's text unchanged and every finding still open after the refusal.
  **Accepting a fix REPLACES the span it pointed at.** `resolveSuggestion` has carried a comment since T-053 saying *"the anchored per-item apply arrives with the anchor model"*; it has arrived. An optional anchor makes the apply an `overlay` over the finding's own offsets instead of an append — appending a corrected sentence to the end of a chapter is not a correction — and the unanchored path is byte-identical for the callers that pass none. **A bulk accept applies descending by span**, so writing one never moves the next.
  **A drifted anchor degrades and never blocks** (T-112's pattern, and the sandbox head is mutable by design). The drift test runs **before** the Signal is written, because a Signal is the record that a human resolved something and an acceptance that could not land resolved nothing: nothing is written, no Signal exists, **the finding stays open** because its defect has not been dealt with, and the panel says which marks moved and that the reviewer should look at them rather than take the suggestion blind.
  **Bulk dismissal takes anything and records no reason** (ADR-0053 §6) — declining forty advisory findings from one rule is one professional judgement, not forty skipped — and it **resolves** rather than overrides: a test dismisses one of two findings and asserts the promotion gate still counts the other. There is no reason column to fill in, deliberately, and the resolution names who did it, which is what makes it an audit record.
  🔒 **A QUOTED RULE IS NOT A SOURCE CHIP** (ADR-0048 §5), and this is pinned in `apps/web`'s own suite because *"the distinction survives in the model and dies on the screen"* is a failure that still looks like a working page. A rule renders as a quotation with its clause address and the source it binds through — *"project style guide"* or *"your firm's rulebook"*, which are two different answers to who may read it — and never as a `SourceChip`. An attached excerpt says on its face that it is **not a project source** (ADR-0022). A finding measured against the draft itself cites nothing at all. Only a corpus finding gets chips, because only a corpus finding is grounded. Five renders, five assertions.
  ⚠ **The org-private wall is in the server's read, and today it sits BEHIND a wider one — recorded rather than asserted around.** `listFindings` withholds a quoted **firm-rulebook** clause from any other organisation, resolving the owning organisation through `rulebooks` so the wall has one answer, and **fails closed** on a reference that no longer resolves; a quoted **project style guide** clause reaches everyone on the project, because it binds everyone (ADR-0053 §9). That guarantee is proven at store grain. At the **route** layer it is currently defence in depth: every `/sandbox-documents/:id/*` endpoint runs `documentScope`, which is org-private on the document's own organisation, so another firm cannot reach the document at all — share or no share. This endpoint follows that established posture rather than inventing a wider one, and the test says so in words instead of quietly passing for the wrong reason.
  **The panel never says the document is fine.** An empty state reads *"no findings have been recorded against this draft"* and points at the coverage statement that will sit beside them — because *"no findings"* must always mean *"no findings in what was read"*, and this surface is not the thing entitled to say how much that was.
  **One small vocabulary decision.** `dismissed` is not `rejected`: a rejected **Suggestion** is a judgement about proposed prose and writes a Signal (ADR-0026's raw material), while a dismissed **finding** is a judgement about the defect — and most findings carry no proposal at all, so there is nothing to have an opinion about. Both close the finding; only the first records one. *(Review correction: the drift banner states how MANY marks moved, not which — the record's "says which marks moved" overstated the copy. The banner now carries a render test either way.)*

- **T-336 — The QA checker as a tool: the launcher, the plan, and the run.** ✅ **Built 2026-08-31.** *(Plainly: make the QA checker a tool anyone can open — pick a draft, see what the run will do and cover before it runs, then run it.)* ✅ **Un-fogged 2026-08-30 → [ADR-0053](../architecture/adr/0053-the-checkers-run-and-the-executor-rule.md).** The number was reserved on the fog note and is claimed here. **Reached two ways that are one mechanism**: from Tools (T-334), or from the document editor via a tool chip that opens the same launcher with the document pre-bound — the editor route being the Tools route with its first step pre-filled, so there is **one run shape and one place the scope is stated**. **A run covers one document.** **The launch is a sequence that keeps its state**: pick the document → pick the checks and their settings → see the plan → step back, change one thing, come forward with the rest intact. Presets — **Quick check** and **Full check** — set the families and the corpus depth together and stay individually adjustable, with **Full the default**. 🔒 **The planner is CODE, and that is load-bearing rather than an optimisation.** It reads the document's structure and length and emits the plan; if a model decided the run's shape, the same document would produce different plans on different days and the checker could not be a **declared** workflow at all — losing the one guarantee a tool is sold on. Three shapes, and the plan names which it took: **short** → one pass, all checks together (self-contradiction free, one reader sees everything); **ordinary** → fan out per section, then compare summaries; **very long** → summaries compared in **groups**, and **the plan says cross-section checking is weaker**, because it degrades loudly or not at all. 🔒 **Split rather than drop, and state coverage twice.** A style guide that will not fit alongside a section runs over it in **two passes** — the context limit becomes something the plan routes around rather than a silent truncator. Coverage is stated **in the plan before the run and beside the findings after, in the same shape** (*"11 sections · 4 checks · style guide 80 of 80, in 2 passes"*), as a **first-class output, not a footnote**: it is the only thing distinguishing a clean result from an unexamined one, and it closes the same failure arriving through three doors — the style guide truncated, retrieval matching nothing, and a user-narrowed scope. **The plan is rendered but not editable**; the user shapes it by changing **parameters**, which keeps the run `declared` (hand-editing a step list would not — see the deferred register on T-267). **Two document-selection affordances, named differently because they are two guarantees**: *check against library documents* (default the whole access-resolved library, narrowable by a picker; findings **cite normally**) and *attach a document* (upload or from the user's own sandbox; **never grounds, never cited**, ADR-0022). Attaching a *library* document silently yields the weaker treatment, so the copy must say which you get. The picker is **assembled, not filtered** — an unreachable document is **absent**, never greyed. | *(Deps: T-334, T-310, T-311, T-396, T-397)*
  **As built. *Plainly: the QA checker is now a tool anyone can open. You pick a draft, pick how hard to look, and are shown — before a penny is spent — how the run will be broken up, roughly what it will cost, and exactly what it will and will not cover. Afterwards the same sentence comes back with what actually happened in it, beside what was found.*** The tile in Tools flipped from *not built yet* to live in this commit, and the copy that named T-336 by name went with it.
  🔒 **THE PLANNER IS CODE, AND ITS DETERMINISM IS ASSERTED RATHER THAN ASSUMED.** [qa-plan.ts](../../packages/capabilities/src/qa-plan.ts) reads the section split, the clause count and the chosen parameters, and emits the plan; nothing in it consults a model and nothing it reads was written by one. `qa-plan.test.ts`'s first case plans the same document **twice and requires the two to be deep-equal** — every step, every family, the priced estimate and the fan-out lists — because a test that only checked the plan looked sensible would pass just as well against a model-planned run. There is a second one over HTTP, at the boundary a user meets. If a model decided the run's shape, the same document would produce different plans on different days and the checker could not be a **declared** workflow at all.
  **Three shapes, and the plan names which it took.** *Short* — it all fits in one call, so self-contradiction comes free and no comparison step is planned, because one reader genuinely saw everything. *Ordinary* — a pass per section, then one comparison. *Very long* — the summaries themselves exceed one call, so they are compared in **groups**, and the plan says in words that a contradiction between two sections in different groups will not be found. 🔒 It degrades **loudly or not at all**, and the caveat renders **above** the run button, which `apps/web`'s own suite pins by string position.
  🔒 **SPLIT RATHER THAN DROP** (ADR-0053 §5). A style guide that will not fit alongside a section is run over that section in two passes, half the clauses each — one more call, and the whole manual covered. Two tests carry it: one asserts every unit gets more than one pass when the clauses are tight, and one plans a manual at 60 clauses and at 90 and requires the pass count and the cost to **rise visibly** while both state their full clause ratio. There is **no day on which the checker silently weakens**.
  ⚠ **And that test found a real second-copy bug before it found anything else.** The coverage sentence recomputed the pass count with its own arithmetic instead of reading the passes the planner had produced, so a plan could describe a split it was not taking. The sentence is now built from the fan-out list itself. **Two formulas is how a plan starts describing a run it is not**, which is T-373's finding in a smaller place.
  🔒 **THE PLAN AND THE RUN CANNOT DISAGREE ABOUT WHAT RUNS**, and this took three corrections to get right — each caught by a test rather than by review. Every step count in the plan is the length of a bound `id_list`, so the fan-out widths ARE the plan: `passes` is empty when no per-section family was selected, `groups` is empty in the short shape, and `measures` is the arithmetic step. The `qa_document_check` capability now also **honours the selected families** — it used to run both halves regardless, reporting findings from a check the user had switched off. And **the arithmetic step always runs**, because it is also where the run totals up what it read: the checker's answer is its **coverage**, not prose, which is why it is the `present` step.
  **Coverage, stated twice in the same shape** (ADR-0053 §5). *"6 sections · 5 checks · the whole library, searched statement by statement · style guide 5 of 5 clauses"* before, and *"6 of 6 sections read · 5 checks · 5 passages of the record read · style guide 5 of 5 clauses"* after. It states the absences the findings list cannot show — a section the library said nothing about, a suggested finding the admission rules discarded, a library that returned nothing at all — because **it is the only thing distinguishing a clean result from an unexamined one**. The launcher's result card says *"No findings in what was read — the sentence above is what that claim rests on"* rather than anything resembling *your document is fine*.
  **The launch keeps its state, and the plan is rendered but not editable.** Pick, configure, see the plan, step back and change one thing without re-entering the rest; changing any answer discards the **plan** and keeps the **answers**. Presets set the families and the depth together and stay individually adjustable, with **Full the default** — a too-cheap default fails invisibly and a too-expensive one fails visibly, and a system should prefer the failure its user can see. Hand-editing a step list would make the plan `model_chosen` by T-267's own correct rule (ADR-0053 §12), so there is no control that would do it, and a test asserts the absence.
  **The editor route is the Tools route with its first step pre-filled**, which is the whole of *one launcher, one run shape, one place the scope is stated*. The editor's Check button navigates to `tools/qa-check?documentId=…`; it does not run anything, because a checker that ran straight off a toolbar button would be a second launcher with no plan and no coverage statement.
  **Two document-selection affordances, named differently because they are two guarantees** (ADR-0053 §3). *Check against library documents* defaults to the whole access-resolved library, narrows through an **assembled** picker (an unreachable document is absent, never greyed), and its findings **cite normally**. *Attach a document* never grounds and is never cited; its evidence is an excerpt. Both sentences are pinned in `apps/web`'s suite, because attaching a *library* document silently yields the strictly worse result and a user would otherwise have no way to know they took the weak path.
  ⚠ **What is NOT built, said plainly on the screen: uploading a file straight into a check.** ADR-0053 §3 names *"upload or from the user's own sandbox"* and only the second half landed — a pinned sandbox document is read directly and treated correctly, and an upload would need the parse-and-store path the style-guide loader has. The copy says so where the control would be, rather than leaving a dead affordance.
  **A DECLARED WORKFLOW, and it needed one engine addition.** [qa-check.yaml](../../packages/workflows/definitions/qa-check.yaml) fans out over the planner's own lists; a reference to a fanned-out step (`{{steps.check.output}}`) now resolves to the **array of its expansions' outputs, in plan order**, which is the natural completion of T-396's fan-out rather than a new mechanism — the comparison step exists precisely to read what every section read produced. Nothing that references an ordinary step changes.
  🔒 **AND A CHAT TURN IS NOW NEVER CLASSIFIED INTO A PLANNER-SHAPED WORKFLOW.** T-309 had already excluded workflows that **write**; the checker writes nothing, so that filter did not catch it — and the classifier promptly matched it, which the T-266 suite caught as a run labelled `model_chosen` that should have been `declared`. A fan-out's width is computed by a planner before the run and a chat turn runs no planner, so a classifier that matched the checker would bind a width of zero and report success over a run that did nothing. One clause in `runs.ts`, and the guarantee is structural.
  **Five things this ticket found by running against the seeded world**, each recorded because the failure was invisible from the code alone. (1) **The section splitter required a blank line BELOW a heading**, which is the shape `document_builder` writes and *not* the shape people write — so a real chapter became one section and the fan-out never fired. (2) **`RunTrace`'s label map** needed the three new step types, and it typechecks until the turbo cache is cold. (3) **Nothing seeded either style source**, so T-397's two stores could not be demonstrated at all — both are seeded now, differently, because they are scoped differently. (4) **The e2e substrate carried no workflow or worker registry**, so a tool shipped in T-334/T-335 could not be driven through a browser and the walkthrough could not photograph one. (5) **The coverage tally read the wrong step key** once `measure` gained a fan-out, and reported *"1 of 6 sections read"* for a run that read all six; understating coverage is the same class of error as overstating it.
  ⚠ **`pnpm run check`'s exit status was being swallowed.** Piping it into `tail` reports the pipe's status, so three earlier greens in this session meant nothing — the one that mattered had `docs/build/data-model.html` stale against T-310's own table.
