It is regenerated here rather than in T-310's commit, which is the one place this session's per-ticket discipline is imperfect, and it is recorded rather than quietly tidied.
  **The walkthrough recapture ran in full — 42 shots, no byte-identical pairs.** The checker sits inside the user stories' one journey, which [v1.md](v1.md) names outright (*"a colleague runs the QA checker over the draft"*), so this is three new beats in Act II and an amended consultant story, not a component-doc note. The capture **works through the marks before Act III**, because it has to: an open finding blocks promotion exactly as an open comment thread does, so a capture that left them open would meet the open-items gate at the next beat instead of the QA-source one it is there to show. The mechanical group goes in one click and the rewrite is read and set aside, which is the distinction on the screen. *(Review notes, 2026-08-31: "42 shots, no byte-identical pairs" means no two shots equal each other — seven are unchanged from before the branch, correctly, being screens this work never touched. The unbuilt upload half is now owned: minted as T-399.)*

**T-399 — Upload a file straight into a check.** ✅ **Built 2026-08-31.** *(Minted 2026-08-31 in review — the absence was stated on screen and in T-336's record, and owned by nobody.)* *Plainly: today you can only check a draft that already lives in your working area; handing the checker a file directly is the other half ADR-0053 §3 names.* The parse-and-store path exists in the style-guide loader (T-397) and the checker's scope statement already covers attached documents; this wires an upload into that path and removes the "not built yet" copy at its control. Transient-input rules apply as T-337 established them: parsed in-request unless deliberately stored, never quietly corpus. | *(Deps: T-336)*
  **As built. *Plainly: you can now hand the checker a file directly instead of filing it in your working area first.*** The screen's *"not built yet"* sentence is gone and an **Upload a file…** control stands where it was, taking Word, Excel, PowerPoint and PDF — **the same extractor the style guide and the corpus already use** (T-397, T-303), because two parsers would be two answers to what a document says. An unreadable file is refused in that loader's own vocabulary, **before the plan is computed and long before anything is spent**. **THE TICKET'S REAL CONTENT IS WHERE THE TEXT TRAVELS, and the first shape drawn for it was wrong in a way that would have shipped silently.** The obvious move is a workflow parameter carrying the excerpt. But a declared workflow's bound parameters are written to `plan_steps.inputs`, a `jsonb` column, for every step the executor walks — so that parameter would have written the user's file into the run record. That is the upload being **stored**, which T-337's transient-input rule forbids and which this ticket's own *"deliberately stored nowhere"* clause forbids a second time: **the mechanism built to satisfy the rule would have violated it, and every other acceptance test would still have passed.** *(Caught by the owner in review, against the schema, before it was built.)* **So the text rides the run's in-memory context and the record keeps a fingerprint.** `ChainInput` and `LeafContext` gained `attachments` — the door T-299's Lens already uses for request-scoped facts, resolved at the API boundary and held for the life of the walk. The section check reads `ctx.attachments` **beside** the excerpts it resolves from `attached_document_ids`, so an attachment is an attachment from there down: same excerpt markers, same never-cited treatment, same coverage count. What persists is `attached_uploads`, an ordinary `string` parameter carrying **name, byte size and SHA-256 per file and not one word of the text** — enough for the record to say exactly which file the run read, and checkable by anyone holding the same file, which is what an audit of an unstored input can honestly offer instead of the input. **The consequence is stated in the plan before any spend, because it is the design and not a gap:** a run with an upload cannot be re-executed from its record alone, and the caveat says so — *"read for this run and kept nowhere afterwards … running this check again means attaching the file again"*. **The uploaded file is NAMED, where a sandbox pin is counted**, in both the plan's scope statement and the coverage sentence — *"attached: Ecology_Baseline.docx — never grounds, never cited"* — and the asymmetry is deliberate: a pin can be looked up later by its id, an upload is stored nowhere, so its name is the only handle the record will ever have. The two sentences stay in the SAME SHAPE (ADR-0053 §5) or they stop being comparable. **`attachedSourceId` is minted per run** — a handle, not a stored document's id; `findings.evidence` is `jsonb` with no foreign key, so no migration. **⚠ ONE HONEST QUALIFICATION on "stored nowhere":** where a finding arises from the upload, that finding's evidence carries its excerpt, and findings are stored. That is ADR-0022's own rule — *the evidence is an excerpt* — and it is exactly the treatment a sandbox-pinned document already gets; the document's text as a whole is never written. Said here because *"stored nowhere"* would otherwise read as broader than it is. **Verified, not assumed: no fan-out width depends on the attachment.** `passes` comes from the draft's sections and the style-clause token budget, `groups` from the section count, `measures` is the literal `['code']` — `attachedDocuments` reaches only caveat and coverage prose. A test asserts the plan's step list is identical with and without a file, so attaching one cannot change how many calls a run makes. **Nine acceptance tests, and the negative ones carry the ticket**: the fingerprint is in `plan_steps.inputs` and the file's words are not; the upload becomes no sandbox document, no version and no style guide; an unreadable file and an unsupported format are both refused; and the plain JSON request is asserted unchanged, since an upload is an addition to a check request and not a new shape for one. **Three render tests** pin the deleted sentence stays deleted, the control offers the formats the extractor actually reads, and the *kept nowhere* promise is made **on screen** and not only in the record. **Reported rather than folded in silently:** the CSRF guard's multipart allow-list gained both qa-check endpoints (ADR-0044's posture is unchanged — they take the same browser-provenance check every other upload route takes), and the `.docx` test fixture moved out of `style-guide.test.ts` into `test-docx.ts` so the two suites build a real file the same way instead of twice. **The plan endpoint takes the file too**, because a preflight that could not see the attachment would understate the coverage of the run it previews. **No migration, no personal data.**
  *(Review, 2026-08-31 — two hardenings applied, one analogy corrected, one gap noted.)* (1) 🔴 **The upload parse was unbounded on an unthrottled route any project participant can post to** — the plan legitimately recomputes on every changed answer, so this was the one place a member could spend the server's memory freely; the style-guide precedent the record leans on is curator-gated and the repo's other capped route (`plan.ts`, 5 MB) is the stronger one. Bounded in review: **5 files, 20 MB per file**, refused in words before anything is buffered, with tests for both refusals. (2) **The CSRF allowlist matched on path alone**, so a plain-JSON request to the two dual-mode check routes bypassed the content-type gate; the allowlist branch now applies only to genuinely multipart requests, tested. (3) The record's "the door T-299's Lens already uses" is inexact — a Lens rides `ChainInput` but not `LeafContext`, and it IS persisted to the plan, which the attachments deliberately are not; the mechanism is new and correct, the precedent named for it was not. (4) **The signature output is unphotographed**: the capture shows the upload control but never a file actually attached, so the *"attached: Ecology_Baseline.docx — never grounds, never cited"* coverage sentence exists in tests and in no photograph — noted for the next capture pass rather than forced now.

### The walkthrough learns the tools

*Built 2026-08-31, the session after the checker landed, on the owner's ruling of the same day that widened the walkthrough's charter. Capture and narrative only — no product code was touched, and where a screen could not be photographed well the defect is recorded rather than fixed around.*

- **T-400 — The walkthrough gains a section per tool.** ✅ **Built 2026-08-31.** *Plainly: until now the walkthrough photographed one journey — a document being planned, drafted, checked, reviewed and accepted. It did not photograph the two standalone tools a consultant opens from the Tools menu, so two shipped surfaces existed in the product and in nobody's picture. This ticket adds a section per tool, each following the user's own clicks: the document creator, then the QA checker.* **Owner ruling, 2026-08-31: the page's charter is the journey AND the tools, because a product surface nobody has photographed is one nobody has read back.** The rule is now in `CLAUDE.md`'s "a surface is not finished when it merges", amended in this commit and dated to the ruling, with the rest of the rule — component docs for other outside-the-journey work, a card rather than a forced beat where a thing cannot be photographed, and the mockup dying at capture — left intact. The walkthrough's row in [the architecture index](../architecture/README.md) now regenerates on a change to the journey *or to a tool's section*. | *(Deps: T-335, T-336, T-368)*
  **A TOOL GETS NO USER STORY, AND THAT IS THE REASON THEY NEEDED A PART OF THEIR OWN.** [user-stories.md](../architecture/user-stories.md) follows one deliverable through its life; a tool is a thing a consultant opens on any day against whatever is in front of them, and writing one into that document would have bent a journey around a menu item. So `user-stories.md` is untouched, the tools' sections sit **after** the seven acts under their own head, and that head says in one line why they are there without a story. The non-duplication rule the sections are built to: **at most one journey beat per tool**, saying what happened in the story and pointing into the tool's section, with the granular shots living in the section.
  **THE ACT II RECONCILIATION.** The checker had arrived in the journey the day before as three beats — the plan (09a), the coverage statement (09b) and the marks (09c). Two of them were photographs of the *tool* rather than of the story, and they are exactly what the checker's own section now shows step by step, so **09a and 09b are gone from the page and from the capture**, their two PNGs deleted, and their shot calls removed while the run itself stays — the story depends on it, because an open finding blocks promotion at Act III exactly as an open comment thread does. What remains in Act II is **one beat, 09c**, rewritten to say what Eleanor did to her draft before anyone else saw it and to point at the section. The creator gains **no** journey beat: nothing in the story is drafted by it, and inventing a beat to balance the two tools would have put a fiction in the one document that photographs only what happened.
  **THE SHOTS.** 59 in the page, 19 of them new, **no byte-identical pairs** — the known capture failure, checked by checksum over the whole set on every run. The creator's section is 8 beats: Tools and its tiles, the launcher as it opens, the outline chosen and the intent stated, the sources bound, the plan with its price, the run's coverage statement, the draft landing in the working area, and the bound-deliverable refusal. The checker's is 11: the draft chosen, the presets with one check adjusted by hand, the two document-selection controls and the upload that is not built, the plan, the run's before-and-after in one frame, the marks in the text, the panel pointing back into it, the drift banner, the accept-all above the mechanical fixes, the rewrite alone with none, and the bulk dismissal. Every new below-the-fold shot uses an explicit `scrollIntoView({ block: 'start' })` or the new `panelTop` helper; `scrollIntoViewIfNeeded` is a no-op when the target already peeks in, which is how a beat comes out a duplicate of its neighbour.
  **THE DRIFT BANNER WAS STAGED RATHER THAN SKIPPED, and it is the beat this section would have been poorer without.** The degrade path's only visible sentence: the capture edits the very sentence a finding points at — *"the former works"* becomes *"the former railway works at Wrenfield Sidings"*, visible in the shot — then asks the checker to apply its own correction to it. Nothing is written, the finding stays open, and the banner says one mark has moved and that the reader should look at it themselves rather than take the suggestion blind. The capture then **puts the sentence back exactly as the check read it** before the triage beats below, which is the one act in these two sections that is a reset rather than a step of the tool, and the page's provenance footer says so.
  **THE CHECKER RUNS ON A WORKING COPY OF ITS OWN**, created and filled through the API. By the time the tools' sections run — last, deliberately, so a tool writing into the sandbox halfway through cannot put a stray document in Act II's shots — the journey's draft has been frozen, promoted, reviewed and accepted, and a frozen head is read-only while every triage beat rewrites the text it works on.
  ⚠ **THREE THINGS THE CAPTURE WALKED INTO, PHOTOGRAPHED AS FOUND AND NOT FIXED — this session was allowed one number and spent it on the page.** (1) **The bound-deliverable refusal renders its clause number and its link as columns.** `.banner` is `display: flex`, so every inline child of a notice becomes a flex item and the prose is broken into fragments; the refusal is close to unreadable. It is a defect in the shared notice component, not in the creator, and it affects **every notice that carries a link or a code**. (2) **The creator's coverage sentence counts a section the document does not have.** The run reports *"1 of 4 sections written"* into a document that is **empty**: `splitByHeadings` files text that arrives before any of the template's headings as `unsectioned`, the content assembly correctly writes nothing for it, and the coverage tally counts the same material as a section written. The substrate's deterministic stand-in is what produces headingless prose here, but the tally would overstate for any model whose headings did not match — and this is the one surface whose whole job is to be the difference between a clean result and an unexamined one. Both carry gap cards on the page; the second is flagged **"Found by this capture"**, which needed the gap card's fixed *"Designed, not yet surfaced"* label to become a field. (3) **Both tools' estimated cost reads *not priced***, because this substrate declares no rate for the model that would serve the call — correct behaviour, and the beats say so rather than pretending a number.
  🐛 **A rendering bug in the page's own narrative, fixed here.** `esc` escaped the `<` of a `<strong>` written into a beat, so Act IV's moderation beat had been rendering a literal `&lt;strong>` since T-356. Prose now passes through `rich`, which lets `<strong>` and `<em>` through and escapes everything else in one pass, so an escaped `&` cannot be unescaped by a later replace and a beat still writes "Calder & Hale" rather than an entity.
  **GATES.** Full recapture to completion on a fresh seed, 59 shots, checksum-clean; downscaled into `docs/architecture/user-story-screens/`; `build.mjs` rebuilt. The e2e suite then ran **twice on one fresh seed** with the API restarted, because the capture mutates the world and a suite run on its leavings means nothing. `pnpm run check` was read from its own exit code, never through a pipe — the mistake T-336's record already carries once. *(Review notes, 2026-08-31: the report described the creator's two gap cards as "Q-037 and T-399" — those live in beat prose; the cards are the per-section-intent design gap and the coverage miscount, the latter now minted as T-402 alongside T-401 for the banner layout. The "checksummed after every capture run" claim described a manual step as a mechanism — the guard now exists in code: `shot()` hashes every frame and the run fails naming any byte-identical pair. The drift beat's "nothing is written" is likewise now asserted against the document before the restore, not implied by the banner.)*

### Slice Creator 2 — the document creator re-cut

*Built 2026-08-31 → the owner's comment-directed session on the built creator, ruled the same day as three dated addenda to [ADR-0053](../architecture/adr/0053-the-checkers-run-and-the-executor-rule.md). The slice's two open creator defects, T-401 and T-402, built first in the same pass, because T-407's coverage counting had to land on a corrected tally rather than on top of a wrong one.*

**T-401 — A notice with inline children reads as one sentence again.** ✅ **Built 2026-08-31.** *(Minted 2026-08-31 in review, from Session G's capture findings.)* *Plainly: any notice that carries a link or a code — the creator's Q-037 refusal is the worst case — currently renders its words, its code and its link as separate columns, because the shared banner style lays its children out side by side.* `.banner` is `display: flex` with no direction (packages/ui `styles.css`), so every inline child becomes a flex item. Fix at the component so every notice heals at once; the walkthrough's `t1-08` shot photographs the defect and recaptures with the fix. | *(Deps: none)*
  **As built. *Plainly: a notice that carries a link or a code now reads as one sentence, everywhere in the product, because the fix went into the one style every notice shares.*** `.banner` was `display: flex` with no direction, so React's inline children — a word, a `<span class="mono">`, a `<Link>` — each became a flex column. It is now `display: block`: normal text flow, which is what a sentence is. **Two notices genuinely wanted a row** and were the only reason the flex was load-bearing: the dismissible error notices on the cycle and deliverable-status screens pushed their close button right with `margin-left: auto`. They now carry a new `.banner--dismissible` modifier that takes the button out of the sentence's flow and pins it to the corner, so the words still read as words. **Two more notices are better under block than they were under flex** and were quietly broken before: `destination-selector`'s override notice laid its explanation and its control row side by side rather than stacked, and `findings-panel`'s drift notice fragmented on every interpolated count. **Pinned at the source, not on a screen:** a guard in `packages/ui/src/ui.test.tsx` reads `styles.css` and fails if `.banner` ever goes back to flex — the repo's own idiom for a rule that would break silently and still look plausible. ⚠ **Found and deliberately not fixed:** `.banner--warning` is used at nine call sites and **has no CSS rule at all** — every warning notice renders in the neutral tone. *(Review, 2026-08-31: this finding's only home was this closed record, where nobody looks for open work — ticketed as **T-411** on the board.)* That is a second defect in the same file, it is not this ticket, and widening the ticket to take it in would have put an unreviewed tone change into a fix the owner asked for by name. Reported rather than absorbed.

**T-402 — The creator's coverage sentence stops counting a section the document does not have.** ✅ **Built 2026-08-31.** *(Minted 2026-08-31 in review, from Session G's capture findings — flagged on the page itself as a gap card.)* *Plainly: the creator reported "1 of 4 sections written" for a document that came out empty — text arriving before any template heading is filed as "unsectioned", the assembly correctly writes none of it, and the tally counts it as a written section anyway. On the one surface whose whole job is separating a clean result from an unexamined one, the count overstates.* The tally is `new Set(manifest.usedFor).size` (apps/api `document-creation.ts`); `unsectioned` must not count as a template section written, and material that matched no heading should be stated the way the checker states discards. | *(Deps: none)*
  **As built. *Plainly: the creator no longer says a section was written when the document has none — and where the words it drafted actually went is now written on the same line.*** The drafting call files any prose arriving before one of the outline's headings into a bucket called `unsectioned`. The assembly writes the outline's own sections and nothing else, so that bucket never reaches the document — but the tally was `new Set(manifest.usedFor).size`, which had no way of knowing the bucket was not a section. **Three changes, at three grains.** (1) `unsectioned` is now an **exported named constant** in `packages/orchestration/document-builder.ts` rather than a bare string spelled at each site, because the miscount happened at a site that could not have known the string was special. (2) The builder returns **`outsideOutline`** — how many *grounded* sentences matched no heading — alongside `withheld` and `unreachableSources`, the two absences it already reported for the same reason: it is material the run produced and the document does not contain. (3) `coverageAfter` counts sections of the **outline** only, and appends a new clause in **the shape the checker states its discards** — *"3 sentences written outside the outline and left out of the document"*, singular where it is one. **The empty-document case now reads honestly: `0 of 4 sections written · … · 3 sentences written outside the outline and left out of the document`**, where it used to read *1 of 4 sections written* into a document with nothing in it. **Pinned at both grains**: a builder test drives a headingless answer through the whole path and asserts the document comes out empty, `outsideOutline` is above zero, and every manifest entry is the bucket; an API test asserts the sentence's first number equals the count of outline sections in the manifest, so the two can never drift apart again. **No contract change** — coverage crosses the wire as the sentence it has always been, so `DocumentCreationRunResponse` is untouched and there is nothing for `contracts.md` to record. **No migration, no personal data.** The walkthrough's *"Found by this capture"* gap card for this defect closes on the recapture at the end of the slice.

**T-403 — The Tools page becomes cards.** ✅ **Built 2026-08-31.** *Plainly: the Tools page's tiles should look like the cards on the sandbox screen — an icon for each tool, its name, and a short description of what it does.* The description copy already exists under each name (T-334); what changes is the presentation: sandbox-style cards on the design tokens, one icon per tool. The unbuilt/waits-on state (if any tile still carries one) keeps its note inside the card form. **Done when:** each tool renders as a card matching the sandbox's card idiom, with icon and description; a render test pins both; the assembled-not-filtered rule is untouched (an unentitled tool stays absent, never a greyed card). | *(Deps: none)*
  **As built. *Plainly: the Tools page now shows each tool as a card with an icon, its name and a sentence saying what it does — the same kind of card you pick a sandbox from.*** The tiles were `Card` with a bolded name, a paragraph and an *Open* link underneath. They are now a real card grid — `.tool-cards` / `.tool-card` in the kit's stylesheet, built on the sandbox selector's idiom so the two screens read as the same kind of thing to pick from: elevation 3 (design-rules §A's nested-card level), `radius.md`, and §C's stated default grid for a column count nobody has designed, `auto-fill / minmax(260px, 1fr)`. Every spacing value is a multiple of 4. **The whole available card is the link**, so the click target is the card rather than five words at the bottom of it. **The icon is chosen on the surface, not sent over the wire**, and the record should say why: what a tool *is* — its name, its description, whether the viewer may reach it — is the server's to say and does; which glyph sits beside it is presentation, and putting an icon name in `ToolSummary` would make the API answerable for the icon set. **A tool the icon map has never met falls back to a neutral glyph and still renders as a card** — a tile is never dropped for want of a picture — and that fallback is tested rather than assumed. **The assembled-not-filtered rule is untouched and is now pinned rather than trusted**: the card form is more inviting than the row it replaced, and the pull of an even grid is exactly towards rendering an unentitled tool greyed out to fill the gap. There is no `enabled` prop on `ToolCard` to do it with, an unentitled tool still never reaches the component, and the render test asserts an unbuilt card is **not a link at all**. `unbuilt` keeps its badge and its *waits on* note **inside** the card, on a sunken, unshadowed variant that does not pretend to be clickable. **Both of V1's tiles are `available` today**, so the unbuilt state is pinned on a fixture rather than on a live tool — deliberately, because it is the state that would rot unseen. Three render tests, no contract change, no migration.

**T-405 — The source picker says what each document is.** ✅ **Built 2026-08-31.** *Plainly: when picking the library documents a draft may draw on, you currently see too little. Each row should show the document's reference, its title, and a description of what the document is.* Reference and title are **already in the contract** (`GroundingSource.documentReference` / `.title` — verified against [endpoints.ts](../../packages/contracts/src/endpoints.ts)); showing them is a render change. **Description is new**: a nullable `description` column on `containers` (**migration 0062**, drawn in [data-model.md](data-model.md) drawer 2 before writing), **typed by whoever files or edits the document's metadata, never generated** (session residual, Claude-ruled 2026-08-31), surfaced through the metadata modal and carried into `GroundingSource`. Not personal data — it describes a document, not a person. **Done when:** picker rows render reference, title and description; the description is editable where document metadata already is; the e2e seed carries descriptions so the walkthrough can photograph them; migration drawn first, then written. | *(Deps: none)*
  **As built. *Plainly: when you choose the library documents a draft may draw on, each row now says what the document actually is — its reference, its title, and a sentence or two written by whoever filed it.*** **The migration is 0062**, `containers.description`, `text`, nullable — drawn in [data-model.md](data-model.md) drawer 2 before it was written, generated with `drizzle-kit generate` and then read, renamed and given its plain-language header; the drawer's drawing block has folded down to narrative in the same commit, per the state rule. **Reference and title needed no contract change**, as the ticket said; `description` needed one in three places, and the reasoning is in [contracts.md](contracts.md)'s dated note. The one worth restating here: on `patchContainerBody` it is **`.nullable().optional()`, and absent and `null` are different answers** — absent means *"this request is not about the description"*, `null` means *"clear it"*. Without that distinction every metadata edit would silently be a description edit too, and someone who wrote one by mistake would have no way to take it back. All three cases are tested. **Editable where document metadata already is**: the metadata dialog gains a Description section above the authoring fields, saved through the existing `PATCH /containers/:id` under the permission that endpoint already enforces — producing organisation, super-user or the row's live lead author. It renders **only for callers that have one**, so the sandbox freeze-series dialog is untouched. `TextArea` gained a `disabled` prop it had never needed, because nothing had put prose behind a permission before. **One `SourceRow` component serves both tools' pickers — a deliberate widening past the ticket's letter, reported rather than absorbed.** T-405 names the creator's picker; the checker's list is the same control over the same data doing the same job, and two copies is how the two tools end up telling a user different things about one document. **An absent description renders as nothing at all** — not "no description", which would spend a line saying nothing — and the test asserts the absence of that stand-in copy, because most of a real corpus predates the column. **The e2e seed now carries a real description on all eight seeded containers**, so the picker can be read and photographed with sentences in it rather than a column of codes. **Typed, never generated**, in the schema comment, the migration header, the contract and the component — a model-written description would be an uncited claim about a document rendered beside that document's own grounded content. **Not personal data**: it describes a document, and `check:personal-data` is green.

**T-410 — The price line goes.** ✅ **Built 2026-08-31.** *Plainly: the cost estimate shown on the tools' plan pages is not wanted and comes off — both tools.* It was on screen because ADR-0053 §4 ruled it there, so this is **addendum A3** executing, not a defect fix: the visible price (and the "not priced" wording that guarded it against a false £0.00) retires from the creator's and the checker's plan surfaces. **Per-step cost attribution is untouched** — cost stays recorded on Step rows (§7) as an audit and operations fact. **Done when:** neither tool's plan shows a price or a pricing caveat; the tests that pinned the price line invert to assert its absence; step-level cost recording is asserted unchanged. | *(Deps: none)*
  **As built. *Plainly: neither tool's plan page shows a cost any more — not a number, and not the sentence that used to explain why there was no number.*** Both `<p><strong>Estimated cost:</strong>…</p>` blocks are gone, from the creator's plan card and the checker's, along with the *"not priced — this deployment has no rate for the model that would run it"* wording that guarded them against a plausible £0.00. **Where each one stood there is now a comment saying whose ruling took it off**, because the estimate was on screen by a deliberate ADR-0053 §4 decision and a future session reading §4 alone would put it back believing it was fixing a regression. **PER-STEP COST IS UNTOUCHED, AND IS NOW ASSERTED RATHER THAN ASSUMED.** Every Step row still records what it spent (§7); the plan object still computes and carries its estimate; only the display retired. A new API test walks the run's steps, checks each one carries its usage record, and checks the plan still carries `cost` — the half of this ruling nothing else would catch, since a later tidy-up that stripped the estimate from the object or the cost from the row would look like finishing the job while destroying an audit fact. **The two render tests that pinned the price are INVERTED, not deleted.** They asserted that an unpriced deployment said so rather than showing £0.00, and that a real total rendered; the same two cases now assert the absence of `£`, of *not priced*, and of *Estimated cost*. Deleting them would have left the surface free to grow the line back with nothing watching. **The walkthrough's beat text still described the price** — that copy is rewritten in the recapture at the end of the slice, along with the creator's whole section.

**T-406 — The launcher asks Purpose, Language, Style and Type.** ✅ **Built 2026-08-31.** *Plainly: the creator's first screen stops asking for a "shape" and asks four plain questions instead — what kind of document (technical note, planning document, internal document, external document), what language register (technical, non-technical, simple English), which style guide or guides apply, and whether this is a whole document, a chapter or a section.* ADR-0053 **addendum A1** is the ruling; this ticket is its launcher half. *Shape* retires as a term and a control. **Style is the new capability**: the drafting call **consumes the selected style guides and the Language answer** — today `document-builder.ts` reads no style material at all (verified) — with the ruled precedence stated in the plan: *a guide wins on terms and vocabulary; the Language answer wins on register*. **Multiple guides need no migration** — `project_style_guides` already keys many to one project (verified); the launcher lists what is loaded and lets several be selected, and a project with none loaded shows the Style control honestly empty rather than absent. The four answers are run parameters, recorded on the run and in the manifest. **Done when:** the four controls replace shape; the drafting prompt provably carries the selected clauses and the register instruction (asserted, not assumed); the precedence sentence appears in the plan; the launch flow still keeps its state (ADR-0053 §1 — change one answer, keep the rest, the plan regenerates). | *(Deps: T-397)*
  **As built. *Plainly: the creator's first screen no longer asks for a "shape". It asks what kind of document this is, what language it should be written in, which style guides apply, and whether it is a whole document, a chapter or a section — and for the first time the thing that writes the draft is actually shown the project's writing rules.*** **The style half is the substance of this ticket, and it was a real hole.** Project style guides existed only for the *checker* to mark a finished draft against, so the product could tell you that you had broken a rule it had never told the writer about. `composeTemplatePrompt` now takes the selected guides' clauses verbatim with their addresses, a register instruction per Language answer, and a sentence per document Type; the builder reads those clauses from the store itself, narrowed to the ids the author selected. **Reading them in the builder rather than accepting them as text is deliberate and is the mirror of the `sources` rule one line above it**: sources are handed in explicitly so the builder cannot choose what it sees, and clauses are read internally so a caller cannot put words in a guide's mouth. Both are the propagation guarantee, from its two ends. **Asserted, not assumed, at two grains**: eight unit tests on the prompt composer, and a database test that loads two guides, selects one, runs the whole path and reads the system prompt the router was actually handed — the selected guide's clause is in it, the unselected guide's is not, and the register travelled. That second test is the wiring, which is the half that breaks silently while every composer test stays green. **The ruled precedence is one exported constant**, `STYLE_PRECEDENCE`, used by the prompt and by the plan, because A1 requires the plan to *state* it and two copies of a resolution is how two resolutions start. **`ToolPlan` gained `notes`, and it is deliberately not `caveats`** — a caveat is a degradation said before the run button, and diluting that word with a non-degradation would cost it its meaning; the reasoning is in [contracts.md](contracts.md)'s dated note with the rest. **Three states of the Style control, all said out loud**: guides loaded (a checklist — more than one may apply, and the store always allowed it, so no migration); **none loaded**, where the control is *honestly empty* per A1 rather than absent, because a missing control reads as "style is handled"; and **the read failed**, which is a third thing and is pinned by its own test — saying "no style guide is loaded" off a request that did not answer is a claim about the project the screen cannot make. **The workflow went to v2** rather than being edited in place, since a plan records the version it ran. ⚠ **ONE DEVIATION, REPORTED RATHER THAN ABSORBED: the template control survives this ticket as *"Starting outline"*.** *Shape* is retired as a **word and as a control** — it appears nowhere a user can see, which is what the ticket asked. But the select it labelled still has to supply an outline until T-407 builds the define-sections step that absorbs it, and removing it here would have left the tool with nothing to draft into for one commit. It is relabelled, commented as transitional, and T-407 moves it. **The `documentType` field is named that and not `type`** — `type` collides with too much to be a good field name at this depth. **No migration, no personal data.**

**T-407 — The outline is composed: define sections.** ✅ **Built 2026-08-31.** *Plainly: after the four characteristics, the author builds the document's outline — add a section, say what it should include ("an introductory section setting out X, Y and Z"), add the next — instead of the outline arriving ready-made from a template.* This is T-335's own spec ("compose the outline, state the intent for each section") coming back through the front door — the walkthrough has carried it as a *designed, not yet surfaced* gap card since T-400 — **as re-cut by addendum A1**: sections carry a purpose each, and **source binding stays whole-document** (the per-section binding half of the old spec is superseded, so the gap card closes to this design). The two shipped templates survive as **optional starting outlines**: choosing one pre-fills sections whose purposes are the template's per-part guidance, all editable, all removable. Section definitions are run parameters. The T-336 finding about heading shapes applies: the assembly must write into sections as people actually head them, not only as `document_builder` writes them. **Done when:** sections can be added, reordered, edited and removed, each with its stated purpose; a template seeds but never locks the outline; the manifest records the sections; the coverage statement counts these sections (which is where T-402's fix must hold). | *(Deps: T-402, T-406)*
  **As built. *Plainly: the author now builds the document's outline — add a section, say what should go in it, add the next, move them around, take one out — instead of picking a ready-made shape. A template can still be chosen to start from, and everything it puts on screen is then yours to change or delete.*** T-335's own spec, back through the front door as A1 re-cut it. **The outline is the author's all the way down**: `documentCreationBody` lost `templateId` and gained `sections`, the builder lost its template lookup, and the planner takes the composed list. A starting outline is a **menu**, served by a new `GET …/starting-outlines`, whose per-part guidance becomes the pre-filled section purposes — leaving `templateId` beside `sections` would have left two answers to one question. **The composer starts EMPTY, deliberately**, and its test says so: a helpfully pre-filled outline is a shape arriving ready-made wearing a new name, which is the thing A1 retired. **A purpose says what belongs in a section and never what to conclude** — the rule the shipped templates' authoring guide always held their guidance to, now on screen in the composer's own copy, because the words became the author's and the rule did not stop mattering. ⚠ **T-336's heading finding, applied, and it is bigger than it looks.** The checker's splitter GUESSES at an unmarked heading: short, unpunctuated, blank line above. Those were safe guesses while every heading came from one of two templates. An author types *"3.2 Baseline conditions, including the 2025 survey."* and every one of them fails, so a section the creator wrote becomes prose the checker never sees as a section. **The assembly now writes headings as markdown `##`**, which `ATX` matches unconditionally whatever the length or punctuation, and which the editor renders as the heading it is. A test drives exactly that long, full-stopped heading through. **Heading matching was normalising only one side** — the model's line was stripped of hashes and trailing punctuation while the outline's own heading was compared raw — which was invisible while headings came from templates and would have silently orphaned any author heading ending in a full stop. One `asHeading` now normalises both. **Sections are identified by POSITION, not by heading**, because an author may honestly write "Mitigation" twice; a repeated heading resolves to its **first** position and the count is of sections rather than of names. **T-402's tally moved to where it belongs** as a consequence: `sectionsWritten` is now counted by the builder, beside the assembly that decides it, rather than derived downstream from the manifest — a count off the manifest's headings would under-report duplicates, which is the same class of error as T-402's over-report, the other way round. `usedFor` is now the section's **heading**, because a manifest is read by people and *"the evidence"* says what a source was used for where `s1` does not. **🛑 STOP-AND-REPORT ITEM, HANDLED WITHOUT THE WIDENING.** A workflow parameter's declared type is one of `string | number | boolean | id | id_list` — a fixed union — and an outline is a list of objects. Rather than widen it, the outline crosses as a **JSON string parsed by a narrowing helper in the capability registry**, which is precisely the shape `families` already takes in `qa-check.yaml` and precisely what `familiesOf` already does with it *(review correction, 2026-08-31: not precisely — `families` is a comma-separated list of scalar names, this is JSON-encoded objects; the **class** of workaround is the shipped one, the serialization is new)*. It works, it follows a shipped idiom, and it is one line from becoming `object_list` if the owner rules that way. **The recommendation is in the session report.** **No migration, no personal data.** The walkthrough's *"per-section intent, and sources bound per section"* gap card closes to this design on the recapture — **source binding stays whole-document** per A1, so the card's other half is superseded rather than built.

**T-408 — The plan becomes the proposed document.** ✅ **Built 2026-08-31.** *Plainly: the plan page sets out the document about to be written — a short overview of the overarching instructions, then, section by section, a short description of what will be written into each — and the author can click any section and correct its description directly before accepting. A chip at the bottom accepts the plan and creates the document.* ADR-0053 **addendum A2** is the ruling: what the author edits is the **brief — a parameter**; the step list underneath stays computed in code, never editable, and regenerates when a brief changes, so the run stays `declared` and §12 stays closed. Editing a section's description keeps every other answer (the launch-keeps-its-state rule, one step deeper). The coverage statement stays, in its same two-shape form; the price line is gone (T-410). **Done when:** the plan renders overview + per-section briefs computed from the launcher answers and section definitions; direct edit of one brief regenerates the plan without touching the others; the accept chip runs the workflow; a test asserts the same parameters produce the same plan twice (the T-336 determinism pattern, on this surface). | *(Deps: T-407, T-410)*
  **As built. *Plainly: the plan page stopped being a list of machinery and became the document you are about to get — a short overview of the instructions, then section by section what will be written into each. Anything wrong, you click and correct it there, and the page redraws. A chip at the bottom accepts it and creates the document.*** **The design's whole weight is on where the editable thing lives, and it lives on the parameter.** `DocumentSection` gained an optional `brief`, in the request body, beside every other answer; correcting one asks the server for a **new plan computed from the new inputs**. Had `brief` been a field on the plan object, correcting it would have meant editing a plan — the run would have stopped being `declared` and ADR-0053 §12 would have reopened. **The step list stays on the page** rather than being hidden behind the prospectus: a page showing only the pretty half would be a page that stopped saying what the machine will actually do. It is rendered, editable by nobody, and regenerates from the new brief — pinned by a planner test that edits a brief and asserts `steps` come out **identical**, which is §4's guarantee surviving A2 rather than being traded for it. **A correction the plan showed and the draft ignored would be the worst of both**, so `composeDraftingPrompt` now takes `section.brief ?? section.purpose`: the author's words win where they gave any, and where they did not the purpose stands rather than the planner's computed description, which is that same purpose plus register-and-grounding boilerplate the prompt already carries. **Editing one description leaves every other alone** — the launch-keeps-its-state rule one step deeper — and that is asserted both ways: the untouched section's brief comes back byte-identical, and its `edited` flag stays false. **`edited` is on the wire deliberately**: a page that has been corrected must not read as one the planner wrote, so a corrected section wears a *Your wording* badge. **Four render tests, and the negative ones are the point**: exactly two editable controls for two briefs and none for any step, *"are not editable"* on the page, and no `Edit step` anywhere. **The accept control is a chip**, as the ticket asked, and a refusal **replaces** it rather than sitting beside it (§5). The price line stayed gone (T-410) and the coverage statement stayed in its same two-shape form. **No migration, no personal data.**

**T-409 — The agent pane: correct the plan by saying so.** ✅ **Built 2026-08-31.** *Plainly: beside the plan, a pane where the author can tell an agent what it got wrong for a section — "no, this should set out X in bullets" — and the agent revises that section's description in the plan.* ADR-0053 **addendum A2**'s second half: the agent **edits the brief and only the brief** — a parameter — and the plan regenerates in code, so the model never touches the step list and the run stays `declared`. Reached per section (a chip on each section opens the pane targeted at it). The agent's calls route on the existing task classes and are entitlement-checked like any capability; its turns land in the run record's existing shape. **No new named-person data** — the pane stores nothing about a person the run record does not already hold. **Done when:** a per-section chip opens the pane; a prompt revises that section's brief and the plan regenerates with every other section untouched; a test asserts the step list after an agent tweak is byte-identical to the step list after the same brief edited by hand — the two doors produce one plan. | *(Deps: T-408)*
  **As built. *Plainly: each section on the plan page now has an "Ask the agent" chip. Press it and a small pane opens under that section; say what is wrong — "no, this should set out the three constraints in bullets" — and the agent rewrites that one description. Nothing runs, and you still have to accept the plan.*** **The design's whole safety is that there is ONE DOOR, and it is structural rather than remembered.** The agent's revised text is handed back to the surface, which puts it through **`editBrief` — the very function a typed correction uses** — and the plan is recomputed in code. There is no second path a future edit could add without deleting the first. The planner test that closes the ticket asserts exactly that: an agent tweak and a hand edit of the same brief produce one plan, `steps` compared byte for byte. *(Review correction, 2026-08-31: that planner test compared two identical object literals — it could not fail, whatever the agent path did, because at the planner there is no such thing as a door. Deleted, and replaced with a test that walks the real doors: the agent endpoint answers with the model's actual reply through the actual parse, the returned brief goes to the plan endpoint, the same words typed by hand go to it separately, and the two plans are asserted byte-identical — `document-creation.test.ts`, T-409.)* The model never sees a step list, let alone edits one, so the run stays `declared` and ADR-0053 §12 stays closed. **The third embedded assistive agent, and the narrowest.** It follows T-337's and T-364's preview-confirm lane — it **proposes and never applies** — and it reads **no project material at all**: not a source, not a document, not the library. That is narrower than the structure agent, which at least reads its organisation's plan disciplines, and it is narrower on purpose: a description of what a section will contain is an *instruction*, and an agent that reached into the record to write one would be drafting the document a step early — ungrounded, uncited, and in the one field that then steers the grounded call. **Reached per section**, because an agent told *"the second one is wrong"* about a whole plan is an agent guessing which one. **Entitlement-checked like the tool it belongs to, and absent rather than refused**: a requester whose assembled set carries no `document_builder` gets `404`, the same answer the creator itself gives them, because a pane that returned `403` would tell someone a tool exists that they were never shown. **Routed on the existing `draft` task class** — no new class, no new step type, nothing widened. **Six parser tests, and every one is a way the model comes back wrong**: unparseable, empty, fenced, a question instead of an answer, both at once, and the one worth naming separately — **an answer that drafted the section instead of describing it**, capped at 600 characters and returned as a question the author can act on. A 4,000-character "description" reaching the drafting prompt would be a draft written by a model that had not seen a single source. ⚠ **ONE READING FLAGGED RATHER THAN ASSUMED.** The ticket's prose says the agent's *"turns land in the run record's existing shape"*. There is **no run at plan time** — the run is created when the plan is accepted — and the two agents already shipped in this lane (T-337, T-364) record nothing, since ADR-0027's S10 amendment reserves `agent_acts` for agents that *execute directly*, which this one does not. So **no run and no agent act is written**, and no new record shape was invented, which is the reading the ticket's own **Done when** clause supports (it names the chip, the revision, the untouched sections and the two-doors test, and no record). Reported rather than silently decided. **No new named-person data** — the pane stores nothing at all. **No migration.**

**T-404 — The creator meets the design system.** ✅ **Built 2026-08-31.** *Plainly: the owner found the creator's screens cramped. Audit every creator screen against the design rulebook and re-lay them out to it.* Runs **last** in the slice, over the re-cut surface T-406–T-409 produce, so nothing is restyled twice. The audit is against [design-rules.md](../design/design-rules.md) and the tokens — spacing, type scale, measure, grouping — and its findings are listed in the closing commit so the fix is checkable against a list rather than a feeling. **Done when:** the creator's screens follow the design rulebook and the commit names what was out of line; the walkthrough recaptures the tool's section. | *(Deps: T-406, T-407, T-408, T-409)*
  **As built. *Plainly: the owner said the creator's screens were cramped, and they were — the cards had no padding and no gap between them, so the form sat flush against the card edges. That is fixed at the component, so every card in the product healed at once.*** **THE AUDIT, AS A LIST, so the fix is checkable against it rather than against a feeling.**

  1. 🔴 **`.card` had no padding and no gutter, and that is the whole of "cramped".** The rule set a background, a radius and a shadow and stopped. `--card-padding` (16px) and design-rules §C's 12px gutter both exist in the token set and neither had ever reached it. **Every other screen that noticed had compensated inline**: settings seven times, login, cycle and workspace once each, all with a hand-written `padding: 16` — the §A hard rule (*"never hardcode a raw px value in app code"*) broken at ten call sites with the same value re-decided at each. The creator's cards wrap **form fields** rather than a padded table, so they had nothing to hide behind. Fixed at `.card`; the ten compensating wrappers removed, because leaving them would have double-padded four screens I had not been asked to change.
  2. 🔴 **No vertical rhythm inside a card.** `.field` sets 4px between a label and its input and **nothing between one field and the next**, so the launcher's four questions ran together as one block. New `.card-stack` (12px, §A `gap.loose`), decided once.
  3. 🟠 **Card headings were bare `<strong>`** — body size, no hierarchy against the field labels beneath them. New `.card-title`. Two cards had no heading at all; both now say what they are (*"What this document is"*, *"The brief, and where it goes"*).
  4. 🟠 **Muted paragraphs written as inline `style={{ color: 'var(--text-muted)' }}` at eight sites** — a token reference, but layout re-decided per call. New `.card-lede`, and `text-secondary` rather than `text-muted`: §D measures `text.muted` at 4.53:1, which passes AA and is the wrong choice for a sentence that is not an aside.
  5. 🟠 **The plan's step list was an unstyled `<ul>`** — browser furniture inside a designed card. New `.plan-steps`. The coverage sentence and the notes ran into it as one undifferentiated block; both now carry their own margin.
  6. 🟠 **The page's one primary action was its faintest control.** The accept control is a chip because the owner asked for a chip by name, and `Chip` had one tone — `warning`. §A reserves the near-black accent for a primary action, so `Chip` gained `tone="primary"` and wears it.
  7. 🟡 **The outline's section controls stacked down the left of a two-field group**, leaving the remove button floating beside a textarea it does not act on. Number, heading and controls now read as one row, with the purpose beneath.

  🐛 **AND ONE DEFECT THE AUDIT FOUND THAT IS NOT A DESIGN DEFECT AT ALL, FIXED HERE RATHER THAN LEFT.** The run body's section mapping dropped `brief`. It was written in T-407 before briefs existed and kept dropping them after T-408 added them, because the *plan* path passes its own sections and only the *run* path goes through that mapping — so **the plan showed a correction and the document would have been drafted without it**. Every test passed either side of it: the planner tests exercise the plan, the prompt tests take sections directly. It was found by reading the surface for a layout audit. Reported loudly because a silent fix inside a design ticket is exactly how a defect like this stops being visible. 🔴 *(Review, 2026-08-31: this fix closed only HALF the drop, and the record's own warning applied to the fix itself. The client now sent `brief` with the run body — but the server's step-input parser (`sectionsOf`, `capability-registry.ts`) stripped it again while narrowing the parsed JSON, so the run path still drafted without the author's correction, and nothing tested it. Completed in review: the parser preserves a real brief, and the closing test sits at the far end of the pipe — the author's corrected words asserted present in the prompt the model actually received, over HTTP, verified to fail without the fix.)*

  🐛 **AND A SECOND DEFECT, IN THE CAPTURE RECIPE ITSELF, FOUND BY RUNNING IT.** `shots/` is gitignored and the capture never emptied it, so it accumulates across runs — and when a beat is **renamed**, its old file stays behind. The recipe's downscale step copies `shots/*.png` wholesale, so **six screenshots of the creator as it was before this slice re-cut it** were copied into the committed folder beside their replacements, unreferenced by the page and invisible in a diff of 12,000 lines. The duplicate-shot guard could not catch it: it checksums the frames a run **wrote**, not the directory it wrote them into. `capture.mjs` now empties `shots/` before it starts, which is the only place the two can be made the same set, and the six stale files are deleted.

  *(Review note, 2026-08-31 — a substrate change this record did not mention.)* The same commit taught `apps/api/src/e2e-server.ts` two new fake-router behaviours: a canned agent-revision reply for T-409's pane, and a drafting reply that reads the outline's headings off the prompt and answers **under them** — which is what turned the capture's coverage line from an empty document into *"3 of 3 sections written"*. The in-file comments are honest about why, and the change is right (a substrate that cannot follow a heading cannot photograph the creator working); it is recorded here because the walkthrough's result beat presents that number as the product's behaviour, and a reader auditing the capture should know the stand-in was taught to cooperate the same day.

  **Rendered and looked at, not reasoned about from tokens** (§G.1): the walkthrough's full capture ran on a fresh seed, the creator's fourteen shots were read back, and items 6 and 7 above were found **in the photographs** after the token-level pass was already green — which is what §G exists to catch. ⚠ **Deviation, reported: this ticket changed four screens outside the creator.** Fixing `.card` at the component is where the rulebook says the fix belongs, and it forced the removal of the ten inline paddings that had been compensating for its absence; leaving them would have shipped four double-padded screens. Settings, login, cycle and workspace are those four, and none of them changed in any other way.

**T-411 — Warning notices get their warning tone.** ✅ **Built 2026-08-31.** *(Minted 2026-08-31 in review, from T-401's own reported-not-fixed finding, which until this ticket lived only in a closed record where nobody looks for open work.)* *Plainly: nine notices in the product are written as warnings — the checker's weaker-coverage caveat among them — and render in the same neutral grey as an ordinary remark, because the shared notice style has success and error tones and no warning tone at all.* `.banner--warning` does not exist in `packages/ui/src/styles.css` (only `--success`, `--error`, `--dismissible`) and is used at nine call sites across `destination-selector.tsx`, `findings-panel.tsx` and `tools.tsx`. Fix at the component, on the tokens, so all nine heal at once — T-401's own pattern, one tone along. **Done when:** the warning tone exists and is visibly distinct from neutral and from error in both themes; a render test pins it the way T-401's pins the block layout; any recaptured shot that shows one is checked rather than assumed. | *(Deps: none)*
  **As built. *Plainly: a notice written as a warning now looks like one — a warm amber left edge and a pale amber background, instead of the same neutral grey an ordinary remark gets. All nine healed from one rule; not one of the nine call sites was touched.*** **The whole ticket is one CSS rule and three token values**, which is the point: `.banner--warning` did not exist, so nine notices asking for a tone were silently served the default. **The rule is built on `feedback.warning`, the design system's own name for this tone, not on the older `--amber` pair its two neighbours (`--success`, `--error`) still use.** Those two sets resolve to the *same* values in light mode (`#8a5a12` / `#f8efdd`), so there is no visual seam between the three tones — but writing a new rule onto the deprecated set would have added debt the tokens file exists to retire. **`feedback.warning` carried light values only**, where success and danger both carried light and dark, so a dark-mode warning would have painted a dark brown on a dark panel. `amberDark` was added to [design-tokens.json](../design/design-tokens.json) (`500` `#b8862f`, `600` `#d1a04e`, `tint` `#322a1a` — the `600`/`tint` pair are the values the old set's dark block already shipped, so dark mode gains no new colour, only a name for one it was already using) and `feedback.warning.{text,dot,tint}` gained their `dark` halves; `packages/ui/scripts/build-tokens.ts` regenerated `tokens.ts` and `tokens.generated.css`. This is design-rules **§F.6** — a feedback colour must carry light *and* dark — being satisfied rather than a sixth hue being invented; the closed set of five is untouched. **A side effect wider than the nine notices, and a strict improvement: every other dark-mode surface already reading `--feedback-warning-text` was painting `#8a5a12` on a dark panel** — the `.b-warning` status badge, the citation-footer's withheld and open-world markers, the skipped/pending run states. All of them were near-illegible in dark mode and are now legible. Nothing in light mode changed anywhere. **Four render tests** pin the rule at its single source the way T-401's pin the block layout: that it exists at all (its absence being the entire defect), that it is toned from the token and contains no raw hex, that it lands somewhere different from both the neutral notice and the error tone, and that the dark block resolves — the last because the regeneration is mechanical and a future token edit could drop the dark half again in silence. **`.claude/skills/infora-design/` was deliberately not touched**: it is a mirrored kit, not an authority, and it carries no dark block at all, so it is not out of step with anything. **No DesignSync push** — repo-side only. **No migration, no personal data, no contract change.**
  *(Review corrections, 2026-08-31 — three claims in this record did not survive verification, none affecting the build's correctness.)* (1) **The kit claim is wrong**: `.claude/skills/infora-design/tokens/dark.css` is a full 53-line dark remap whose own header promises every semantic token a counterpart — amber was the one missing, so the kit WAS shipping exactly the defect this ticket fixed. The amber dark values were added to the kit in review; the next DesignSync pass should carry them to the design project. (2) **"Dark mode gains no new colour" overreaches**: the `600` and `tint` dark values were indeed already shipped in `styles.css`, but `amberDark.500 = #b8862f` existed nowhere at base — the dot colour is new. (3) The pre-fix state was not "the same neutral grey" — the base `.banner` paints a **green** `--accent` left border, which is worse: a warning was dressed as a success. Also in review: the distinctness test asserted token *names* only and would have survived a token retargeted to the danger colour — a value-level test over both theme blocks was added beside it, along with the missing `--feedback-warning-dot` dark assertion; and the count is four new render tests, not three.

## Slice Tools 2 — the second tools feedback pass *(minted 2026-09-01; building from 2026-09-01)*

*The owner's second render review of both built tools, ruled the same day as [ADR-0053](../architecture/adr/0053-the-checkers-run-and-the-executor-rule.md) addenda A4–A5; session record in [grill-history.md](../grill-sessions/grill-history.md). Records move here ticket by ticket as they close, per the standing convention.*

**T-412 — A section can carry sub-sections.** ✅ **Built 2026-09-01.** *Plainly: when composing the outline, an "add sub-section" under any section creates a nested part that becomes its own separately-drafted piece of the document.* One level of nesting in V1. This is not only a form control: the splitter, the manifest, the coverage count and the drafting prompt all have to know a sub-section is a section of its own with a parent — the coverage sentence counts what the outline holds, at whatever depth. **Done when:** sub-sections can be added, edited, reordered within their parent and removed; the drafted document carries them under their parent's heading; the manifest and both coverage sentences count them honestly; the T-408 determinism test still holds over a nested outline. | *(Deps: none)*

  **As built. *Plainly: a section can now carry sub-sections, and the document carries them under their parent's heading.*** Under every section in the outline step there is now an **Add a sub-section** button; a sub-section gets its own heading, its own "what should go in it", and its own move-up / move-down / remove controls. It is numbered `2.1`, `2.2` — the decimal numbering every engineering document already uses, so the nesting needs no explaining. The finished document carries it as a `###` heading under its parent's `##`.

  **One level, and the TYPE is what enforces it rather than a rule somebody has to remember.** `DocumentSubSection` is a separate type from `DocumentSection` and carries no nesting of its own, so there is no site in the codebase that *could* read a second level. A recursive type would have made "one level" a check at every reader, and the first reader to forget would have produced a document with a depth the splitter, the manifest and the coverage count were never written for. The wire schema matches: `documentSubSectionBody` declares no `subSections`, so a request carrying two levels is honoured to the depth V1 has rather than rejected outright — and a sub-section with no heading or no purpose is refused exactly as a section is.

  🔒 **ONE TRAVERSAL, AND EVERYTHING COUNTS THROUGH IT.** `flattenOutline` in `packages/contracts/src/creator.ts` reads an outline flat, parents before their children — which is also the order the document carries. The splitter, the manifest, the assembly, both coverage sentences, the plan's proposed document, the prompt's numbered list and the surface's own readiness check all read that one function. **A second traversal written somewhere else is how two counts of one outline start disagreeing**, and this ticket is nothing but that risk in six places at once: the outline that leaves the browser, the parser that reads it back off the persisted step input, the prompt, the splitter, the manifest and the assembly. The end-to-end test in `apps/api/src/document-creation.test.ts` asserts the whole chain over HTTP for exactly the reason T-408's own record gives — six of those could pass a unit test each while the document came out flat.

  **A parent heading is written when it hosts a surviving sub-section, and is still not counted as written.** Those are two separate facts and both had to be got right. If a section survived nothing of its own but one of its sub-sections did, its heading is still written — otherwise the `###` would float under whatever section came before it, which is a document saying something nobody wrote. But it does **not** join the `sectionsWritten` tally, because nothing was written into it: that is T-402's discipline held one level down, where a bucket that was not a section was once counted as one.

  **The manifest names a sub-section under its parent** — *"The evidence — Trial pits"*, not *"Trial pits"*. A manifest is read by people, and a sub-section heading on its own is one that three sections of a long outline could share; an entry a reader cannot locate in the document is not a manifest entry. Sections are still keyed by **position**, now flattened position, so two parts that honestly share a heading stay two parts.

  **The corrected description still has exactly one door, at either depth.** The plan's proposed document is a flat list, so a correction arrives as a flat index; `withBriefAt` turns that back into a nested outline. The agent pane (T-409) goes through the same function a typed correction does, which is what A2's guarantee rests on — two doors would be two chances to produce different plans. `withBriefAt` **removes** the key rather than setting it to `undefined`, because absent is a meaning here ("the planner's own description stands") and a key holding `undefined` compares as present.

  **Deviations and things reported rather than absorbed.** ⚠ **`ProposedDocument.sections` gained a `depth` field** — a contract change, noted in [contracts.md](contracts.md). The plan page is the prospectus of the document you are about to get, so an outline that read flat there and came out nested would be describing a different document; sending the depth is cheaper and more honest than making the surface re-derive it from a list it did not build. ⚠ **`coverageAfter`'s `sectionsPlanned` was reading the unflattened count at the API**, which produced *"4 of 2 sections written"* — the after-sentence contradicting the before-sentence about the same outline. Found by the end-to-end test, fixed in `apps/api/src/document-creation.ts`. ⚠ **The planner's computed description for a sub-section now says whose it is** (*"It sits under 'The evidence'."*): a purpose written knowing what sat above it, read back on its own, reads as a section that wandered off the outline. **No migration, no personal data, no new union or parameter type** — the outline still travels as T-407's serialized string and `sectionsOf` reads the sub-sections back off it, dropping a deeper level exactly as it drops an unnamed section.


**T-413 — The creator starts from a working-area location, and never from the plan.** ✅ **Built 2026-09-01.** *Plainly: in your working area, a location gains "create a document here" — the creator opens with the destination already set to that location. And the door that offered to start the creator from a deliverable in the owner's plan is removed, because the owner ruled it should not be possible.* ADR-0053 **addendum A4** is the ruling; `Q-037` closed on it. **Done when:** the sandbox route opens the same launcher (one launcher, ADR-0053 §1) with the destination pre-filled and changeable; the `?containerId=` bound-path refusal and every doorway to it are gone, its render test inverting to assert the absence; nothing anywhere reads a plan row into the creator. | *(Deps: none)*

  **As built. *Plainly: the working area now offers "Create with AI", which opens the creator with the destination already set to where you were standing — and the screen that used to appear when you arrived from a deliverable in the plan is gone, because the owner ruled that arrival should not be possible.*** The sandbox toolbar gains **Create with AI** beside *New document*, visible once a sandbox is selected; it navigates to the same creator route with `?sandboxId=`, and the destination select opens on that location with a line under it saying so. It stays changeable — **one launcher** (ADR-0053 §1), starting on a different answer, not a second screen with a fixed one. A pre-filled control the user did not set and is not told about is one they read as their own choice, which is why the sentence is there.

  🔒 **THE DOORWAY CARRIES THE LOCATION AND NOTHING ELSE.** No deliverable, no title, no reference. The ruling cut the plan→creator link rather than deciding what may cross it, so a doorway that helpfully passed a plan row's facts along would re-open at the back exactly what was closed at the front — and would walk into `Q-034`'s wall-through-content territory that A4 exists to keep out of.

  🔒 **AND THE PRE-FILL READS THE ASSEMBLED LIST, NEVER THE PARAMETER.** A `sandboxId` the requester cannot reach is absent from their own sandbox list, so it fills nothing and the select stays on *"Choose a working area…"*. Trusting the URL instead would let a hand-typed id appear on screen that the requester was never shown — a surface answering *"does this exist"*, which is the question deny-as-404 exists to refuse. This is the assembled-not-filtered rule one control along.

  **The render test INVERTED rather than being deleted** *(review correction, 2026-09-01: no such test existed at the base — the base suite never pinned the refusal's presence, so nothing was inverted; the five absence assertions are new, which is the right outcome under a false provenance)*, which is T-410's own argument one ruling along: a test that was simply removed would leave the screen free to grow the doorway back with nothing noticing. Five assertions now pin the absence — the refusal copy is gone, `params.get('containerId')` and `boundContainerId` appear nowhere, the pre-fill exists and stays changeable, the pre-fill goes through the assembled list, and the sandbox's doorway carries only `?sandboxId=`. One assertion had to be narrowed in the writing: the file still contains the string `Q-037`, in the comment above the removal that records **why** the screen went, so the test asserts the user-facing copy is gone rather than the number. That is the record doing its job; the screen is what had to stop naming an open question at a user.

  ⚠ **Deviations, reported: three things outside `tools.tsx` changed, and all three had to.** (1) [component-8-surfaces.md](../architecture/components/component-8-surfaces.md) carried the refusal as a live standing property of the surface — it now states the ruling and the two front doors instead, because a component doc describing a screen that no longer exists is worse than no paragraph. (2) The walkthrough's **capture recipe** photographed the refusal as beat `t1-14-bound-refusal`; the step now clicks *Create with AI* and photographs the working-area launch as `t1-14-from-the-working-area`. (3) The walkthrough's **beat prose** was rewritten to match, and says plainly that this beat replaced a refusal and why. **The page itself is not recaptured here** — the recapture is T-420's, sequenced last over the whole slice so nothing is photographed twice, so the published walkthrough still shows the old shot until then. **No migration, no personal data, no contract change.**


**T-414 — A composed outline saves as a starting outline** (migration **0063**). ✅ **Built 2026-09-01.** *Plainly: having built an outline you like, save it — next time it appears beside the shipped starting outlines, for your firm only, marked as yours.* ADR-0053 **addendum A5** is the ruling: the word is *starting outline*, the store is **org-private** (firm know-how, the rulebook's scoping), **anyone in the firm saves**, saved outlines render **visibly as the firm's own** beside the Infora-shipped ones, and **a curator may delete one** (currency by state — retired, never a deleted row). **A named person rides this ticket:** who saved an outline is stored and registered in [personal-data.md](../architecture/personal-data.md) same-commit, the style-guide loader's precedent. **Done when:** save from the outline step (sub-sections included); the outline step lists shipped and firm outlines with the firm's marked; curator delete works and a retired outline stops being offered while documents already made from it are untouched; another organisation's member never sees it (asserted, not assumed). | *(Deps: T-412)*

  **As built. *Plainly: an outline you built can now be kept for your firm — it appears beside the ones Infora ships, marked "Your firm", and only your firm ever sees it.*** Under the outline step there is a **Save this outline for your firm** control: name it, save it, and it joins the *Start from:* row with a **Your firm** badge beside its name. Choosing it is a copy exactly as choosing a shipped one is — A1's *seeds but never locks* is untouched. **Sub-sections ride** (T-412): the whole point of saving an outline is saving the one you actually built, and an outline saved flatter than it was built would be worse than none.

  **Migration 0063, drawn in [data-model.md](data-model.md) drawer 7 before it was written**, generated by drizzle-kit against the current snapshot and read before applying; the file was renamed from drizzle's own `0063_material_veda` to `0063_starting-outlines` (journal updated with it) and carries its reasoning header and a hand-added `GRANT`, as every migration here does. The drawer's field list has folded to narrative per the state rule, since the drawer is now built.

  🔒 **`organisation_id` IS THE ONLY SCOPE KEY, AND IT COMES OFF THE RESOLVED SESSION.** No project column, no wall predicate — how a firm structures its documents is firm know-how that travels to every project it touches (ADR-0020, the rulebook's own argument). The `projectId` in the route exists for the entitlement check and touches the query nowhere. **`sections` is jsonb rather than rows**, and that is the opposite decision from `rulebook_clauses` for a stated reason: a starting outline is a seed for a form, never quoted and never cited, where a clause is rows precisely because a finding quotes it verbatim and must resolve to the words it quoted.

  **The tiers are A5's, and they are two different tiers on purpose.** **Anyone in the firm saves** — there is no permission check on the save route or the save control, and adding one would re-rule the addendum. **Only a curator retires**, and the curator is the rulebook's tier (`orgRole === 'admin'`), because this is the firm's own material curated at account level with no project seat to check against. The retire control is **absent** for anyone else rather than rendered and disabled — the assembled-not-filtered rule at a button — which is why `mayRetire` is an optional field the server sets rather than something the surface works out.

  **The wall assertion is the one worth having written.** *"Somebody off the project sees nothing"* is true of every route in this app and proves nothing about this store, so the suite gained a new subject: **an admin of a second organisation that is a member of the same project**. They pass the entitlement check, reach the same route, and get the shipped menu with none of the firm's rows in it. Also asserted: an ordinary member saves successfully; the same member's retire answers 404 (nonexistence, not a refusal — principle 4 and the org wall at once); retiring twice is nonexistence the second time; the row survives retirement with `retired_at` set; and **a document made from an outline is untouched when that outline is retired** — which is true by construction, since a chosen outline is copied into the request and no document has ever referenced the row.

  **Deviations and choices worth naming.** ⚠ **A firm outline's description is computed, not typed and never generated** — *"3 sections, saved by Cal."* The description's job on this menu is to let a colleague choose between two outlines, and what settles that is its size and whose judgement it is; asking the saver for a description would be asking for a second label, and asking a model would be an uncited claim about somebody's work. ⚠ **`StartingOutline` gained `origin`, `savedBy`, `savedAt` and `mayRetire`** — a contract change, noted in [contracts.md](contracts.md); `origin` is required on both kinds rather than optional on one, so a reader can never mistake an absent field for a shipped outline. ⚠ **The name of the person who saved an outline is shown on the menu**, which is why the register entry says the name is held for two reasons and both are the feature. **No new union or parameter type; no change to the run path.**


**T-415 — The checker's launcher: tick a check, see its options.** ✅ **Built 2026-09-01.** *Plainly: each check gets a tick-box, and ticking it unfolds that check's own settings beneath it — so "how hard to look" appears under the accuracy check, where it always belonged, and ticking style shows which style guides will be applied.* ADR-0053 §2 always ruled depth a property of the corpus check alone; the shipped global control was a build error, confirmed against the code in session Cr2.
