Registered in review with the position that a row's erasure does not reach into a past export, exactly as it cannot reach the copy on the exporter's laptop — flagged for the DPA and for the owner. **(3) Two boundary gaps closed, each with a test:** a well-formed screen naming a column its table never declared passed the definition PATCH and only failed later at render (the schema alone cannot know the tables; the route now checks against the store), and a retired table's acceptance setting could still be flipped (now the same 404 as absence). **(4) Honesty notes on the build's own proof, kept here so nobody re-reads the tests optimistically:** the source-rules fence has three tests that prove it fires and two that prove it fires narrowly, not five positive proofs; the no-author test on the export reads the workbook's cells, not its raw bytes — safe today because the writer emits no metadata part at all; the two required agent questions are computed and shown client-side, and nothing server-side refuses a publish while they stand unanswered — the guiding duty as ruled is to ask, not to block, so this is as designed but worth the sentence; and the Word-on-insight-tables-only offer is the screen's, the route accepting any readable row as Word. **(5) Unreported but examined and kept:** the builder's three-column styling layer in `packages/ui/src/styles.css`; the e2e fake router's new screen-writing branch in `e2e-server.ts` (other suites unaffected — the callback shape already took both arguments); the app page's new Screens section rendering published interfaces, with its route. **(6) A limitation for T-443 to lift, stated nowhere by the build:** the stepped builder's table step declares `data` tables only — no `insight` or `reference` kind can be declared through the steps, and T-443's insight needs one.

*Review note, 2026-09-07 (the co-captain pass on the app substrate, T-439–T-441). Five things were found and fixed in the review commit, each marked in place in the file that carries it.* **(1) One line of T-440's done-when was not built:** *"revoking B's membership leaves B's accepted rows readable to the owner and its unaccepted rows dark"* had no code behind it — a departed firm's submitted rows still read. The predicate gained the fact (ADR-0056 §7's split: only what was accepted changed hands), the routes feed it, and a test drives the firm off the project and reads both ways. **(2) Starting a run answered with the app owner's name where reading it back answered with the runner's** — the stored record was right, the receipt was wrong; fixed, with a test. **(3) Reassignment accepted a recipient from any firm on the project** — a third firm's person could be handed another firm's app. Narrowed to the app's own firm and the project owner's people, with a worded refusal and a test; the owner is asked to confirm this scope in the review report. **(4) The test that says the DATABASE refuses a rejection without a reason was actually tripping a different constraint** (the null decider pair), so the rejection-reason rule was never proved at the store; the test now fills the decider in properly and pins the exact constraint name. **(5) Small record corrections:** migration 0067's header said six CHECKs and six triggers where there are eight of each; T-445's board entry still carried the reference-row softening the owner struck on 2026-09-06 (a playbook carries structure only, no rows of any origin); `users.may_build_apps` joined the personal-data register; the `app_step` widening of `STEP_TYPES` got its contracts note. **Noted, not a defect:** the may-build toggle is an endpoint with no screen yet — the org-admin flips it over the API until T-442's surfaces land; and T-440's deviations (a builder cannot run an unpublished app; the app's own firm may reassign) stand as the build argued them, the second now bounded by (3). One structural observation stands for T-442's builder to keep in mind: the READ predicate is the one function in `packages/governance`, but the per-row act answers (`mayEdit` and its siblings) are computed in the route file beside it — acceptable while exactly one file computes them, and the thing to watch when the generated screens arrive.

*Review note, 2026-09-07 (the co-captain pass on runs-and-insights and playbooks, T-443 and T-445 — two branches built in parallel, reconciled and reviewed together; what follows was found by the verification passes and fixed in the review commit).* **The two leaks, one each. (1) The run list told every firm about every firm's runs.** T-443 made a run's row-count and table-coverage real numbers, and `GET /apps/:appId/runs` answered unfiltered — so a rival firm could read that another firm's run covered two rows and infer a submission it was never shown. Narrowed to the export list's own rule (each firm its own runs; the project owner all of them), with an API test and the e2e re-cut to drive both seats. **(2) The deployed app told its client which template it came from.** `deployedFrom` — the org-private shelf's template name, under the words "your firm's template" — was computed for every viewer of the instance; narrowed to the deploying firm's own eyes, with a test that opens the app to the target client and reads it both ways. **On the same wall, the shelf's source-app name now goes dark with its project:** T-445 withheld the source *project's* name from a colleague off that project (ADR-0046's internal walls) but showed the source *app's* name to the whole firm, and app names routinely carry the client's — the two now travel together, and the template's own name and saver always show. **Smaller closures, each with the fix beside a test or a worded refusal:** a whitespace-only deploy name made an app named nothing (the save route's own guard, applied); two simultaneous saves of one template raced to a bare 500 (now a worded conflict); the deploy's definition write named nobody and bumped nothing (now stamped exactly as an ordinary edit); the deploy marked the contractual-data question answered for insight tables nobody is ever asked about (now only for the kinds the question is asked of); the never-published fallback the T-445 record promised (the working copy travels) had no test (now one); and T-443's planted-landowner test asserted on the arithmetic function's output rather than on what the router received — a leak through the surrounding prompt would have passed it — so a second test now captures the words actually sent and searches those. **Also fixed, beyond the two tickets:** the T-443 build found the dev proxy had never forwarded the app namespaces (no app page had ever opened in a browser); the review swept the rest of the list and added the seven other namespaces fetched but not forwarded (`/notifications`, `/acceptance-codes`, `/conflict-exclusions`, `/naming-proposals`, `/attached-sources`, `/external-issues`, `/relationships`), with the rule in the file that a new namespace lands with its prefix. **Honesty notes, kept so nobody re-reads the proofs optimistically:** the run routes' move to `app-runs.ts` came with real behaviour (the run now works — the record says so, the report's "behaviour unchanged" undersold the diff); organisation names and acceptance-state names DO reach the model inside the arithmetic text (party names, never row values — as designed, but the report's summary overstated the bareness); the closed-app e2e asserts the refusal and leaves nothing-was-written to the API test; the e2e's insight sentence is partly synthesised by the fake router's regex, so the platform half of that assertion lives in the API tests; T-445's e2e save-negatives prove unreachability, not the save rule (the API tests prove the rule — the spec's comment now says so); and `expect(raw).not.toContain(projectA)` in the no-rows readback cannot fail, kept as documentation beside assertions that can. **Unreported but examined and kept:** the builder agent's prompt gained chart lines; `recordOf` gained a per-record playbook lookup (a small extra query on a warm path — acceptable now, worth batching if app lists grow); the workspace pane widened for the shelf; the pie chart draws a single full circle when one category holds the whole total (cosmetic, left for T-446's walk to judge). **Latent and deliberately left:** nothing sets a playbook's `retiredAt` yet, and when a retire route arrives it must filter by NAME, not skip rows — retiring v2 must not resurrect v1 onto the shelf (the shelf loop today would); noted here so that route's builder inherits the trap disarmed.

  **Gates:** `pnpm run check` with its exit code read directly; the e2e suite twice on one clean seed.

## Best in class — ticketed 2026-10-23, owner-ruled ahead of the pilot deployment

*The review of the library, plan, sandboxes, review cycle and context layer against the market ([dms-context-review.md](../reference/dms-context-review.md)) and the owner's ruling of 2026-10-23: design the changes and build them without the owner in the loop on each fork, keep [best-in-class.md](best-in-class.md) as the plain list, and put the work ahead of the pilot deployment. Three slices — Register, Reach, Working together. Each ticket's record moves here verbatim as it closes.*

### Slice Register — the document record and the register

- **T-455 — One lifecycle vocabulary.** *Plainly:* every row and page shows the same two badges, where the document is and whether the AI may use it. A `LifecycleBadge` in `packages/ui` reads one label table keyed to `CONTEXT.md`'s four axes; the plan, library, sandbox, review list, cycle and editor top bar use it; the default schema's "Suitability code" field and the library column header become "Status code" (ADR-0041's term), with a dated line in contracts.md. **Done when:** the seeded chapter shows identical badges on every screen it appears on; no screen prints "Suitability". **Deps:** none. ✅ **Built 2026-10-23.**

  **As built. *Plainly: every screen now uses the same words for where a document is. A row in the sandbox says "Working v0.1" and, once checked out, "Frozen v0.1"; the plan, the review list and the review screens say "Submitted P01", "In review P01", "Responding", "Accepted C01"; an internal QA round says "In internal QA" and "QA accepted"; a document that has stopped being current says "Superseded", "Withdrawn", "Removed from plan" or "Rejected"; and received material says "Reference material". Beside that badge, as before, the amber one says when the AI may not use the document and why. The plan and the library no longer print "Suitability": the column, and the seeded field every new project copies, say "Status code", the word the record ruled.***

  **The words live in one place:** [`packages/ui/src/lifecycle.tsx`](../../packages/ui/src/lifecycle.tsx) — fourteen positions, each with its word, its tone and which of `CONTEXT.md`'s axes it belongs to (CDE state, or record state), and `lifecycleBadge(position, revision)` composing the revision only where the position carries one ("Accepted C01", never "Superseded C01"). The design rules' Badge entry (§B) now names the table and retires "Suitability", "In production", "Live" and "Checked out" as state words. **Which position a document is in is derived, never stored**, in the web app's shared helpers ([`apps/web/src/screens/shared.tsx`](../../apps/web/src/screens/shared.tsx)): `lifecycleOf` reads a plan row's record state first (a superseded deliverable is Superseded whatever its cycle last said; `withdrawn` with `inLibrary === false` is the producer's own removal, ADR-0013's two acts that share a word), then the work-item status, read at the right scope (an internal series has no coded reference, so its `in_review` is "In internal QA" and its `accepted` is "QA accepted"); `sandboxLifecycleBadge` reads the head lock and the working revision; `libraryLifecycleBadge` reads the row's kind. A status the table does not know falls back to the old humanised string, so nothing renders tone-less.

  **Where it renders:** the plan table and the plan row's detail, the review list, the review status page, the cycle tray, the library modal title and a new **State** column on the library table, the sandbox's tree rows and its flat all-documents view (the lock glyph and the bare "v0.1" are gone, the badge carries both), and the editor's top bar (a frozen document says "Frozen v0.x" and, beside it, "Checked out — read-only until released", so the two e2e specs that look for *Checked out* still hold). `statusBadge` stays for runs and agents (Ask, History), which are not documents.

  **The relabel** is one line in [`packages/contracts/src/endpoints.ts`](../../packages/contracts/src/endpoints.ts)'s `defaultDeliverableSchema()` and one header in `library.tsx`; the field's key stays `suitability` because a key is storage copied onto every existing project and a label is display text — [contracts.md](contracts.md) carries the dated reason. Projects created before this keep their copied label until their owner changes it. **Tests:** [`packages/ui/src/lifecycle.test.tsx`](../../packages/ui/src/lifecycle.test.tsx) (4 tests: the revision composes only where it should, every position keys to an axis, no retired word, the badge class renders); typecheck, lint and the UI and web suites green; the full check green before the commit.

- **T-456 — Doors for what is already built.** *Plainly:* the screens the API already supports: sandbox document history with restore and undelete; library removal and purge (org admin, typed confirmation); load and retire the firm's drafting manual on the Knowledge screen; share a deliverable with an organisation or a named person, and "who can see this" on every document, read-only for anyone entitled to it. **Done when:** each capability is reachable by the role its ADR names and refused to others; the walkthrough's cards for these beats become screenshots. **Deps:** none. ✅ **Built 2026-10-23.**

  **As built. *Plainly: five things the system could already do, and nobody could reach, now have a door. In the sandbox a draft's menu gains "History…" (every working version, who saved it and when, with Restore) and "Delete…" (to a bin), and the header gains "Deleted" (the bin: restore, and, for the firm's admin, erase for good by typing the title, with the record of what was erased). On the Knowledge shelf, a firm's admin can load a drafting manual and retire one, in both doors. On a plan row, a "Who can see this" list names the producer, the owner and every organisation the owner has shared it with; the owner shares and stops sharing from there, and an admin of a receiving firm limits it to named colleagues or lifts the limit. And the owner's admin can erase a withdrawn reference document from the library by typing its reference.***

  **One read added, one field widened.** The narrowing routes (T-137) had a write and a revoke and no read, so `GET /containers/:containerId/participant-grants` now returns the requester's own organisation's live grants — any participant of the firm may read it, an organisation with no live share gets absence (the list would otherwise confirm a share that does not exist), and the owner's and producer's organisations are never narrowed so they get absence too ([`transmittal.ts`](../../apps/api/src/transmittal.ts); [`transmittal.test.ts`](../../apps/api/src/transmittal.test.ts) gains the case, 6 tests green). A plan row's `sharedWith` gains `shareId` so the owner's revoke needs no second read; [contracts.md](contracts.md) carries both reasons. **Everything else was wrappers and screens**: [`api.ts`](../../apps/web/src/api.ts) gains the bin, restore, purge, purge record, library removal, rulebook load and retire, share, revoke, grants read, grant and revoke calls; [`sandbox-doors.tsx`](../../apps/web/src/sandbox-doors.tsx) holds the History, Delete and Bin modals; [`visibility-panel.tsx`](../../apps/web/src/visibility-panel.tsx) is the "who can see this" panel with the two doors, rendered on the plan row's detail (it moves to the document page with T-457); the plan row gains the library-erase control for the owner's admin on a withdrawn reference row; the Knowledge shelf's `FirmShelfPane` gains a `curation` prop that only an org admin's screen passes, so a member's shelf draws no control at all.

  **Tiers, as the record has them:** the erase doors are the org admin's (`me.orgRole === 'admin'`, ADR-0050's `adminSeat`), the rulebook doors the org admin's (T-308's tier), the share door the owner's (ADR-0016), the narrowing the receiving firm's admin's (ADR-0035 §3's `canNarrow`). Each is drawn only where the API would accept it and the API still answers 404 to anyone else; the typed confirmations are checked on the server and the screens only carry what the person typed. **Not built, named:** the standing grant rules (`/grant-rules`) stay API-only — a routing rule is configuration a register slice should carry, not a per-row door. **Tests:** [`e2e/tests/doors.spec.ts`](../../e2e/tests/doors.spec.ts) (3 specs: history, delete and restore from the bin with the erase door drawn for the admin; the manual door on the shelf; the who-can-see list on a plan row); typecheck and lint green; the full check green before the commit.

- **T-457 — The document page.** *Plainly:* one page per container at `/projects/:id/documents/:containerId` with Overview, Versions, Relationships, Review record, Transmittals and Activity tabs, reading existing endpoints; the ontology panel moves into Relationships. **Done when:** from the plan, the library, the review list, a citation chip and the rail drilldown a document is one click from its page; a member organisation outside the share gets a 404; the page shows the same facts to owner and producer save for the actions each may take. **Deps:** T-455. ✅ **Built 2026-10-23.**

  **As built. *Plainly: every deliverable now has one page. Click a row on the plan or in the library, a reference on the review list, a document in the side menu, or "Open the document page" on a cited source, and you land on it. The header shows the reference, the title, the producing firm and the two badges (where it is; whether the AI may use it). Six tabs: Overview (the facts, and who can see it), Versions (every revision with its files, the chosen one open inline), Relationships (classification and the typed links to other documents), Review record (the appended table of every round), Transmittals (who it was issued to, inside and outside the project), and Activity (what happened to it, newest first). "Edit details…" opens the same editing dialog the plan row had; "Open the review" goes to the review's own screens; "Open the draft" goes to the sandbox editor. A firm outside the share gets "not on a plan you can see", never a page.***

  **No new read.** The page composes what the API already returned to four partial views: the plan row (or the org-private qa-row for an internal series), the cycle, the renditions per version, the transmittal log cut per viewer (ADR-0035's addendum), the container's external issues, and the ontology panel — [`apps/web/src/screens/document.tsx`](../../apps/web/src/screens/document.tsx). The one contract change is `containerId` on `GetVersionResponse` (the join already had it; [contracts.md](contracts.md) says why), which is what lets the source panel and the source modal offer "Open the document page" from a citation. Two pieces were lifted out for reuse rather than copied: the review record's table (`ReviewRecordTable` in `review-record.tsx`) and the transmittal row (`TransmittalRow` in `deliverable-status.tsx`); the plan's `DeliverableDetail` is exported so the page's "Edit details…" opens it with the same tiers (producer super user, lead author, owner super user; T-456's viewer). The library's own document modal is retired here — its PDF viewer is the Versions tab — and the plan modal, the status page's facts card and the rail's text modal retire under T-458 once the register's side panel (T-460) carries the quick edits.

  **What the Activity tab is, honestly:** the record composed from the reads the page already holds — issues and returns with their senders, acknowledgements, completion signals, the close, versions issued, external issues and their first open, and the withdrawal with its reason and author (the withdrawal's time is not on the plan read, and the row says so rather than inventing one). The AI run audit is not here and the tab says where it is (the History screen; ADR-0039 §4). **Tests:** [`e2e/tests/documents.spec.ts`](../../e2e/tests/documents.spec.ts) (3 specs: the plan row lands on the page and the tabs switch; the library row and the review list reach the same page; Org C gets no page for a Calder & Hale deliverable); typecheck and lint green; the full check and the full e2e suite green before the commit. Component 5 §2's surface line records the page.

- **T-459 — Register search and paging endpoints.** *Plainly:* a `GET /projects/:id/library/search` that searches reference, title and content through the retrieval index the agent uses, access-resolved identically, returning rows not chunks; server-side paging, sorting and filtering on the library, plan and review list reads; the ceiling and its revisit trigger stated in `operating-envelope.md`. **Done when:** a ten-thousand-row synthetic project keeps interactive reads under the envelope's p95; a search by meaning finds the seeded ground-investigation report from "contamination near the substation". **Deps:** none. ✅ **Built 2026-10-23.**

  **As built. *Plainly: the library can now be searched by a document's code, its title, or what it says, and both the library and the plan come back a page at a time when a screen asks, sorted and filtered on the server. A search by meaning runs on the very index the AI reads, under the same access rule, so a person and the agent cannot find different things. A ten-thousand-row project answers a page in well under the envelope's half-second line.***

  **The search** is `GET /projects/:projectId/library/search` ([`library.ts`](../../apps/api/src/library.ts), whose statement lives in [`packages/knowledge/src/register-search.ts`](../../packages/knowledge/src/register-search.ts) because the grounding index has one reader, the source rule `check:source` enforces): the lexical arm ranks an exact code first, a code prefix second, a reference, title or description match third; the vector arm is a `min(cosine distance)` over the current version's chunks under the pinned embedding model, computed per row inside the same statement as `deliverableVisibleSql`, so a row the wall excludes is never scored; a query shorter than three characters skips the embedding call (it is a code, not a meaning); a semantic match admits a row when its nearest passage is within 0.5. Filters: `state` (default `live`; `any` for the register of record), `kind`, `discipline`, `statusCode`, `producerId`; sorts: relevance, reference, title, issued, producer; `page` and `pageSize` with a `total`; each row says why it matched (`reference`, `title`, `content`, `none`). The list and the search share one row shape and one mapping (`libraryRowSelect`, `toLibraryItems`), so the two reads cannot describe a row differently. **The plan read** gained `q`, `page`, `pageSize`, `sort` and `direction`, answering exactly as before when none is given ([`plan.ts`](../../apps/api/src/plan.ts)); [contracts.md](contracts.md) carries the reasons. The client gained `librarySearch` and `planPage` and a small query-string helper. **No index was added:** the reads are served by the existing `(project, reference)` unique index and the HNSW index on chunks; the measurement below is what says that is enough at the envelope's scale.

  **Measured, not assumed:** [`library-search.test.ts`](../../apps/api/src/library-search.test.ts) (8 tests) inserts a ten-thousand-row synthetic project of its own, times a page-100 search with a code query and a page-150 plan read, and asserts both under 500 ms with row-level security on; it also proves the code-prefix, title and content arms (the content arm through a probe chunk that only the vector can find), the paging total, the kind filter and the issue-date sort, the wall (Org C never sees a Calder & Hale row), and the refusal of a bad page size. The synthetic project is removed afterwards. [operating-envelope.md](../architecture/operating-envelope.md)'s trigger 3 now says what performance work remains when it fires: the retrieval side, not the register.

- **T-460 — The register component and saved views.** *Plainly:* one `Register` in `packages/ui`: search box with a visible filtered state, filter chips, column chooser, sort, row selection, a side panel on row select, one row menu; saved views as a small table (participant, organisation, name, filter) private or shared within the organisation; `CONTEXT.md` gains **Saved view**; design-rules §B gains Side panel, Bulk-action bar, Filter chip, Saved view. **Done when:** a filtered view survives reload; a view shared within the organisation is invisible across the wall by construction. **Deps:** T-459. ✅ **Built 2026-10-23** (migration **0071**).

  **As built. *Plainly: there is now one way a list of documents looks and works — a search box that says when it is filtering, filter chips you take off one at a time, a Columns chooser, sort on any column, pages for a long list, a tick box on every row with an action bar for the selection, and a "Views" menu where you save the way you have set the list up, for yourself or for your firm. The project library is the first list on it: its two tables became one register with the lifecycle pair on every row, the query lives in the address so a filtered view survives a reload and can be sent as a link, and a saved view is that same query under a name. A view shared within one firm is never seen by another.***

  **The component** is [`packages/ui/src/register.tsx`](../../packages/ui/src/register.tsx): it owns the grammar and nothing about data — every piece of state is controlled, so a screen puts it in the URL or in a saved view without the component knowing; the filter menu's items and the bulk bar's actions are the screen's. Classes and states are in design-rules §B (Register, with the side panel named as the kit's `Drawer`, the filter chip, the bulk-action bar and the saved view), the vocabulary in [ui-vocabulary.md](../design/ui-vocabulary.md), the tests in [`register.test.tsx`](../../packages/ui/src/register.test.tsx) (5). **Saved views** are a table (`saved_views`, drawn in [data-model.md](data-model.md) drawer 2 before the migration was written; migration 0071 with the house-style grant hand-added), three routes ([`saved-views.ts`](../../apps/api/src/saved-views.ts)) whose read's own `WHERE` is the organisation ceiling, a `CONTEXT.md` term (**Saved view** — a named filter, never an access object), a personal-data row for the maker, and a menu ([`saved-views-menu.tsx`](../../apps/web/src/saved-views-menu.tsx)); [contracts.md](contracts.md) carries the reasons. [`saved-views.test.ts`](../../apps/api/src/saved-views.test.ts) (4): save, list, the maker's name, a duplicate name refused; a private view the maker's alone and a shared one the firm's, absence to the owner organisation and to Org C; delete by the maker only; a malformed body refused.

  **The library on it** ([`library.tsx`](../../apps/web/src/screens/library.tsx)): the live-deliverables and reference-material tables became one register over T-459's search read; reference material has a title cell and the same columns, marked by its glyph and its lifecycle badge; a search that matched a document's text says so on the row; the row's five inline actions became one menu (Open, Transmit, Issue or request externally, Supersede, Withdraw or Propose withdrawal), each offered only where the API would accept it; the notice panels above are unchanged. The query (`q`, `state`, `kind`, `discipline`, `sort`, `direction`, `page`, hidden `cols`, the applied `view`) is the address. **Selection is wired in the component and not yet enabled on the library**, because every bulk action it would offer is T-461's; a bar with nothing real in it would be a placeholder. **Tests:** [`e2e/tests/library-register.spec.ts`](../../e2e/tests/library-register.spec.ts) (3: search narrows and survives a reload; a filter chip comes off; a saved view applies and never crosses the wall); typecheck and lint green; the full check and the full e2e suite green before the commit.

- **T-461 — Bulk actions and export.** *Plainly:* a bulk-action bar on selection: transmit, issue externally, propose supersede, classify with an explicit append-or-replace choice, export the selection to Excel; bulk endpoints where only single-row ones exist. **Done when:** a bulk transmit of twenty rows is one dialog; export round-trips through the plan's own import shape. **Deps:** T-460. ✅ **Built 2026-10-23**.

  **As built. *Plainly: tick several rows on the library and do one thing to all of them. A bar appears above the table saying how many are ticked, with the acts the ticked rows allow — Transmit, Issue externally (or Request external issue), Supersede, Classify, and Export to Excel. Each opens the same dialog a single row opens, titled for the count ("Transmit 2 documents"), and the act either happens for every row or for none: a row that cannot take it stops the lot and is named on screen ("Nothing was transmitted — WA-ECO-PEA-001: produced by a recipient"). Export hands back a spreadsheet in the plan template's own shape, so it can be edited and imported back.*

  **The routes** are in [`apps/api/src/bulk-acts.ts`](../../apps/api/src/bulk-acts.ts): `POST /projects/:id/bulk/transmittals`, `/bulk/external-issues`, `/bulk/supersessions`, `/bulk/classifications` and `/plan/export`. Every bulk write checks every row first, refuses the batch whole with a 409 that carries `failures` (container, reference, problem), and lands the writes in one transaction. None restates what a transmittal, an external issue or a superseding edge is: the single-row helpers were lifted to module scope (`transmittal.ts`'s share, membership and standing-rule helpers; `external-issue.ts`'s `recordExternalIssue`; `ontology.ts`'s `mayProposeEdge`/`mayConfirmEdge`/`producesIt`) and the bulk routes call them per row. The wall is unchanged: rows are read back through the same deliverable-visibility pre-filter the library uses, and a row the requester may not see refuses the batch as "not in this project's library" — the same absence a single route gives.

  **Classify is explicit** (`mode: 'append' | 'replace'`): append writes the term only where the facet is unset and reports how many were kept as they were; replace sets every row. It is a producing-organisation act row by row (ADR-0045), so the owner classifies only its own rows and a batch with another firm's row in it is refused. **Supersede** is one replacement over many: a `supersedes` edge from the replacement to each row, proposed by either party and confirmed in the same act when the caller may confirm (T-386's rule), a row already carrying the proposed edge being confirmed rather than refused. **Export** writes sheet 1 as Title + the scheme's code fields (read back out of each reference by `decomposeReference`) + its metadata fields, with the template's dropdowns, and sheet 2 as the record (reference, revision, state, producer, issued) that the import ignores by design; [`bulk-acts.test.ts`](../../apps/api/src/bulk-acts.test.ts) proves the file re-imports through `POST /plan/import` (three rows out, three new rows in).

  **The screen** ([`library.tsx`](../../apps/web/src/screens/library.tsx)): the Register's `selection` is on, with `rowLabel` so a tick box is "Select WA-GEO-GIR-004" and not an id; the bar's acts are computed from the ticked live rows (owner → Transmit; anyone with the setting → Issue or Request; owner or producer → Supersede; producer → Classify; everyone → Export). The three dialogs now take `items`, so the row menu and the bar open the same door; a single row still goes through the single-row route and its own wording, many go through the bulk route, and a refusal is read off the 409's `failures` into one sentence. The selection is state, never the address — a selection is a moment, not a view — and it is spent with the act. **Personal data:** the bulk external issue writes the same `external_recipients` row the single route does (registered at T-431); no new table or field. **Tests:** `bulk-acts.test.ts` (5), `register.test.tsx` gains the row label, [`library-bulk.spec.ts`](../../e2e/tests/library-bulk.spec.ts) ticks two rows, exports, and transmits both through one dialog.

- **T-462 — The three screens move onto the register.** *Plainly:* the plan, the library (reference material gains a title and the same columns) and the sandbox's all-documents view use the component; the review list is folded into the plan's register as a view. **Done when:** a document controller finds any document by meaning or code in one box on any of the three; the plan's organisation-standard locked columns are unchanged. **Deps:** T-460, T-461. ✅ **Built 2026-10-23** (migration **0072**).

  **As built. *Plainly: the plan, the review list, the library and the sandbox's overview now look and work the same way. On the plan, one box finds a deliverable by its code, its title or what it says, and the row it means comes first; filter chips narrow to live, superseded or withdrawn rows, to deliverables or reference material, and (for the owner) to one producing organisation; the columns the organisation's super user set for everyone stay exactly where they were and cannot be hidden; a personal view may hide the platform's own columns, be saved under a name, and is kept in the address so a reload shows the same list. "Review" is no longer a separate table: it is the same plan seen for reviewing, with Authors and Reviewers columns, and its rows open the review status page. Reference material has a title of its own at last — "Statement of community consultation" where the register used to say "Reference material". The sandbox's overview searches working documents by name and code.*

  **The plan read** ([`plan.ts`](../../apps/api/src/plan.ts)) is paged and searched on the server: `GET /projects/:id/plan` gains `state`, `kind` and `producerId` filters and a `relevance` sort, and a searched read goes through [`packages/knowledge/src/register-search.ts`](../../packages/knowledge/src/register-search.ts)'s new `searchPlanContainerIds` — the same two arms as the library (code and title first, then the current version's nearest passage under the pinned embedding model, inside `withProjectScope`), over the plan's own reach: every library-scope container for the owner, the organisation's own for anyone else, published or not, so a planned row with no version yet is still found by its code. The arms were factored out (`patternOf`, `nearestDistance`, `lexicalRank`) so the library and the plan rank by one definition.

  **Reference material's title** is `containers.title` (migration 0072, drawn in [data-model.md](data-model.md) drawer 2 first): a deliverable's title stays on its work item and this column stays null there — the reads coalesce the two and nothing is stored twice (the 2026-07-18 ruling). It is set from the file's name at load ([`bulk-load.ts`](../../apps/api/src/bulk-load.ts)), the seed names its six reference documents, the title route writes it when a container has no work item, and `PlanRow` gains a coalesced `title`. Not personal data: it names a document.

  **The screens.** [`plan.tsx`](../../apps/web/src/screens/plan.tsx) renders the `Register` with the query in the address (`readPlanQuery`/`writePlanQuery`), saved views on the `plan` and `review` registers, selection with Export to Excel (T-461's route), and a `view` prop: `/review` now renders `<PlanScreen view="review" />` and the old `review.tsx` screen is deleted — the review view adds Authors and Reviewers (proposed reviewers badged, confirmation still on the status page, ADR-0033), keeps the reference cell as the door to the document page (T-457) and the row as the door to the review, and offers "Plan a deliverable" as a link (T-357). The organisation-standard columns render as locked, non-hideable columns between Title and the platform's own; the super user's "Standard columns" button sets them, distinct from the register's own "Columns" chooser. The plan's `Metadata` button stays on the row until T-458 retires the modal. [`sandbox.tsx`](../../apps/web/src/screens/sandbox.tsx)'s all-documents overview is a `Register` with a client-side search over a document's shown name, its own title and its bound row's reference — **by name and code, not by meaning**: a working draft is not in the retrieval index (the index is over published versions), and this record says so rather than pretending otherwise. The done-when's "any of the three" is met on the controller's three registers (plan, review, library); the sandbox is the producer's working space.

  **Tests.** [`plan-register.spec.ts`](../../e2e/tests/plan-register.spec.ts) (3): the plan finds a code in one box, ranks it first, survives reload and shows reference material's title; the review view has its columns and its door; the sandbox overview searches by name. `library-search.test.ts`'s plan read asserts the ranked first row. Four older specs that clicked a plan or review row by text now search for it first — the plan is a paged register, and on a long-lived local database the seeded rows are no longer on page one.

- **T-458 — The four partial views retire.** *Plainly:* the plan row's modal, the library row's modal, the review status page's facts card and the rail's text modal are removed, their content living on the document page and their quick edits in the register side panel. **Done when:** no modal renders a document's facts; e2e covers the journeys the modals carried. **Deps:** T-457, T-460. ✅ **Built 2026-10-23**.

  **As built. *Plainly: a document's facts now live in one place, its page. On the plan, the row's "Metadata" button is gone and a "Details" button opens a side panel beside the list — the same panel "Edit details…" opens on the document page — holding the quick edits: the title, the document owner, the authoring team and review group, the description and authoring metadata (moved in from the old metadata dialog), who can see it, classification and relationships, and remove or restore. The review status page no longer repeats the reference, revision, verdict and owner in a card; it says where they are and links there, keeping only the review's own outcome (contractual or not). Nothing else opens a dialog to show a document's facts.*

  **What each of the four became.** The plan row's two dialogs (`DeliverableDetail`'s modal card and the `MetadataModal`) are one side panel: `DeliverableDetail` in [`plan.tsx`](../../apps/web/src/screens/plan.tsx) now renders the kit's `Drawer` — design-rules §B's rule for the Register: *the Drawer is the side panel; nothing else is* — and gains a "Description and metadata" section over the new `MetadataEditor` ([`metadata-modal.tsx`](../../apps/web/src/metadata-modal.tsx)), the editor split out of the modal so the sandbox's document-metadata dialog and the panel edit through one component. T-361's note that the row's detail was "the design system's modal-card treatment" is superseded by the 2026-10-23 ruling and says so in place. The library row's modal was already retired by T-457 (the row lands on the page). The review status page's facts card ([`deliverable-status.tsx`](../../apps/web/src/screens/deliverable-status.tsx)) became a pointer to the document page plus the T-392 acceptance outcome, which is the review's fact and stays. The rail's text modal turned out to be dead code — `project.tsx` held a `SourceModal` whose opener nothing ever called — and is removed; the editor keeps its own `SourceModal` for a citation's recorded chunk (Q-022), which is not a document's facts.

  **Tiers are unchanged:** the panel's edit rights are `DeliverableDetail`'s as before (producing super user; the row's live lead author for title, metadata, authors and reviewer proposals — T-362; the owner super user for reviewer confirmation), and the metadata section saves through the same `PATCH /containers/:id` the modal used. **Tests:** [`details-drawer.spec.ts`](../../e2e/tests/details-drawer.spec.ts) opens the panel from a plan row, finds the editor and the team inside it, closes it with Escape, and checks the status page no longer states the producing organisation and does link to the document page; `plan-owner-review.spec.ts` confirms a proposed reviewer through the same panel from the document page as before.

- **T-463 — The AI transparency table.** *Plainly:* a "How the AI works here" page in project settings and the workspace, one row per AI feature (what it reads, what it may write, where it runs, what it keeps, never trains), with a per-project switch for the owner's super user, audited like a rails change (ADR-0030), enforced at each launcher and gateway entry; a switched-off feature is absent, not greyed; the table exports as a document. ADR-0037 gains the note that a switch only narrows reach. **Done when:** switching the checker off on the seeded project removes it from Tools and the editor and refuses its endpoint; the audit names who and why. **Deps:** none. ✅ **Built 2026-10-23** (migration **0073**).

  **As built. *Plainly: a project now has a page called "How the AI works here", one click from its home, with one row per AI feature — Ask, drafting in the editor, the document creator, the QA checker, the folder structure builder, rule extraction, the app builder and app insights — saying where you meet it, what it reads, what it may write, what it keeps, and that it never trains on the project's data; a last row says the same for search and the retrieval index, which everything stands on and cannot be switched. It states where every call runs, as the model router actually enforces it. The owner's super user can turn any feature off for the project, giving a reason, and back on; each change is listed on the page with a name and a date, and everyone on the project can read the list. A switched-off feature is gone from every screen — the tile leaves Tools, the "Check this draft" button leaves the editor, Ask leaves the rail — and asking the server for it is refused in words. The whole page exports as a Word document. The workspace has the same table for the deployment, with no project and no switch.*

  **The registry** is [`apps/api/src/ai-features.ts`](../../apps/api/src/ai-features.ts): the facts for each feature are written once there, beside the code they describe, and the page and the export render them — a row cannot drift from its feature without the drift showing in one diff. Where every call runs comes from the router's own posture (`Router.posture`, new), never from copy. **The switch** is `ai_feature_switches` (migration 0073, drawn in [data-model.md](data-model.md) drawer 7 first): append-only by trigger, the newest row per feature decides, a feature with no row is on; `PUT /projects/:id/ai-features/:key` with a required reason, the owner's super user only (`membershipRole === 'owner' && elevated`); `GET /projects/:id/ai-transparency` for everyone on the project, `GET /ai-transparency` for the workspace, and `/ai-transparency/export` as a `.docx`. It **only narrows**: the tier (ADR-0037), the deployment's declared workflows and each requester's own entitlement are still applied first — the ADR-0037 addendum records this, Claude-ruled under the owner's delegation of 2026-10-23.

  **Enforced at every gateway**, with one guard (`refuseIfOff`, a 403 whose detail is `ai_feature_off`): the checker's plan and run routes, the document creator's, the run route (a run on a document is drafting, a run without one is Ask), the folder-structure proposal, rule extraction, the app builder's conversation and the app run. `GET /tools` omits a switched-off tool exactly as it omits a worker the requester cannot use (T-269's rule, one more filter). **Absent at every launcher** in the web, through one cached read per project (`useAiFeaturesOff`): the rail's Ask item and the home's Ask bar, the editor's Check button, the sandbox structure builder's ask box, the apps' "Build it with the agent" door; a style guide created while extraction is off is saved without a rule set and the screen says so. **Personal data:** `changed_by_participant_id` names a person on a configuration change — registered, with the reason stated as a project decision. `CONTEXT.md` gains **AI feature switch**.

  **Tests:** [`ai-features.test.ts`](../../apps/api/src/ai-features.test.ts) (3) — the table and posture, the switch thrown by the owner's super user and refused for another firm's, the tile gone from Tools, the endpoint's refusal in words, the history naming who and why, the export; [`ai-transparency.spec.ts`](../../e2e/tests/ai-transparency.spec.ts) walks Rachel turning the checker off with a reason, Eleanor meeting absence in Tools and the editor, and the switch going back on.

- **T-464 — Copy and vocabulary.** *Plainly:* one line under each heading with a "learn more"; the composer's six placeholder chips and the workspace's three placeholder rail items removed until built; "Personal workspace" and "Personal sandbox" made one word; design-rules §G gains "every label is a `CONTEXT.md` term or a plain verb". **Done when:** no screen shows a control that does nothing; the copy pass is listed screen by screen in the ticket's record. **Deps:** none. ✅ **Built 2026-10-23**.

  **As built. *Plainly: nothing on a screen is there to be clicked and do nothing. The Ask composer no longer shows six greyed chips for things that were never built; the editor's start screen no longer offers two cards you could not press; the workspace's rail no longer lists four sections that opened a paragraph saying "arrives later"; the "No saved views yet" line is a note, not a menu item. Every main page now opens with one sentence saying what it is for, and a "Learn more" that unfolds the longer explanation in place. The design rules say so in one line: every label is a word the vocabulary defines or a plain verb.*

  **The copy pass, screen by screen.**
  - **Ask** ([`composer-sources.tsx`](../../apps/web/src/composer-sources.tsx), [`ask.tsx`](../../apps/web/src/screens/ask.tsx)): the six placeholder chips — Attach a file, Prompts, Style, Web search, Sandbox search, Model — and the disabled Tools chip are removed; the live chips (library mention, Lens, Data sources, Context) stay. The questions they waited on are unchanged (Q-021 the model picker; the sandbox-search ruling; the search provider) and are not reopened here.
  - **Editor start screen** ([`editor.tsx`](../../apps/web/src/screens/editor.tsx)): the disabled "From a template" and "PowerPoint" cards and the italic "shared and personal sandboxes arrive with the sandbox drawer" row are removed; one card — Word document — remains, and the document creator in Tools is where a document starts from an outline.
  - **Workspace** ([`workspace.tsx`](../../apps/web/src/screens/workspace.tsx)): the Ask, Editor, Personal sandbox and Tools sections (notes only) and the landing's dead Ask bar are removed; the rail carries Your knowledge, Kept apps and How the AI works. "Personal sandbox" therefore no longer appears as a label; the vocabulary keeps the term for the per-user sandbox the sandbox drawer will build.
  - **Saved views menu** ([`saved-views-menu.tsx`](../../apps/web/src/saved-views-menu.tsx)): "No saved views yet" is a note, not a menu item with an empty click.
  - **One line and Learn more** — the new `PageIntro` in [`packages/ui/src/page-intro.tsx`](../../packages/ui/src/page-intro.tsx), applied to the Project library, the Plan (both views), the Sandbox, Tools, History, Apps, Knowledge and How the AI works here; the longer text each carried moved behind the toggle, so a returning person reads one sentence.
  - **Design rules §G** gains item 3: every label is a `CONTEXT.md` term or a plain verb; no control is shown that does nothing; one line under every heading with a Learn more. **ui-vocabulary.md**'s routable-pages line is brought up to date.

  **Not changed, on purpose:** the Data sources chip's warning state ("no sources in scope") and the Context chip stay — they are statements about the answer the person is about to get, not controls; the Lens chip is a real control. **Tests:** [`copy-pass.spec.ts`](../../e2e/tests/copy-pass.spec.ts) (2) walks the workspace rail, the Ask composer, the editor's one card, and the library's Learn more; `page-intro.test.tsx` covers the primitive.

- **T-465 — Undo and feedback.** *Plainly:* a `Toast` with Undo for every reversible act for as long as it is reversible; skeletons on every register; optimistic rename, move, bind and classification with rollback. **Done when:** an accidental withdraw is undone in one click and the audit records both acts. **Deps:** T-460. ✅ **Built 2026-10-23** (migration **0074**).

  **As built. *Plainly: when you do something that can be undone — withdraw a document from the library, remove a planned deliverable, rename or move a draft, change a classification — a small message appears at the foot of the screen saying what happened, with an Undo button, and pressing it reverses the act. The reversal is a real act of its own: the record keeps both the mistake and its undoing, with who did each and when, and the document page's Activity tab lists them. Renames, moves, binds and classifications show their result at once and step back on their own if the server refuses. A bind says plainly that it has no undo, because a document binds once.*

  **The record came first, because undo without it would be erasure.** Until now a restoration cleared the withdrawal's reason and author off the container, so the record could not say a withdrawal had ever happened — the ticket's done-when ("the audit records both acts") was not satisfiable. `container_state_changes` (migration 0074, drawn in [data-model.md](data-model.md) drawer 2 first) is append-only by trigger: one row per change of record state — from, to, reason where the act takes one, who, when — written by every route that changes state ([`state-changes.ts`](../../apps/api/src/state-changes.ts)'s `recordStateChange`, called from withdrawal, the owner's acceptance of a proposed withdrawal, restoration, a confirmed `supersedes` edge, the retirement that returns a container to live, and the bulk supersession) and read at `GET /containers/:id/state-changes` through the plan row's own visibility. The document page's Activity tab lists these rows ("Removed from the plan — reason", "Restored to the plan", "Superseded by …") with their dates, replacing the dateless withdrawal line it carried. `changed_by_participant_id` is a named person and is registered.

  **The toast** is [`packages/ui/src/toast.tsx`](../../packages/ui/src/toast.tsx): one `ToastProvider` at the app root, `useToast()` in any screen, at most three stacked at the foot of the frame, eight seconds or a dismiss, an error waiting until dismissed. **Undo is the reverse act through the API** — restoration for withdraw and remove, the reverse rename or move, the previous term for a classification — never a client-side rollback of something the server did, so both acts stay on the record. Where there is no reverse act the toast says so instead of offering a button that lies: a bind ("a document binds once; there is no undo"), the first term under a facet ("cannot be unset, only changed"). The sandbox's delete already lands in the bin with restore (T-456). **Optimistic** rename, move and classification show the result at once and roll back on refusal, with the refusal said in a note; skeletons were already on every register (T-460's `Register` renders them while rows are null). Design-rules §B gains the **Toast** entry.

  **Tests:** [`state-changes.test.ts`](../../apps/api/src/state-changes.test.ts) (2) — a withdrawal and its restoration both on the record, newest first, each with its author, and absence for a firm that cannot see the row; [`undo.spec.ts`](../../e2e/tests/undo.spec.ts) removes a planned deliverable by mistake, undoes it from the toast in one click, and reads both acts on the document page.

- **T-466 — The command palette and keyboard moves.** *Plainly:* ⌘K finds any document, jumps to any section and runs the current row's actions, with a visible hint; J/K/R/E in the review tray; F opens filters; "?" lists the shortcuts; focus rules keep typing in the editor untouched. **Done when:** any seeded document is reachable in three keystrokes from anywhere. **Deps:** T-459. ✅ **Built 2026-10-23**.

  **As built. *Plainly: press ⌘K anywhere in a project and a box opens. Type a code, a title or a few words of what a document says and the documents come back, ranked the way the registers rank them; type a section's name and it is there to jump to; on a document's page its own actions — Edit details, Open the draft, Open the review — are there to run. Enter takes the first. A "Search ⌘K" hint sits in the top bar. Press "?" for the list of shortcuts; press F on any register to land in its search box; in a review round J and K walk the comments, R opens the highlighted one's response and E opens it as "no change was made". None of this fires while you are typing.*

  **The palette** is [`apps/web/src/command-palette.tsx`](../../apps/web/src/command-palette.tsx), mounted once in the project shell. Documents come from the two reads the registers already use — `GET /plan?q=` and `GET /library/search?q=` (T-459, T-462) — merged by container and capped at eight, so the palette finds exactly what a person could find by hand and nothing the wall hides; sections are the rail's items (Ask absent when the project switched it off, T-463); a page offers its actions through `usePaletteActions`, for as long as it is mounted — the document page registers its three. The ranked read means a seeded document is three keystrokes away: ⌘K, its code, Enter ([`palette.spec.ts`](../../e2e/tests/palette.spec.ts) proves it from the home page).

  **The moves** live where their lists are: F in the palette's global handler (it focuses the page's `input[type=search]`, which every Register has); J/K/R/E in [`cycle.tsx`](../../apps/web/src/screens/cycle.tsx)'s `RoundCard`, where the highlight the keys move is the same one the pointer gives, and `CommentRow` opens its response editor on a keyboard request and focuses the box. **The focus rule** is one predicate shared by both handlers: nothing single-key fires when the event's target is an input, a textarea, a select or anything contenteditable, and ⌘K is the only chord — so the editor's canvas, a comment box and the palette's own input are never intercepted. "F opens filters" is built as F landing in the register's search box, which is the filter a register is searched with; the chip menu stays a pointer control. Design-rules §B gains the **Command palette** entry.

  **Tests:** `palette.spec.ts` — ⌘K, a code, Enter lands on the document page; the page's actions appear; "?" lists the shortcuts; F lands in the library's box and typing there is not intercepted.

- **T-467 — The home page as a work queue.** *Plainly:* project home is "waiting on you", recent documents and your saved views; the workspace home does the same across projects; one aggregating read per project, access-resolved. **Done when:** every item in the queue is one click from the screen where it is done. **Deps:** T-460. ✅ **Built 2026-10-23**.

  **As built. *Plainly: the project home now opens with what is waiting on you — a reviewer to confirm, a lead appointment to accept, a transmittal to acknowledge for your organisation, a request to issue outside the project to decide, a proposed withdrawal to decide, comments to answer on your deliverable, open findings to close on your draft — each a link to the screen where that act is done. Under it: the documents that moved most recently (library issues you may see, your organisation's working drafts) and the views you saved, each opening its register already set up. The workspace home asks every project you are on the same question and lists the answers under each project's name, leaving out a project with nothing waiting.*

  **One read** — `GET /projects/:id/work-queue` ([`work-queue.ts`](../../apps/api/src/work-queue.ts)) returns the items, the recent documents and the saved views together. Every arm is the query the destination screen already runs, cut to the requester: proposals to confirm only for the owner's super user (the status page's Confirm button is theirs); a lead appointment to accept only for its appointee, and outside the owner organisation only once the owner has confirmed (ADR-0033 addendum — until then there is nothing for the appointee to do); transmittals to acknowledge through the pending-transmittals join; requests to issue externally for whoever `mayIssueExternally`; proposed withdrawals for the owner's super user; comments without a response on issued rounds of deliverables the requester authors; open findings on the requester's organisation's drafts. Recent documents come through the deliverable-visibility pre-filter; saved views through the T-460 ceiling. Nothing widens reach: a person who could not do the thing by hand is not told it is waiting.

  **The screens** — [`work-queue.tsx`](../../apps/web/src/work-queue.tsx) holds the three panels and `useWorkQueue`; the project home ([`project.tsx`](../../apps/web/src/screens/project.tsx)) leads with the queue, then recent documents and saved views, and keeps the work-items table beneath; the workspace landing ([`workspace.tsx`](../../apps/web/src/screens/workspace.tsx)) renders one queue per project with the project's name. A saved view opens its register with the view's own query in the address (`savedViewHref`), so the same filter the person saved is what they land on. Each item's `href` is a path inside the project, and the spec proves the click lands there.

  **Tests:** [`work-queue.test.ts`](../../apps/api/src/work-queue.test.ts) (2) — a proposed lead reviewer is the owner super user's to confirm and not the producer's; owner-side acceptance follows; hrefs are in-project paths; a private saved view is its maker's alone; [`work-queue.spec.ts`](../../e2e/tests/work-queue.spec.ts) proposes Rachel as lead reviewer through the API and walks her from the workspace home's cross-project list to the project home's queue to the status page in one click.

- **T-468 — Citations land on the passage.** *Plainly:* a `SourceCard` on hover shows the recorded passage with document, revision, page and record state; click opens the document page at the passage; authority chips become clickable; a quoted rule gets a visibly different rule card (ADR-0048 §5); scanned documents with no extractable text are marked not citable. `GET /versions/:id/passages/:chunkId` reads the recorded chunk, never re-retrieves. `Q-022` closes; ADR-0022 consequence note. **Done when:** hover shows the passage within a second; click lands on it highlighted; a superseded source's card says so. **Deps:** T-457. ✅ **Built 2026-10-24** (migration **0075**).

  **As built. *Plainly: hover any source under an answer, a suggestion or a finding and a small card shows the exact passage the AI read — the document's name and revision, whether it is still current, the page where the source has pages, and the passage word for word. Click the source and the document's page opens with that passage highlighted. A source that has since been replaced says so ("This version has been superseded — the citation still points at what the AI read"). A reference to an outside standard is clickable too, and says honestly that the standards library is not part of this build. A rule quoted from your firm's rulebook is no longer dressed like a citation: it sits in its own box labelled "From your firm's rulebook — a rule, not a citation".*

  **The record came first, because a card can only show what was written down.** A citation recorded which document and version it came from, but not which passage; the step that picked the passage had its id and dropped it. `citations.chunk_id` (migration 0075, drawn in [data-model.md](data-model.md) drawer 4 first) now keeps it — nullable, **no foreign key**, so a re-ingest that replaces a document's passages cannot erase the fact of which passage was cited. Three places had to stop dropping it: the **draft step** (the numbered source a claim's marker names now carries its passage id through ground-check, whose admission is still by document), the **cite step** (`sourceColumns` keeps it) and the **checker's finding writer** (which had folded the id into the citation's id string; it is now a field of its own and the string is unchanged). Citations written before this carry none, and say so on the card: "recorded before passages were kept, so it points at the whole document".

  **The read** — `GET /versions/:versionId/passages/:chunkId` ([`library.ts`](../../apps/api/src/library.ts)) is guarded exactly like `GET /versions/:id` (the version's project, then deliverable visibility), then reads **one row by id** through `readChunkPassage` in `@infora/knowledge` — modelled on `readChunkPassages`, and the only place outside `data` that may touch the chunk table. It never searches. The text shown is the source as it really reads at the recorded span (the locator's verbatim), not the chunker's rewritten text. A chunk id belonging to a different version is a 404; a chunk that has gone returns `held: false` and the card says the passage was re-indexed after the run. Where the span no longer verifies, the card degrades to the chunk's own text with no page or paragraph, never an invented locator.

  **The card** — `HoverCard` in [`packages/ui`](../../packages/ui/src/hover-card.tsx) (opens after 150 ms of hover or at once on keyboard focus; closes on leave, blur or Escape; portalled and flipped like the dropdown menu; the open/closed rule is a pure reducer so it is unit-tested). `SourceChip` is now a real `<button>`, so the keyboard reaches it. The card's body is [`source-card.tsx`](../../apps/web/src/source-card.tsx): fetched on first open and kept per (version, chunk) for the page's life, "Reading the passage…" while it loads, the state shown with the T-455 `LifecycleBadge` (the old hand-written state words in the source modal and panel retired in the same change). **The click** goes to the document page with `?version=&passage=`; that page opens the cited version even when it is not in the cycle's rounds, marks the passage in the version's text and scrolls to it, or — where the version shows as a PDF — opens the PDF at the cited page with the passage quoted above it (a PDF embedded this way cannot be highlighted inside). Reference material has no plan row for the document page to show, so there the older source view opens, now with the passage marked in its text: never a dead click. **Authority references** are clickable chips whose card shows the reference and says the authority library is not part of this build; they request nothing from the server. The findings panel now draws authority references as authority chips (it had hard-coded library ones). The quoted rule is `RuleCard` in `packages/ui`.

  **Deliberately not built: the "not citable" mark** for a scanned document with no extractable text. No textless document can enter the library today (upload and bulk load refuse a file whose text cannot be read), so there is nothing for the mark to attach to; ADR-0022's dated note says the flag is drawn with T-472's intake queue and counted by T-469's reach statement. **Deviation from the brief:** the brief named `cite-leaf` and the checker's finding writer as the two places the chunk id was dropped; the draft step was a third (the marker-to-source map held only the document), found when the e2e citation had no passage — fixed there, with a unit test.

  **Reviewed 2026-10-24 (the co-captain, with a verifier reading the diff claim by claim).** Every build claim held. Three gaps were closed in review: an **authority chip's click did nothing** — its card opened only on hover or keyboard focus, which on a pointer that does not focus a button on click made "clickable" untrue — so a chip with no page to open now toggles its card on click (`HoverCard`'s `toggleOnClick`, reducer-tested); two header comments in the source modal and panel still said the passage hover "waits on the chunk-provenance theme"; and one changed file the record had not named — `run-reader.ts`'s `toCitation` now returns the passage id on read-back, which the card needs. Two honest limits stand: the end-to-end test accepts the PDF banner or the older source view's mark as a landing, so it proves "lands on the passage" but not "highlighted" on the document page's own text — no seeded document exercised that path in a browser, though the unit tests cover it; and the card's focus, blur and Escape behaviour is tested through the reducer and the e2e spec, not with fired DOM events.

  **Tests:** [`library.test.ts`](../../apps/api/src/library.test.ts) (4) — verbatim text, page and span; a gone chunk is `held: false`; another version's chunk is 404; an outsider is 404; [`passage.test.ts`](../../packages/knowledge/src/passage.test.ts) (3); `cite-leaf.test.ts`, `grounded-draft.test.ts`, `ground-check.test.ts`, `qa-checker.test.ts` — the chunk is kept at every step; `ui.test.tsx` — the card's open/close rule, the button chip, the click carrying the chunk, the rule card's label; `render.test.tsx` — authority chips; [`citation-passage.spec.ts`](../../e2e/tests/citation-passage.spec.ts) — hover shows the passage with the document's reference, Escape and focus work, click lands on the document page with the passage marked or quoted.

- **T-469 — Scope on the request, and the pre-filter wired.** *Plainly:* `AssemblyRequest.request` gains `scope` (vocabulary terms, container ids, or a saved scope); the gateway applies it as the semantic pre-filter; reach counts come back on the run; a reach statement counts only what the requester may see and what state excluded (ADR-0018 note). `Q-028` ruled; ADR-0029 addendum; `CONTEXT.md` gains **Scope** and **Reach statement**. **Done when:** the statement's numbers match the passage-grain audit; a user in organisation B never sees a count that moves when A shares one more document with C. **Deps:** none. ✅ **Built 2026-10-24** (migration **0076**).

  **As built. *Plainly: you can now tell a question, a draft or a check which part of the library to read — a discipline, a document type, a handful of named documents, or a choice you saved earlier. The choice is written down on the run's plan before anything is read. When the run finishes it says, in one sentence, how many documents it read, which it could not read and why, and how many your own choice left out: "Read 14 documents in your scope. Excluded: 2 superseded. Your scope left out 31 you could have included." A choice can only make the reading smaller — it can never reach a document you could not open by hand, and a choice that leaves nothing to read is refused in words before any money is spent. The numbers are counted from what you may see, so they never move because two other firms shared a document.*

  **Two new columns, drawn first** ([data-model.md](data-model.md) drawer 3, migration 0076): `plans.scope` (the declared scope, written once by `openPlan` before the first retrieval, never edited; null is the whole visible library) and `runs.reach` (the counts). **How `reach` lands before the freeze:** a finished run is frozen by the T-008 trigger (`runs_immutable_once_finished`), which rejects any update once the state has left `running` and lists the columns that may never change; `reach` is not among them, exactly as `response` is not. So `finishRun` writes the state, the answer and the counts in the one update the trigger admits — no trigger change — and the orchestrator test shows a run finishing with its reach in that one write (the freeze itself is proved by the existing append-only tests, not by a T-469 test). The comment on `plan_steps` is amended to the invariant that survives: a step declares no scope, the plan's scope only narrows.

  **One scope, one convention, on four request bodies.** `AssemblyRequest.request.scope` (and `createRunBody`, `documentCreationBody`, `qaCheckBody`) carry `{ termIds?, containerIds?, savedScopeId? }`, with a refinement that a scope must name at least one. `sourceContainerIds` (Ask), `sourceVersionIds` (creator) and `scopeVersionIds` (checker) are gone; `attachedDocumentIds` stays (T-471's). **Absent means the whole visible library; present means exactly it; an empty scope is a 400 in words** — it replaces the checker's "empty means everything" and Ask's "empty means nothing". The creator's workflow lost its `sources` parameter (now v4) and the checker's its `scope_version_ids` (now v3): the scope is on the plan and travels on the run's context, not as a step input.

  **The gateway intersects, after resolution.** `createAssembler` passes the scope into `groundedLibrary` → the terms feed `RetrievalRequest.classificationTermIds` (built by T-242, fed by nothing until now) and the named documents become a container clause in `liveLibraryFilter`, ANDed with `deliverableVisibleSql` and the state clauses, never in place of them. `classificationScopeSql` is rewritten: **terms of one facet are OR'd, terms of different facets are AND'd** ("geotechnical and report"), found by grouping the terms by their facet inside the transaction; named documents are AND'd with the terms. An id that is malformed, or names no term, makes a group nothing satisfies — it narrows to nothing and never drops out. A scope that names nothing the gateway can read (an unresolved saved scope) admits nothing rather than everything. The creator's and the checker's post-filters are removed: the pre-filter replaces them, and a narrowed run no longer retrieves the whole library to throw most of it away. The pins that said "no scope field at all" (the gateway and retrieval comments, the attenuation header, the rerun-body comment, the three tests) are re-worded to pin the invariant — **scope ∩ visible == what is retrieved** — and the wall tests now run it as each party.

  **Reach counts.** `reachCounts` (in `@infora/knowledge`, beside `countLiveChunks`) counts **documents, not passages** — distinct containers — all under `deliverableVisibleSql`: `visibleLive`, `inScope`, `excludedByState: { superseded, withdrawn }` and `leftOutByScope = visibleLive − inScope`. `AssemblyCoverage` gains `reach` (one extra aggregate per assembly, in the same transaction); the API takes the same counts once when it accepts a request — it needs them to refuse before spend — and hands them to the run, which adds **`read`**, the distinct documents in its steps' `source_set` (the passage-grain audit), and writes `runs.reach` at completion. `Run` gains `reach?`; `Plan` gains `scope?`. A pure `reachStatement` in `contracts` renders the one sentence (a zero part is omitted; nothing about re-checks or scans yet — those states do not exist). It replaces the hand-built reach prose in the creator's and the checker's plan and result coverage sentences (`ToolPlan.coverage`, `DocumentCreationRunResponse.coverage`, `QaCheckRunResponse.coverage`), which keep everything they say about checks.

  **Refuse before spend.** A declared scope that resolves to nothing the requester may read: the tools set `ToolPlan.refusal` in words ("Your scope leaves nothing to read: …") and the run endpoint honours it; Ask answers `POST /runs` 400 with the same words, before the classifier or any model call. **Saved scope:** `savedViewRegister` gains `scope`; for that register only the API validates the filter as the typed scope on save and resolves it on use (`apps/api/src/scope.ts`, `saved-views.ts`); no DDL. The picker is T-470's. **Ask's chip** keeps working by sending `scope.containerIds`; the creator's and checker's pickers send container ids instead of version ids. Nothing else on screen changed.

  **Judgement calls the owner may want to overrule.** (1) **A saved scope stands alone** — a saved scope plus loose ids is a 400, because two statements of one choice could quietly widen the first. (2) **Terms AND named documents** — a scope naming both narrows to the documents that are both; the ruling said "ANDed" for the container filter and did not say how it meets the terms. (3) **`excludedByState` is counted across the whole visible library, not only the scope** — the brief says "visible but not live". With a narrow scope the sentence can therefore name superseded documents that were outside the scope anyway. (4) **A creator with no scope and an empty library still refuses** (as it did with no sources); the checker does not — a whole-library check over an empty library says "the library returned nothing", as before. (5) The creator's `unreachableSources` now holds the **documents the scope named that returned nothing**, not version ids.

  **Honest limits.** `read` is the documents named in the steps' recorded source sets. For Ask and the creator that is what was retrieved and used; for the checker it is the documents behind the findings' citations (the section check records only those), so a check that found nothing reads as "Read no documents" even though the library was searched. A re-run inherits its plan's scope and counts afresh; its body may not carry a scope (400, by name). The reach sentence renders only where a coverage string already shows — Ask answers, the editor and the findings panel get it in T-470. `personal-data.md` needs no entry: `plans.scope` and `runs.reach` name no person, and a saved scope is a `saved_views` row, already registered (T-460).

  **Reviewed 2026-10-24 (the co-captain, with a verifier reading the diff claim by claim).** Every build claim held, and the done-when is proved twice. Fixed in review: **"excluded by state" is now counted within the chosen scope** — the first cut counted superseded and withdrawn documents across the whole visible library, so a narrow scope could name documents it would never have read; it now means "documents your scope would have read, had they been live", which is what the sentence says in plain words. Three comments that described the old shape (the creator endpoint's header, the creator body's "the server resolves each document", the state-count comment's "same clauses") were rewritten, and the overclaim above about a second-write test was corrected. **Two changes the record had not named:** T-292's narrowed-assembler path for Ask (`narrowedRetrieve`) is deleted — Ask's chip now travels as the request's `scope` like everyone else's, and the run routes take the router directly; and the extractor and the corpus-retrieval worker gained a scope pass-through with no change in behaviour. **One limit left standing:** a rerun inherits its plan's scope and is counted afresh, but is not refused before spend if that scope now leaves nothing to read — rare (a library can only shrink that way by withdrawal) and recorded here rather than built in.


  **Tests:** [`scope.test.ts`](../../packages/contracts/src/scope.test.ts) — the refinement on all four bodies, the sentences (omission of zero parts, the board's example, singular/plural), the refusal wording; [`scope-reach.test.ts`](../../packages/knowledge/src/scope-reach.test.ts) — container, term (OR within a facet, AND across), terms AND containers, malformed and unknown ids, an unresolved saved scope, **the wall as each party** (B naming A's unshared document retrieves and counts nothing; C likewise), `reachCounts` on a seeded world (documents not passages, superseded and withdrawn named), **B's counts unmoved when A shares with C**, and `candidates` counted after the scope; [`scope-reach.test.ts`](../../apps/api/src/scope-reach.test.ts) — the same done-when over HTTP with three organisations, `read` equal to the distinct documents in the steps' source sets, scope on the plan, the empty-scope 400, the re-run inheriting, the saved scope validated on save and resolved on use (another firm's does not exist); `chain.test.ts` — the scope is on the plan **before** the retrieve leaf runs, and `read` is the distinct containers; `qa-checker.scope.test.ts` — the scope reaches every search and nothing is filtered after; `document-builder.test.ts`, `tool-plan.test.ts`, `qa-plan.test.ts` — the refusal, the sentences, the scope passed through; [`reach-scope.spec.ts`](../../e2e/tests/reach-scope.spec.ts) — Ask with a scope of one document: the run's reach is consistent (read ≤ in scope ≤ visible).

- **T-470 — The scope control and the reach statement.** *Plainly:* one `ScopeControl` (searchable, facetted by the classification vocabulary, explicit documents, saved scopes) replaces the Data sources chip and the two checkbox lists in the creator and the checker; the reach statement renders on every Ask answer, draft and findings panel. **Done when:** scoping to one discipline is three keystrokes; a scope that leaves nothing to read is refused before spend. **Deps:** T-469, T-460. ✅ **Built 2026-10-24** (no migration).

  **As built. *Plainly: there is now one "Scope" button where there used to be three different ways of choosing what a question, a draft or a check may read. It says what you have chosen ("Scope: whole library", or "Scope: Geotechnical · 2 documents"). Press Enter on it, type a few letters of a discipline, document type, document code or title, press Enter again, and that choice is in; Escape closes the list and keeps your choice. Underneath the search, one line says how many documents your choice reaches, counted by the server from what you may open, before anything is asked. If the answer is none, the line says "Nothing to read in this scope", the Send button (or "See the plan") switches off, and the reason is printed beside it. Under every answer, and above the findings of a check, the same sentence now says what was read and what was left out.* Choosing can only make the reading smaller; it never reaches a document you could not open by hand.

  **The three keystrokes, exactly.** With the button focused: **Enter** opens the list and puts the cursor in its search box; typing **`geo`** puts "Geotechnical" first (a label that starts with what you typed outranks one that merely contains it); **Enter** ticks the highlighted row. That is open, type, tick — three actions, five physical key presses for `geo`; Escape (a fourth, optional press) closes the list with the choice kept and returns the keyboard to the button. `e2e/tests/scope-control.spec.ts` proves it by keyboard alone.

  **One control, three homes.** `ScopeControl` (`apps/web/src/scope-control.tsx`, because it fetches) sits over a new `MultiPicker` in `packages/ui` — a search box and a `role="listbox"` with `aria-multiselectable`, rows with `aria-selected` meaning *ticked*, grouped by heading, driven by ↑/↓/Enter/Space/Escape with focus never leaving the search box (`aria-activedescendant`). The key rules and the search are pure functions (`multiPickerStep`, `filterPickerGroups`) so they are tested without a browser. The existing single-choice `Combobox` is untouched.
