Three groups, in order: **Vocabulary** (every term of the project's classification scheme, retired terms hidden, each showing how many visible documents carry it, the facet name beside it), **Documents** (the grounding scope, searched by reference, title and — unshown — the filer's description), **Saved scopes** (the `scope` register). Applying a saved scope replaces the choice and names it; the first edit afterwards drops the name and sends the loose ids, because a saved scope stands alone on the wire. "Save this scope…" reuses the saved-views dialog, which was lifted out of `SavedViewsMenu` into an exported `SaveViewModal` so the two share one. The control **replaces** Ask's Data sources chip (`DataSourcesChip` deleted), the creator's "Sources this draft may use" tick-list (`SourceRow` deleted) and the checker's `LibraryScopePicker`; `ListSearch` and `matchesQuery` stay for the attach picker (T-471's).

  **Live reach preview — one new endpoint, one changed read.** `POST /projects/:projectId/scope-preview` takes the same `scope` as the run and returns the reach counts T-469's `reachCounts` already produced, minus `read`; it runs no retrieval and spends nothing, sits beside `GET /grounding-scope` under the same guard, resolves a saved scope on the server (another firm's is a 404) and refuses an empty scope in words. The gate is two-sided: the control shows the sentence and disables the surface's button with it, and the server's refusal before spend (T-469) stays as the backstop. **Where the reach statement renders:** Ask's completion footer (`cf-reach`, from `run.reach`), the findings panel's header (below), and — unchanged in code, because T-469 already built them from `reachStatement` — the creator's and checker's plan "Covers:" and result "Covered:" lines; before a run the plan cards still show the plan's sentence and the control shows the preview's.

  **Deviations and judgement calls, honestly.** (1) **The brief's "number of visible documents carrying each term" needed a source, and none existed**: the scheme read carries no counts. They ride `GET /grounding-scope` as `termCounts`, counted over exactly the documents that read lists — so a number beside a term can never exceed the Documents group. (2) **The findings panel needed the counts and the findings read did not carry them**: `GET /sandbox-documents/:id/findings` gained `reach`, taken from the newest check run behind the findings **that the reader made** — a run's counts are taken under its maker's visibility, so a colleague sees no sentence rather than someone else's numbers. (3) **Space ticks a row only while the search is empty**; once a word is being typed a space belongs to the word, so "ground inv" can be searched. Enter always ticks. (4) **No browser emulation exists in this repo's unit tests** (static markup only), so "web render … with `userEvent.keyboard`" is done as the pure key-rule tests in `packages/ui` plus the end-to-end spec; the control's open list is rendered open (`initiallyOpen`) for the markup tests. (5) The creator and checker disable **"See the plan"** (their first button) rather than the run button, because their run button only exists after a plan, and a plan over a scope that reads nothing carries T-469's refusal anyway; a scope change discards a drawn plan, as any other answer does. (6) The **Documents group is not paged** — it lists the whole grounding scope, which the old chip and tick-lists did too; a library of many thousands would want the register's paging. (7) `.source-row` styles are now unused and left in the stylesheet.

  **Reviewed 2026-10-24 (the co-captain, with a verifier reading the diff claim by claim).** The build matches its claims: one picker, one control in three places, the old controls gone, a preview that only counts. Fixed in review: **a trap in the checker** — the scope and its "nothing to read" block belong to the Accuracy check alone, but an empty scope kept "See the plan" disabled after Accuracy was unticked, with the control and its reason gone from view; now the scope is sent, and the block applies, only while Accuracy is ticked. Two stylesheet tokens that do not exist (`--status-warning-surface`, `--elevation-level3` on the panel) were replaced with the system's own (`--feedback-warning-tint`, `--pane-shadow`), so the warning holds in dark mode. The end-to-end spec's "read ≤ in scope" could pass on a run that read nothing, so it now also requires the preview to have left documents out and the answer's sentence to say "left out". The Tests line above overstated which request bodies are captured; corrected. Stale comments naming the Data sources chip were tidied. **Two things the verifier noted and I left standing:** the findings panel's reach sentence is the newest run *by the reader*, so when a colleague ran the latest check the reader sees their own older run's sentence — safe (nobody sees another's counts) and stated here; and the spec reclassifies a seeded document as Geotechnical, so the suite was run twice on one seed before commit (the second run is the proof it survives its own change).

  **Tests:** [`scope-preview.test.ts`](../../apps/api/src/scope-preview.test.ts) (7) — whole library, a term, a named document, a saved scope (another firm's is 404), a term from another project reaches nothing, an empty scope is a 400 in words, an outsider is 404, term counts; [`scope.test.ts`](../../packages/contracts/src/scope.test.ts) — the preview body; `ui.test.tsx` — `MultiPicker` roles, grouping, the search order, the key rules, Space only when the search is empty, the footer's reach sentence; `render.test.tsx` — the empty-library chip keeps its warning, the open list in its three groups with counts and retired terms hidden, the "Nothing to read" line, Ask's request body through a fetch stub (the creator's and the checker's `scope` fields are covered by the pure `scopeField` tests, not a captured body), the composer's blocked send, the findings header sentence; [`scope-control.spec.ts`](../../e2e/tests/scope-control.spec.ts) — Ask by keyboard alone, the answer's reach sentence (read ≤ in scope), then a scope that reaches nothing with Send off.

- **T-471 — The working set.** *Plainly:* the checker's "search your working area" picker becomes a `WorkingSetPicker` used in Ask, the creator and the editor; `WorkingSet` accepts many documents; the run records the set; the shared thread shows it to the sandbox's participants only. `Q-020` ruled by an ADR-0022 addendum; `CONTEXT.md` gains **Working set**. **Done when:** pinning two drafts is four clicks with search; an answer leaning on them carries the label and no citation; a participant outside the sandbox cannot see the set. **Deps:** T-470. ✅ **Built 2026-10-24** (migration **0077**).

  **As built. *Plainly: there is now one "Working set" button — on Ask, on the document creator, on the checker and in the editor. Open it, type a few letters of a draft's title, click the drafts you want and press Done. The list shows the drafts in every working area you are part of, yours and any shared with you, each with the name of its working area. The AI reads what you pick as background you vouch for. It never cites it, and the answer says "Drawing on your working area — 2 documents"; hover the words to see which. A colleague who is not in those drafts' working area sees only that there were two documents from a working area they are not in — never their titles. Nothing is ever pinned for you: not the draft you are editing, not a file you uploaded.*

  **A gap closed on the way, which the board did not name.** Before this ticket the checker read an attached draft **by its id alone**: the check on the draft being checked looked at its firm, and nothing looked at the drafts handed in beside it, so an id from a working area the author was not in (guessed, left over from a closed grant, or put into an edited plan) was read straight into the prompt. And `POST …/attached-sources` stored a `sandbox` pin's reference exactly as sent, without looking at it. Both are fixed: reach is now checked per document, through the document's own working area's live grants (`canAccessSandbox`, one function, `apps/api/src/working-set.ts`), when a draft is pinned, when a check or draft is planned or run, and when a conversation's next run starts. A draft that is out of reach refuses the run in words (a 400) before anything is spent — never dropped quietly.

  **One new column, drawn first** ([data-model.md](data-model.md) drawer 3, migration 0077): `plans.working_set` (jsonb, null means none) — the list of `{ sandboxDocumentId, label }` the run was handed, written by `openPlan` with the scope before the first retrieval and never edited. The text the model was shown is the run's, not the record's: the plan keeps the id and the title the draft had, and no excerpt. It names no person (the pinner is on `attached_sources`, already registered in `personal-data.md` under "Attached sources: who pinned a … supplied document into a question", which covers a pinned draft as it covers any supplied document — nothing new to register).

  **What may be pinned: documents from sandboxes you are in.** New read `GET /projects/:projectId/working-area?q=&page=` lists every live document in a sandbox the requester holds a live grant on — their organisation's own and any shared one — searched by title (a literal, so a typed `%` is not a wildcard), newest first, 50 a page with a `hasMore` flag, each row carrying its sandbox's name. It selects only the sandboxes the grants admit, so a draft from any other working area is never selected, never counted and never hinted at. `GET /projects/:id/sandbox-documents` is untouched: it is "my organisation's own", and the sandbox screen is built on that.

  **Run time is checked again, for whoever is running.** A conversation's live `sandbox` pins are its working set. Ask's and the editor's run route reads them, checks each for the person who is starting the run, and refuses in words — naming the draft by the title its pinner saw when the pinner is the requester, and as "a document a colleague pinned" otherwise, so a refusal never teaches a colleague outside the working area a title. The checker and the creator take ids from their launcher bodies and refuse on the plan call as well as the run call, naming the document by the id that was sent. A re-run inherits its plan's working set and re-checks it. **`excerptsOf` is gone:** the section check now reads attached drafts off the run's context, where the API put them after checking, instead of selecting by the step input — so an edited plan cannot name an unchecked id either. `attached_document_ids` stays a bound parameter for the record only.

  **How the set reaches the model.** The draft is handed the excerpt (4,000 characters a document, the checker's own figure) as a block after the numbered sources and before the task: `[A1] (attached by the user — not a project source) …`, with an instruction never to mark a sentence with an `[A#]` or present it as a source. Numbered `A`, never `S`: `parseClaims` resolves only `[S#]` against the retrieved sources and **strips any `[A#]` the model writes**, so a claim that rested on a pinned draft has no source, cannot be cited, and is withheld or labelled model knowledge by the ground check like any unsourced sentence. It never goes through the assembler: the draft leaf's input is unchanged, the set travels on the leaf context. The cite step is proved by test to cite exactly what the same run without a set would. The creator's drafting call gets the same block.

  **The label.** `Run.workingSet` and `Plan.workingSet` (contracts) carry the entries; one function, `workingSetStatement`, renders "Drawing on your working area — N documents" (or "N documents from a working area you are not in" for a reader outside every one), shown as a `.cf-line` entry in the completion footer and on the creator's and checker's results through one `WorkingSetLine`, with the titles in the T-468 `HoverCard`. A finding from an attached draft keeps its "quoted rather than cited" line.

  **Hidden to everyone not in the draft's working area.** Every read that returns a run, a plan, the pins or the findings — `GET /conversations/:id`, `GET /runs/:id`, `GET /runs/:id/plan`, a work item's runs, the re-run and the run-creating responses, `GET …/attached-sources` and `GET /sandbox-documents/:id/findings` — replaces each entry whose draft sits in a working area the reader is not in with `{ hidden: true }` (the pin read: `hidden: true`, no ref, no label). Per document, so a reader may see some titles and a count of the rest. A draft that can no longer be found is hidden to everyone. **Two more leaks, found in review and closed here.** (a) A checker finding that quotes an attached draft stores its title and up to 4,000 characters on the finding, and the findings read returned that to anyone who could read the checked draft — possibly another firm when the checked draft sits in a shared area. That leak existed before this ticket; it is closed here: for a reader not in the attached draft's working area the finding stays but its evidence comes back with a blank excerpt and id and `hidden: true`, and the panel says "Quoted from a document in a working area you are not in." (b) The plan read returned each step's bound `attached_document_ids` verbatim; for a reader not in a listed draft's working area that id now reads `"hidden"`, in place, so the count is still theirs to see. Proved as three people in one firm (the owner in all three working areas; a member of the team area; a member of the whole-firm area only) and as a different firm, which sees no run at all because a run is the producing firm's.

  **Deviations and judgement calls, honestly.** (1) **A `sandbox` pin's label is the document's own title from the store**, not the body's. (2) **The picker pins on each click** (so "Enter pins" is literal) and Done only closes; the brief's "four clicks" is open, A, B, Done, with the search typed. In Ask the conversation is opened when the first draft is pinned, so a set can be chosen before anything is asked. (3) **Only `sandbox` pins reach a run.** `library`, `upload` and `web` pins are still stored and still read by nothing, as before; nothing in the interface creates them any more (library documents are named through the Scope control, where they can be cited). (4) **The editor's `PinModal`, `working-set.tsx`, the checker's `AttachPicker` and the in-page `ListSearch`/`matchesQuery` are deleted**; the `.list-search` and `.attach-row` styles are now unused and left. The draft being checked or edited is not offered in the picker (it would read itself back to itself). (5) **A pinner who loses access sees their own pin as hidden** — the rule is the reader's access now, not the pinner's access then. (6) **No total cap on the number of pinned drafts** — each is cut to 4,000 characters but a very large set would make a long prompt; not capped because the board named no limit, and left here as a decision for the owner. (7) **In a built document a sentence leaning on a pinned draft is withheld**, because a built document keeps only sentences a library source backs; the working set can steer the draft but cannot add words to it. In Ask's chat mode such a sentence appears labelled as model knowledge. (8) **The audit keeps the title.** A purged draft's pins are deleted, but the plans of runs that were handed it keep its id and the title it had (a plan is evidence and is never edited), as a run's request text keeps what was asked; whether a purge should reach that is a question for the owner, not minted here.

  **Reviewed 2026-10-24 (the co-captain, with a verifier reading the diff claim by claim).** The wall held on every read the brief named — the picker lists only what the reader may open, reach is checked at pin, plan, run and re-run, an unreachable draft refuses the run in words, and the refusal wording leaks no title. The verifier then tried to learn a hidden draft's name by other roads and found two: **the checker's findings** carried an attached draft's title and up to 4,000 characters of its text to anyone who could read the checked document — possibly another firm when the checked document sits in a shared area (this existed before the ticket; it contradicted ruling 5 the day it was written) — and **the plan read** returned the attached ids to a same-firm colleague outside the area. Both were closed by the builder on the review's instruction, as three parties, with the record's "every read" sentence corrected to mean it. **Two things stand and go to the owner:** an Ask answer can carry what a hidden draft *said*, labelled as model knowledge, to colleagues reading the thread (`Q-057` — a product judgement about what a shared thread is); and a purged draft's title stays on the plans of runs that were handed it (`Q-058`). The second full e2e run needed a restart — the first server was still shutting down and Playwright timed out before any test ran — and then passed clean on the same seed.

  **Tests:** [`working-set.test.ts`](../../apps/api/src/working-set.test.ts) (21 — the four added in review cover the findings and plan reads as three parties) — the working-area read as four different people over five working areas, paged at 50, searched as a literal, the deleted and other-project drafts never listed; the pin refused in the same words for an unreachable, deleted, made-up and malformed ref; the run refused in words with no run opened (the pinner by title, a colleague without it) and let through once unpinned; the model shown the block and the plan keeping id and label only; nothing pinned by opening the editor; the three-party hiding on thread, run and plan reads and on the pins; another firm seeing no run; [`qa-check.test.ts`](../../apps/api/src/qa-check.test.ts) and [`document-creation.test.ts`](../../apps/api/src/document-creation.test.ts) — an attached id from a working area the author is not in refused on plan and run with nothing spent, a reachable one read, recorded and cited nowhere; [`attached.test.ts`](../../apps/api/src/attached.test.ts) — the sandbox pin now names a real draft; `chain.test.ts` and `cite-leaf.test.ts` — the set on the plan before retrieval (id and label only), on the leaf context, not in the assembled input, and the cite step citing exactly what it would without a set; `grounded-draft.test.ts` — the block in the prompt, `[A#]` stripped; `working-set.test.ts` (contracts) — the label and its hidden form; `ui.test.tsx` — the footer line and the picker's caller-owned search; `render.test.tsx` — the picker's rows, the chip count, the hidden-count note, the editor's raw-id field gone, nothing pinned by the editor, one picker in four places; [`working-set.spec.ts`](../../e2e/tests/working-set.spec.ts) — Ask end to end: open, click, click, Done; the label, no citation to either draft; a colleague in the same firm outside the working area sees the count and no titles. [`copy-pass.spec.ts`](../../e2e/tests/copy-pass.spec.ts) now asserts the Working set chip where it asserted there was no attach chip.

- **T-472 — Reference material upload and intake.** *Plainly:* bulk upload from the library with progress; an intake table where the ontology's proposal path (today written only as null) proposes title and facets per file; an intake screen to confirm, correct and bulk-confirm; nothing grounds before confirmation. ADR-0011 addendum; ADR-0045's deferral split; data model drawer 2 drawn first. **Done when:** fifty PDFs dropped on the library become fifty titled, classified rows after one review pass; the audit names who confirmed what. **Deps:** T-462. ✅ **Built 2026-10-24** (migration **0078**).

  **As built. *Plainly: the owner's super user now adds reference material from the library screen. Press "Add reference material", choose as many PDF, Word, Excel or PowerPoint files as you like, and a line counts them in as they go up ("7 of 50 uploaded · 2 could not be read"). Each file waits in an "Intake" queue — it is not in the library, and nothing the AI can read, until you say so. The AI has read the opening of each file and suggested a title, a kind of document, a discipline and so on, with a word beside each guess — confident, likely or unsure. Correct what is wrong in the table, tick the rows you are happy with, press "Confirm selected", and they become library documents with your name on the confirmation. Reject a file and it is deleted. A scanned file with no readable text is accepted too: if you confirm it the library holds it and opens it, marked "Not citable — no readable text", and no run can read or cite it.*

  **Surprises first.** (1) **Nothing was needed to make "nothing grounds before confirmation" true.** An upload is an intake row, not a library document, so there is no document, version or passage for retrieval to find until a person confirms; no flag was added to retrieval to forget. (2) **The versions table's own guard had to be taught the new column.** It protects its columns by name, so the new `not_citable` mark would have stayed changeable after insert. Migration 0078 adds it to the guard; a test proves it cannot be flipped. (3) **The upload door needed a line in the cross-site guard's list of file doors**, or every upload was refused as not-JSON — found by the first test run. (4) **`step_type` gained `intake_proposal`** — the proposal is an agent run on the record, and its step needs a name (as migration 0067's `app_step` did). The drawing did not name it; the data-model note says so. (5) **No row-level security on the new table**, because the sandbox tables the brief pointed at have none: the wall is the route's. The DB test therefore covers the migration's data step and the table's behaviour, not a policy.

  **One admission path.** `admitReference` ([`reference-admission.ts`](../../apps/api/src/reference-admission.ts)) makes the container, genesis version, rendition and ingest. The operator's bulk load ([`bulk-load.ts`](../../apps/api/src/bulk-load.ts)) now calls it, unchanged in behaviour (its tests are untouched and pass); a person's confirmation calls it too. The CLI still records nobody and stays operator-only — its header now says there is a surface (the library) and this is its path, and why the CLI is still not that surface. `isVersionIndexed` returns "finished" for a not-citable version, so the bulk load's resume never mistakes a confirmed scan for a half-landed ingest; `extract.ts`'s warning names the intake as the one place a textless file is admitted.

  **The upload and the queue** ([`reference-intake.ts`](../../apps/api/src/reference-intake.ts)). `POST /projects/:id/reference-intake` takes one file per request. Owner organisation and `canEditPlan` only, refused in words (403 `owner_super_user_required`) for anyone else on the project. It extracts text as the sandbox upload does, but a file with no text is **not refused**: it lands with the extractor's reason as `text_status`, no text and no proposal. The blob is stored (`putBlob`). Unless the project has switched `reference_intake` off — a new entry in the AI transparency table, skipped rather than refused — the proposer runs. `GET` is the queue (paged, `proposalsOn` tells the screen whether the switch is on), `POST …/:id/confirm` and `POST …/confirm` (bulk, per-row results), `POST …/:id/reject` (deletes the file and the row, asks no reason), and `GET /containers/:id/library-admission` for the document page.

  **The proposer** ([`packages/capabilities/src/reference-intake.ts`](../../packages/capabilities/src/reference-intake.ts)). A pure `composeIntakePrompt` (the file name, the project's own vocabulary by code, the first 3,000 characters) and a pure `admitIntakeProposal` (the `rule-extraction.ts` pattern): a facet or term the scheme does not have is dropped and counted, never invented; one term per facet; confidence is one of three words and anything else — a number included — becomes "unsure". The API makes the call through `router.chat('triage', …)` as a Run on the record: a conversation, a run and one `intake_proposal` step with model, usage, cost and egress; a failed call is recorded as a failed run and the upload still lands.

  **Confirm = admit.** The settled title and terms are checked against the project's live vocabulary (one per facet), the reference is the file name (as the operator's load makes it; a clash is refused in words, `reference_in_use`), and `admitReference` runs with the confirmer's classifications: `set_by_participant_id` is the confirmer, and `proposed_by_run_id` is the proposal run **only on a term the person left as the AI proposed it** — a term they changed is theirs, and a record saying otherwise would be wrong about who is responsible (a term they changed is theirs). The intake row then gets `confirmed_by`, `confirmed_at`, `container_id` and status `confirmed`, and drops its `extracted_text` (the version holds it). A file with no text is admitted with `versions.not_citable = true`, `content ''`, and no ingest.

  **Not citable, shown.** `LibraryItem` gains `notCitable` and `notCitableReason`; the library row carries "Not citable — no readable text" and the reason in words. `ReachCounts` gains an optional `notCitable` (visible, live, current versions with the mark, counted under the same wall and scope as the other counts — so a scope that does not admit it does not hear about it), and `reachStatement` adds "N not citable (scan)." when it is above zero. This closes the deferral in the T-468 note above.

  **The screens.** The library screen gets an "Add reference material" button (a hidden multi-file input, owner's super user only) and an "Intake (N)" button; uploads go up one at a time and the count line is fed from each request's answer, with no timers. The intake screen (`library/intake`, [`reference-intake.tsx`](../../apps/web/src/screens/reference-intake.tsx)) is a `Register`: file and text status, an editable title, one select per facet prefilled with the proposal and the AI's word beside it (the word disappears if the person changes the term), a tick box per row, Confirm and Reject per row, and "Confirm selected". A scan says "No proposal — no readable text"; with the switch off every readable row says "No proposal — the AI is switched off for this project". `SelectInput` and `TextInput` in `packages/ui` gained an optional `ariaLabel` for table cells. The document page's Activity tab shows "Added to the library by <name> on <date>". The library's work queue is not touched (T-473's re-check arm).

  **Audit.** The intake row (kept, `confirmed`) plus `container_classifications.set_by_participant_id` say who confirmed what. Both named columns are registered in [personal-data.md](../architecture/personal-data.md), with where they are deleted: with the project, with the participant, on a rejection, and with the document when the owner erases a withdrawn reference document (`removeLibraryContainer` now deletes the intake row in its transaction — without that line the erase would have failed on the new foreign key).

  **Deviations and judgement calls, honestly.** (a) The new document types carry no `source` of their own — terms have no such column; the facet's source is unchanged — and use the codes STD, GDN, LEG and CRS. (b) The not-citable count is taken inside the scope, as the excluded-by-state counts are; the brief did not say. (c) "Fifty" in the done-when is the shape, not the test's count: the end-to-end walk uses three small PDFs (and a scan) because it makes the same walk in seconds; the unit suite covers per-row bulk reporting. (d) The e2e fake model answers the intake prompt with a title and a Standard / Environmental proposal and, deliberately, one invented term, so the drop-the-invented-term rule runs on the live path. (e) A reference clash on confirmation is refused rather than auto-renumbered; a re-uploaded copy of the same file must be rejected or renamed. (f) **Two kinds of failure, told apart.** If anything fails inside the admission's own transaction (the container, version, classification or file record), nothing lands: the row stays proposed and the person is told "Nothing was added — try again". If the container committed and only the index call failed, the row is marked confirmed against the container the admission itself returned (never one found by looking the reference up), the confirmation says the document is in the library but not yet readable by the AI, and the owner's super user gets "Index again" (`POST …/reference-intake/:id/index`) on the intake screen and on the document's Activity line while the version is unindexed. The file record is now made inside the transaction, so a missing file can no longer leave a half-made document. (g) An upload has no size cap beyond the server's; the board named none.

  **Reviewed 2026-10-24 (the co-captain, with a verifier reading the diff claim by claim).** The build is sound: an upload is an intake row and nothing else, so nothing can be grounded on before a person confirms; confirmation goes through the same admission code as the operator's load; a scan is held and never read. The verifier found one false promise and three record slips, all fixed by the builder on the review's instruction: when indexing failed after a document was admitted, the person was told the operator's load would finish it — it never would, since that load only revisits its own folder — so there are now two honest answers (nothing landed, try again; or admitted but not yet readable, with an "Index again" door for the owner's super user) and the file record moved inside the admission's transaction so a half-made document cannot exist; an internal note was removed from this record; the confirmer's link now cascades on deletion as the personal-data row claims; and v1.md's line no longer suggests the pilot's own corpus comes through the intake (it still arrives by the operator's load, which proposes nothing). Added at the review's suggestion: a stranger-gets-404 test on every intake door, and the end-to-end "nothing in the library yet" check now waits for the search to settle. Two judgement calls the builder made and the review kept: the AI's run is named on a classification only where the person kept its proposal, since a changed term is the person's; and erasing a document deletes its intake row with it (ADR-0050 §7's "erased, not delisted" — the purge event is the record of the act).

  **Tests:** [`reference-intake.test.ts`](../../apps/api/src/reference-intake.test.ts) (api, 15) — a drop lands with text, a proposal that drops the invented term, a recorded run and step, and is not in the library; a scan lands with its reason, not refused; a non-super-user is refused on every door; confirm admits (container with no work item, version with text read by the index, native rendition, classification naming the confirmer and the AI's run on the term left standing, the intake row as audit, the activity read, the wall on it); a confirmed scan is admitted not citable with no embedding call and the library says why; reject deletes file and row; bulk confirm reports per row (an invalid term and a missing id do not sink the others); a duplicate reference is refused in words; the switch off still lands the upload with no proposal and the person's classification claims nothing for the AI; a failing model leaves the upload landed and the run recorded as failed; a failure inside admission adds nothing and leaves the row proposed; an index-only failure confirms the row against the right container, shows it needs indexing, refuses a non-super-user, fails again in words and then finishes with "Index again"; a stranger gets 404 on every door; the cross-site guard; erasing a document takes its intake row; [`reference-intake.test.ts`](../../packages/capabilities/src/reference-intake.test.ts) (capabilities, 6) — compose and admit, including the invented term, the confidence words and one-per-facet; [`reference-intake.test.ts`](../../packages/db/src/reference-intake.test.ts) (db, 5) — the four types from the seed and from the migration's own data step (read off the file, once, idempotent), the intake row, and the not-citable mark frozen after insert; [`scope-reach.test.ts`](../../packages/knowledge/src/scope-reach.test.ts) (+1) — the count under the wall and the scope, never retrieved; `scope.test.ts` (+1) — the sentence; `render.test.tsx` (+7) — the table, the correction removing the word, the scan and switch-off sentences, the bulk body, the bulk door's request, the count line, the label; [`reference-intake.spec.ts`](../../e2e/tests/reference-intake.spec.ts) (2) — three PDFs dropped, counted in, one title and one term corrected, three ticked and confirmed, three titled and classified library rows, the activity line naming the confirmer; and a scan accepted, marked in the queue, confirmed and held as not citable.

- **T-473 — Currency and re-check.** *Plainly:* "confirmed current by" and "re-check due" on reference rows with a per-document-type default; a due re-check lands in the owner's work queue; an unconfirmed document keeps grounding with the fact shown on every citation of it; the confirmer's name joins personal-data.md. **Done when:** a seeded standard past its re-check date shows the mark on its citations and sits in the queue. **Deps:** T-472, T-467, T-468. ✅ **Built 2026-10-24** (migration **0079**).

  **As built. *Plainly: a standard the project relies on can now be "confirmed current" by the owner's super user, and the record keeps who, when, and when it should be checked again. How long a confirmation lasts depends on the kind of document — a year for a standard or guidance, six months for legislation, two years for a consultee's response — and the owner's super user can change those numbers. When the re-check date passes, the document appears in the owner's "waiting on you" list. A document nobody has confirmed is not hidden from the AI: it is still read, and every citation of it carries a small mark and, on the card, a sentence saying nobody has checked it is still the one to rely on. The first confirmation happens for free: when the owner confirms a file into the library from the intake, that is also the first confirmation of currency.*

  **Surprises first.** (1) **The brief said "RLS" for the new intervals table; the drawing was silent, and none was built — ruled in review: none, as `reference_intake` has none.** `recheck_defaults` follows `reference_intake`: the wall is the route's (owner organisation, super user) and the table names no person. If a policy is wanted it is a small follow-up. (2) **Every reference document already in a project is now "unconfirmed", so every citation of the seeded library carries the mark** — including the six that existed before this ticket. That is the honest state of a library nobody has confirmed, and it is the feature working; but it is the first thing a person will notice on opening Ask. (3) **One existing end-to-end spec had to change**: `citation-passage.spec.ts` read the chip's text as the document's name, and the mark is now part of the chip's text. It strips the mark. (4) **A test-only door was added to the end-to-end server** (`POST /__e2e/reset-seeded-currency`, in `e2e-server.ts` only, wrapped around the real app; the production entry has no such route). Confirming is a person's act the product deliberately cannot undo, so a spec that presses "Confirm current" on the seeded standard would leave the seed changed and a second run would find nothing in the queue. The spec calls the door first and puts the seed's two dates back (the confirmer stays Rachel, who is also the only person the spec can confirm as). (5) **The findings panel needed the same treatment as a run's citations**: a finding's citations are stored with the finding, not read through the run reader, so they carry their currency through one extra pass in `listFindings` — else the checker's citations would have been the one place the mark was missing. (6) **A T-472 database test had to change**: it deletes the four document-type terms to imitate a project from before 0078, and those terms now have interval rows pointing at them; it deletes the interval rows first, as a project from then would not have had them.

  **The migration** (0079, drawn first in [data-model.md](data-model.md) drawer 2). `containers` gains `confirmed_current_by_participant_id` (a named person — `ON DELETE SET NULL`, so removing the person erases the name and keeps the document; a cascade would have deleted the document), `confirmed_current_at` and `recheck_due_at`. A new table `recheck_defaults` (project, term or null for the project-wide fallback, months; unique per pair, a second partial unique index so there is only one fallback per project, months > 0, granted to the app role). A data step inserts the five rows into every project that existed; `seedProjectOntology` inserts them for new ones, from the same numbers. No CHECK keeps the columns null on a deliverable (a CHECK cannot reach across tables); `confirmCurrent` and the route do, and a test proves a deliverable stays null.

  **Confirming** ([`reference-currency.ts`](../../apps/api/src/reference-currency.ts)). `POST /containers/:id/confirm-current` — owner organisation and `canEditPlan`; an organisation that is not the owner, a deliverable, a container outside the library and a stranger all get the same 404, and an owner-organisation member who is not a super user gets the 403 in words. It sets who and when from the database's clock and the due date as that plus the interval of the document's `document_type` term (the project's fallback when it has none, twelve if a project somehow has no fallback). The record keeps the latest confirmation: the next one overwrites. `GET /containers/:id/currency` gives the document page's card the state and the interval the next confirmation will run for. `GET`/`PATCH /projects/:id/recheck-defaults` read and edit the intervals (PATCH is the owner's super user and edits the rows the project has; it never invents one). **The intake is the first confirmation**: `admitReference` gained an optional `confirmedByParticipantId`, and when it is given the same `confirmCurrent` runs inside the admission's own transaction, after the classification rows are written (which fixes the interval); the operator's load and the CLI record nobody, pass nothing, and their documents start unconfirmed.

  **Currency on every read** ([`currency.ts`](../../packages/contracts/src/currency.ts), [`currency.ts`](../../packages/knowledge/src/currency.ts)). One pure function, `currencyOf`, turns the three stored facts and the time of the read into `{ state, confirmedBy, confirmedAt, recheckDue }`; `readCurrencies` fetches it for a batch of containers and answers `null` for a deliverable. It rides `LibraryItem.currency`, `GetVersionResponse.currency` and `GetPassageResponse.currency` (null on a deliverable), and `Citation.currency` (absent on a deliverable and on an authority reference), which `run-reader.ts`'s `toCitation` fills at read time and which is never written to the citation row. The same two functions, `currencyWords` and `currencyMarkTitle`, give the sentence and the chip's name, so the screens cannot say it differently.

  **Shown.** `SourceChip` takes `currency` and draws a small circled glyph — `?` for unconfirmed, `↻` for overdue — with `role="img"`, a short accessible name and the full sentence as its title; nothing is drawn for a confirmed document. The T-468 source card adds a line in words ("Not confirmed current — nobody has checked this document is still the one to rely on" / "Re-check overdue since <date> — confirmed current by <name> on <date>"). The library row carries the same words and a badge, and the filter menu has "Needs confirming" (the search takes `currency=needs_confirming`: reference documents with no confirmation or a passed date). The document page (overview tab) has a Currency card: the state, the words, who and when, the due date, the months the next confirmation would run for, and "Confirm current" for the owner's super user only.

  **The queue.** `recheck_reference` for the owner's super user: every live library reference container with `recheck_due_at <= now()`, "Re-check: <title> — due <date>", pointing at the document page, longest-overdue first (the rest of the queue stays newest-first). **A document nobody has ever confirmed is deliberately not in the queue** (ADR-0011's addendum, ruling 4): it carries the mark and the "Needs confirming" filter. The web panel needed no change; it renders the label.

  **The reach sentence.** `ReachCounts.awaitingRecheck` — live, visible, readable documents in scope whose date has passed — counted inside the existing live count, under the same wall and scope; `reachStatement` ends with "N awaiting re-check." when it is above zero.

  **The seed.** One new reference row, `WA-STD-BS5930-001` "BS 5930 — Code of practice for ground investigations", classified Standard, confirmed current by the owner's super user fourteen months ago with a re-check date two months ago (the project's own Standard interval is used, so the dates move with the setting). Its text contains the word "alpha" so that the end-to-end fake index (whose only keyword is "alpha") puts it first for the spec's question; the passage is invented ground-investigation wording and says so in the seed comment.

  **Deliberately not built.** An editor for the intervals on a screen — the doors exist and are tested, no screen asks for them yet. A notification when a re-check falls due (nothing in the ticket; ADR-0049's events are another ticket's).

  **Reviewed 2026-10-24 (the co-captain, with a verifier reading the diff claim by claim).** Every claim held; the done-when holds on the seed. Ruled in review: **no row-level security on the intervals table** — the brief had asked for it, the drawing was silent, and the table names no person and is reached only through the owner's gate, as `reference_intake` is; the record above was corrected to say so. Two wording slips fixed (the reset door writes two dates, not three columns; the library row drops a departed confirmer's name rather than saying so — only the document page says it). **One older problem fixed on the way:** the builder reported that the register search's wall test (T-462's `library-search.test.ts`) fails on a freshly seeded database and passes only after the end-to-end suite has issued a Calder & Hale document into the library — an order dependency that would have failed CI, which seeds fresh and runs these tests first. The verifier confirmed it predates this ticket; the test now issues its own library row and removes it through the purge's door. Proved by reseeding and running it before any e2e. The same file's latency line (a paged read of ten thousand rows under 500 ms) failed once on that cold, just-reseeded database at 12.9 s and passed on the next run — an environment flake worth knowing, not a regression.

  **Tests:** [`reference-currency.test.ts`](../../apps/api/src/reference-currency.test.ts) (api, 11) — the seeded intervals and who may edit them (a member and a producer refused, an unknown type and a zero refused); an unconfirmed document reads as such; confirming sets the three columns, the due date from the type's interval (Standard, Legislation, unclassified fallback), and the latest wins; a changed interval applies next time; a deliverable and a stranger refused (and the deliverable's columns left null); the queue lists an overdue document for the owner's super user and nobody else and drops it on confirmation, never lists an unconfirmed one, and lists the longest overdue first; currency on the library, the version and the passage flips from confirmed to overdue as the date passes; a citation read through `readRun` carries today's currency (confirmed, overdue, unconfirmed) and no currency is stored on the row; "Needs confirming" returns exactly the unconfirmed and overdue references; [`reference-intake.test.ts`](../../apps/api/src/reference-intake.test.ts) (+2) — the intake's confirmation is the first confirmation with the type's interval, and the operator's admission leaves a document unconfirmed; [`recheck-defaults.test.ts`](../../packages/db/src/recheck-defaults.test.ts) (db, 3) — from the seed, from the migration's own data step (read off the file, idempotent), and the constraints; [`scope-reach.test.ts`](../../packages/knowledge/src/scope-reach.test.ts) (+1) — `awaitingRecheck` under the wall and the scope, a future date counting nothing; [`scope.test.ts`](../../packages/contracts/src/scope.test.ts) (+1) and [`currency.test.ts`](../../packages/contracts/src/currency.test.ts) (5) — the sentence, the state at the boundary, the words; `render.test.tsx` (+3) — the chip's mark and name, the card line for unconfirmed and overdue, the Currency card with and without the button; [`reference-currency.spec.ts`](../../e2e/tests/reference-currency.spec.ts) (1) — the owner's super user finds the seeded standard in the queue, opens it and reads "Re-check overdue", asks a question the standard answers and sees the mark on its chip and the sentence on its card, presses "Confirm current" and the queue row is gone; green twice on one seed.

## Where-to-start records — moved 2026-08-28

*The board's Where to start narrative accumulated full closed-ticket records
between 2026-08-03 and 2026-08-27 — above the board guard's old scanned range,
which began at "Building for V1". That is the same regrowth the ticket-grain
rule was adopted to stop, one section higher in the same file. Moved here
verbatim on 2026-08-28, when the guard's scope was widened to the whole board;
the struck pointers remain in [plan.md](plan.md)'s Where to start. Several of
these findings exist only here — the ticket-by-ticket records above predate
them.*

- ~~**T-341** — library removal.~~ ✅ **Built 2026-08-27**, closing T-340's third
  Done-when clause. Its finding: ADR-0050 §7 and §8 pull against each other for
  a *produced* deliverable, so removal is scoped to the incident the ticket
  names — loaded reference material — and the harder case is refused by name
  rather than decided by an implementation. Two of purge's three Done-when clauses are T-341's, and
  ADR-0050 §7 has ruled the shape (withdraw, then the *owner* organisation
  removes, on the producing organisation's request). It is also the answer to the
  realistic V1 incident — the first real corpus load is also the first real test.
- ~~**T-312** — size the eval fixture.~~ ✅ **Built 2026-08-27.** Precision is
  measured for the first time. Its real finding was one level down: the
  harness's embedding had **two dimensions of meaning**, invisible at seven
  documents and fatal at 291. The graded half stays ungraded — that is
  **T-320**, pointed at a non-Anthropic family.
- ~~**T-344** — re-sync the drizzle snapshot.~~ ✅ **Built 2026-08-27.**
  Migrations 0048 and 0049 were both hand-written with hand-appended journal
  entries, which had been the convention for eleven migrations running; the
  cost stopped compounding here. The re-sync's own verification found the
  second half of the answer: `generate` is safe now, `push` never will be,
  because fifteen `CHECK` constraints and `version_chunks`' RLS are objects
  the drizzle schema does not model and push offers to drop.
- ~~**T-345** — wire the eval smoke tier into CI~~ ✅ **built 2026-08-27**, and
  ~~**T-315** — session
  revocation on remove-user~~ ✅ **built 2026-08-27**. Both small, both
  unblocked, both named gaps their own tickets recorded rather than discovered.
  T-315's finding: the act it was supposed to wire *into* did not exist — the
  API could remove a **Participant** and had no way to say a person had left
  the **organisation**, which is why `revokeUserSessions` had nothing to be
  called from.
- ~~**T-308** — the rulebook's home, and **T-328** — the finding schema~~
  ✅ **both built 2026-08-27**: the two Waypoint C items with no remaining
  dependency, T-328 minted ahead of T-310/T-311 because neither can be
  specified without it. T-328 chose severity's vocabulary — `required` /
  `advisory`, two levels — and carried ADR-0048 §7 as a **discriminated union**,
  so a finding that cites the firm's own rulebook no longer compiles.

*What the frontier was until 2026-08-27* — [v1.md](v1.md)'s Waypoint A floor,
because nothing a firm touches can precede it:

- ~~**T-303 → T-304** — the bulk-load path, then the reference-material marker.~~ ✅ **Built 2026-08-27.** The load resumes on **indexed-ness**, not on a row existing — a container that committed while its embedding died is *in the library and answering nothing*, which is worse than absent. Reference material is listed **apart from** the produced record, off an absence that is derived and never stored. Both unblocked **T-306**, which landed the same day.
- ~~**T-305** — PDF text extraction.~~ ✅ **Built 2026-08-27** (migration 0048). The input path exists, and **page is a locator**: the extractor marks page boundaries in the extracted text, so page derives from T-271's stored span with no column of its own. Two things it leaves behind for the tickets below: **T-303's bulk load calls the same extractor and inherits its refusals**, and **T-306's xlsx/pptx refusal path now has a worked pattern** to follow rather than invent.
- ~~**T-307** — the chunker's heading-number split.~~ ✅ **Built 2026-08-27**, in its own commit as the spike asks. It also **found the limit of the instrument**: 11 of the seed set's 17 cases are ungraded for want of a configured grader, so "run the evals either side" currently measures access and recall and not retrieval quality — which sharpens **T-312**.
- ~~**T-276** — the authority-corpus spike.~~ ✅ **Findings 2026-08-27** → [spikes/spike-authority-corpus.md](spikes/spike-authority-corpus.md). Its sharpest finding is a **guard rather than a design**: the authority corpus must not live in `version_chunks`, whose wall predicate is built for project material — a corpus that legitimately has no wall must not sit inside the table enforcing one.
- ~~**T-337** — schema import (Slice V1-S).~~ ✅ **Built 2026-08-27.** Deterministic, therefore **no model call, therefore no Run** — which is how the personal-data constraint is met structurally rather than by remembering to strip a field. It returns **candidates**; the existing `PUT` still commits, and the endpoint's own acceptance test is that the scheme is byte-identical afterwards.
- ~~**T-301 (part)** — only the **supersede** half remains, and it is 🌫 fog behind **`Q-036`**.~~ ✅ **`Q-036` ruled 2026-08-27**, and the remaining half is **absorbed into Slice Document Status** (T-383–T-391) rather than built under its old name: T-301's framing predates the record-state model and would have shipped a narrower thing — an owner state-set — where the ruling says supersession by a *different* document is a confirmed edge and only withdrawal is a state.
- ~~**T-346 → T-350 — Slice Review Surface**~~ ✅ **Minted and built 2026-08-06, one day** — the first slice cut from direct owner UI feedback: ADR-0051's submission acknowledgement gate, the four-state cycle status bar, the deliverable status page between the schedule and the review, the schedule onto the UI kit, and the transmittal history with the ADR-0035-addendum distribution cut. Record in [plan-history.md](plan-history.md). **Follow-ups from the owner's render review, same day: T-351 (✅) · T-352 · T-353** — see the block below Slice V1-P.
- ~~**T-358 → T-368 + T-355 — Slice Walkthrough**~~ ✅ **Closed 2026-08-09, one day** — the second owner-directed slice, and the first cut from a walk of the *built product*: the DMS walkthrough session's nine rulings (S1–S9) became the schema's Excel template and the plan's create-only batch import, org-standard plan columns, the row detail as a card, row-edit delegation to the lead author, the structure builder's plan seed and its agent, plan-locked sandboxes, the bind confirmation card with read-through titles, and the internal QA surface with the promotion-requires-QA gate — then **T-368** recaptured the walkthrough against all of it, so the page that provoked the session photographs the product again. Migrations 0042–0045; record in [plan-history.md](plan-history.md), session record in [grill-history.md](../grill-sessions/grill-history.md). **`Q-039` was raised by it** (a plan-locked shared sandbox discloses the whole TIDP's shape).

- ~~**T-371 → T-375 — Slice Walkthrough 2**~~ ✅ **Built 2026-08-22** *(minted the same day)* — the third owner-directed slice and the second cut from a walk of the built product: the review period gains an owner, the lead reviewer accepts their own appointment, promotion gets a reconfirming window, the receipt narrows to the lead, and the DRR finally renders as the table its component doc has always named. **T-371, T-372 and T-375 are unblocked today**; T-373 and T-374 sequence behind them. All three surfaces were drawn and ruled in [docs/design/mockups/](../design/mockups/) before any code. **Closed out 2026-08-22:** the five screens are **photographed** into [user-stories-walkthrough.html](../architecture/user-stories-walkthrough.html) (33 beats), the four gap cards the walk left are now beats, and the three mockups are deleted — a mockup dies when its capture becomes the record ([design/README.md](../design/README.md)). `Q-041` (where the review record lives) was ruled the same day: **the pane**. The capture itself found two defects worth the run — the promotion window's cards clipped inside the modal grid, and the record stating "0 comments" to the walled side, which is the very absence its notice denies.
